title: Account Specialist, Spasticity & Movement Disorder - South Denver, CO
description:
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas – immunology, oncology, neuroscience, and eye care – and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  X ,  Facebook ,  Instagram ,  YouTube ,  LinkedIn  and  Tik Tok .
This role is field-based and candidates should live within a reasonable distance from the primary city. Talent will be hired at a level commensurate with experience.
The Account Specialist role promotes a product to community practices and health systems. Customer accounts may include community/private practices, community-based hospitals, academic medical centers, and government accounts (military treatment facilities and/or Veteran’s Affairs Medical Centers). The Account Specialist develops and maintains relationships with various accounts/departments such as neurology, pain medicine, physical medicine and rehabilitation, primary care, and pharmacy.
Responsibilities
Promote a product to meet/exceed sales goals in community/private practices as well as hospitals/health systems.
Identify/uncover customer needs (training, clinical, operational, reimbursement) and address with appropriate AbbVie resources
Provide education and clinical/injection training for residents, fellows, and other key hospital personnel.
Expert delivery of anatomical/procedural information and training, including the appropriate use of anatomical terminology to train injection paradigms/postures while highlighting various anatomical and injection insights and considerations.
Effectively utilize AbbVie's sales and data resources to enhance productivity and growth of AbbVie products while implementing U.S. Marketing Plan.
Collaborate with other Account Specialist to promote the product for approved indications and execute individual, department, or group resident/fellow trainings within hospital/health system accounts.
Bachelor’s degree in health, sciences, pharmacy or business-related field preferred or relevant and equivalent industry experience required.
Relevant and equivalent industry experience required in lieu of a bachelor’s degree is at least five (5) years of technical experience with three (3) or more years of experience within sales preferred and a high school diploma/GED required
Experience with Buy & Bill and/or Specialty Pharmacy products is preferred, in both health systems and private practice
Ability to lift/pull 25–100 lb. training models and meet necessary hospital credentialing/vaccination requirements
Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements
Ability to travel adequately to cover territory, as well as overnight attendance at scheduled training events and sales meetings
Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment
Documented history of strong sales performance, preferably in a clinical/technical/consultative sales role with multiple decision makers is preferred. Ability to manage a complex sell, learn procedural, technical, clinical, and anatomical information quickly and communicate/present/train to a variety of audiences
An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials.
These HCIR credentialing requirements may include, but are not limited to, background checks, drug screens, proof of immunization/vaccination for various diseases, fingerprinting and specific licenses required by individual state or cities. Please remember that you are solely responsible for ensuring that you satisfy all HCIR credentialing requirements and for any associated liability for failing to do so. AbbVie has resources available to you to help answer questions you may have.
Key Stakeholders
External: Specialty Physicians in Therapeutic brand area, pharmacists, nurses, others depending on brand plan.
Internal: In-field team members, Sales Management (i.e. DSM), Marketing Management, Training, Customer Excellence, & Brand Plan stakeholders.

title: Associate Director, Business Process Owner
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
Own the end-to-end governance, health, and continuous improvement of assigned clinical business processes, ensuring processes are inspection-ready, scalable, and aligned to enterprise priorities and regulatory expectations. Partner across Clinical Development Operations and enabling functions to translate strategy into clear process outcomes, drive adoption through change management and learning alignment, and monitor process performance signals to proactively address risk and improve execution. Role may be filled as a Sr. BPO depending on experience and process areas.
Responsibilities
Serve as the accountable owner for assigned clinical business processes across their lifecycle (Engage → Evaluate → Execute → Measure → Sustain), defining process scope, intended outcomes, and decision rights.
Establish and maintain an end-to-end process governance model (standards, forums, escalations, and stakeholder alignment) to ensure consistent global execution and a unified, single voice to the business.
Own process health and sustainability by defining and monitoring key process signals/metrics, identifying emerging issues and risks, and driving timely mitigation and continuous improvement.
Translate business and regulatory needs into clear process requirements and partner with Process Excellence roles (e.g., process design/engineering) to ensure documentation is complete, consistent, and inspection-ready.
Act as the authoritative point of contact for process questions within the domain; curate and maintain process knowledge content and ensure availability of fit-for-purpose guidance for end users.
Lead cross-functional stakeholder engagement to align priorities, trade-offs, and adoption plans, ensuring the right SMEs are engaged at the right time and decisions are transparent and durable.
Partner with stakeholders to ensure change narratives, communications, and role-based training enable effective adoption and sustained performance.
Coordinate and coach a domain SME network to support process adherence, identify improvement opportunities, and reinforce standard ways of working.
Partner with system and business owners to ensure process-to-system alignment, impact assessment for changes, and effective implementation support (e.g., acceptance criteria, UAT input, and readiness planning).
Embed innovation and digital/AI enablement into process oversight and improvements where appropriate, ensuring changes are controlled, compliant, and measurable.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree strongly preferred (e.g., life sciences, engineering, or related discipline).
Minimum of 8 years clinical process management experience required with demonstrated experience owning and governing end-to-end business processes in a regulated environment (clinical development, GxP, quality systems, or similar).
Strong understanding of clinical development operations and the regulatory/inspection context; ability to apply this knowledge to process decisions and risk management.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional alignment and stakeholder management, including conflict resolution and escalation when needed.
Experience defining process performance measures, monitoring process health, and driving continuous improvement using data and structured problem solving.
Familiarity with process design/documentation standards and methods (e.g., process mapping/BPMN, Lean/Six Sigma concepts), including partnering effectively with process architects/engineers.
Experience partnering with technology/system owners on process-to-system alignment and change impacts (requirements, readiness, and UAT support).
Strong change leadership skills, including partnering on communications, training alignment, and adoption/sustainment planning.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex process topics into clear guidance for diverse audiences.
Ability to work effectively in a matrixed, global environment and manage multiple priorities with sound judgment and accountability.

Serving as a trusted advisor to franchise VPs, Senior Directors, and IBT leads across Market Access & Patient Services (MAPS) and Sales & Marketing, this individual is the connective tissue between business ambition and technology execution, translating commercial priorities into a cohesive, forward-looking technology roadmap. This role owns the full BTS investment portfolio end-to-end: from strategic prioritization and business case development through delivery oversight and ROI validation, coordinating execution across shared services platforms and data teams’ enterprise wide.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. This position is part of AbbVie's Information Security & Risk Management (ISRM) team within Business Technology Solutions. The Identity & Access Management (IAM) team is responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of the organization's IAM strategy, ensuring secure, efficient, and compliant access to systems and data. The NHI and Cloud IAM function addresses one of the fastest-growing attack surfaces in enterprise security—machine identities now outnumber human ones, and the rapid expansion of AI agents is accelerating that trend. This role does not own the AI agent or cloud platforms themselves—those are owned by partner teams across BTS—but it is the IAM team's authoritative voice on how those platforms must integrate with identity governance, and it is accountable for ensuring that no non-human identity operates outside of AbbVie's visibility or control.
Take the next step in your career with an organization that strategically invests in the long-term health of the company, its technology and its people. The AbbVie Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team shapes the digital transformation necessary for our treatments to positively impact patients' lives. In the role of Non-Human Identity and Cloud IAM – Platform Lead, you'll tackle one of the most complex and rapidly evolving challenges in enterprise security: establishing a unified strategy for non-human identities, AI agent governance, and cloud IAM—bridging today's fragmented landscape into a coherent, observable, and future-ready program. This is a senior, highly technical role that requires both architectural depth and the organizational influence to drive accountability across the teams that own AI, agentic, and cloud platforms—ensuring that every non-human identity is visible, governed, and secured from AbbVie's IAM systems.
In this role, you'll be responsible for:
Define and drive the enterprise Non-Human Identity (NHI) strategy—rapidly assessing all in-flight initiatives across the organization, rationalizing overlapping efforts, and establishing a centralized, authoritative governance program covering all machine identities across on-premises, cloud, and agentic environments
Build and maintain a comprehensive NHI registry encompassing service accounts, APIs, bots, application identities, robotic process automation (RPA), and AI agents—ensuring every non-human identity is discovered, inventoried, classified, and continuously governed within IAM systems
Own AbbVie's identity governance posture for AI agents: while the creation and operation of AI agent platforms is owned by other teams, this role is accountable for ensuring those platforms integrate with IAM—so that every AI agent is inventoried in the NHI registry, mapped to its owning human or system identity, governed through appropriate access controls, and visible for security monitoring
Proactively discover and identify new AI agents and agentic workloads as they are introduced across the enterprise; partner with AI platform, cloud, and business teams to ensure timely onboarding into the NHI governance framework, and drive remediations or mappings where gaps exist
Serve as the IAM point of accountability for all agent-related identity questions: defining standards for how agents authenticate, what credentials they use, how those credentials are secured, and how agent activity is observable from an identity and access perspective
Establish centralized NHI observability by driving integration between IAM platforms and external systems—including AWS, Azure, GCP, and agentic platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock, or similar)—so that IAM maintains a living, authoritative view of all non-human identities regardless of where they originate
Design and implement modern NHI credential security controls including just-in-time (JIT) access, dynamic secrets, short-lived certificates, automated credential rotation, and runtime authentication—reducing standing privilege for machine identities to near zero where possible
Assess the current tooling landscape for NHI and cloud IAM; determine whether existing platforms can be extended or reconfigured, or whether new capabilities are needed; and build a pragmatic, phased modernization roadmap
Own and evolve the Cloud IAM and IGA strategy, closing the integration gap between cloud-native identity platforms (AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, GCP IAM) and AbbVie's central IAM/IGA tools—ensuring cloud identities, entitlements, and access certifications are governed consistently and automatically
Design cloud identity governance frameworks including role-based access models, entitlement management, access certifications, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud environments
Drive cross-functional alignment across IAM, AI Platform, Cloud, Security Architecture, Compliance, Audit, and business teams—translating complex, fast-moving requirements into executable roadmap priorities and holding partner teams accountable for IAM integration commitments
Establish KPIs and maturity metrics for the NHI and Cloud IAM program, providing executive-level visibility into inventory completeness, risk posture, program progress, and open gaps
Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements (SOX, GDPR, PCI-DSS) for machine identities and cloud access controls; respond to and remediate audit findings
Manage budget, resources, and vendor relationships for all NHI and Cloud IAM technologies and solutions
Lead and mentor a team of technical specialists, cultivating a culture of proactive governance, automation, and continuous improvement
Bachelor's degree with 8 years experience OR 7 years of experience OR PhD with 3 years experience
Hands-on experience with non-human identity management, cloud IAM, or machine identity governance in large enterprise environments
Demonstrated experience establishing or maturing NHI programs—including service accounts, API credentials, application identities, and/or automated/agentic workloads
Strong hands-on expertise with cloud IAM frameworks: AWS IAM, Azure Entra ID, and/or GCP IAM, including integration with central IGA platforms
Experience designing and implementing cloud IGA processes: entitlement management, access certifications, role-based access models, and least-privilege enforcement in cloud environments
Proven experience with secrets management platforms and modern credential security patterns (JIT access, short-lived certificates, dynamic secrets, automated rotation)
Architecture-level understanding of identity federation, service-to-service authentication, and cloud-native identity patterns (OAuth, OIDC, SAML, workload identity)
Strong track record of driving complex, cross-functional programs in matrixed organizations—including influencing and holding accountable teams that are not direct reports
Demonstrated ability to proactively identify governance gaps, drive partner teams to remediate, and establish scalable, automated processes to prevent recurrence
Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and build alignment across organizational boundaries
Beneficial:
Familiarity with AI agent platforms and their identity/credential patterns (e.g., Microsoft Copilot ecosystem, AWS Bedrock agents, or similar agentic frameworks)
Experience building NHI discovery and inventory capabilities, including integration with platforms not originally designed for identity governance
Familiarity with containerization and Kubernetes service account management
Hands-on experience with IGA platforms and their cloud connectors (Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent)
Scripting and automation experience (PowerShell, Python, Terraform, or other IaC tools)
Knowledge of certificate management, PKI infrastructure, and API security platforms
Understanding of CIS, NIST, and other cloud security compliance frameworks
Industry certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS/Azure/GCP security certifications, or equivalent
Experience in the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry

Purpose:
The Quality Control Analyst is responsible for conducting the cell-based potency assays (CBPA) of biologics for release and stability of both commercial and late-stage biologics under current good manufacture practice(cGMP). This person will prepare all documentation associated with the cGMP testing and independently or in a team set execute protocols in support of manufacture of AbbVie’s biologics product.

Manage critical reagents and supplies.
Write quality systems records including laboratory investigations, change controls, non-conformances.
Support regulatory inspections where needed.

The Senior Manager, AI Governance & Controls Engineering is responsible for elevating AbbVie’s AI governance operations by ensuring full compliance with AI-specific regulatory requirements (EU AI Act, U.S. state AI law, NIST AI RMF) and AbbVie internal AI policy, while providing advanced strategic leadership across AI risk-control design, monitoring, and validation strategy. This role leads the development and implementation of AI governance control systems and processes, leveraging digital enablement, data-driven methodologies, and automation — including AI itself — to scale governance without proportional headcount growth. Collaborating directly with cross-functional teams (Privacy, Security, Quality, Risk Management, Legal), the Senior Manager provides audit and inspection support, drives Corrective Action and Preventive Action (CAPA) execution for AI governance findings, and oversees adoption of vendor/platform documentation (including the OneTrust risk-management platform), strengthening operations through proactive risk mitigation.
Additionally, the Senior Manager leads and develops a high-performing AI Controls Engineering team — including direct oversight of the Principal Quality Engineer, AI Controls Engineering role —, manages critical partnerships and contracts, and champions continuous process improvement, technology adoption, and innovation. This role acts as the primary liaison for AI governance initiatives, policy frameworks, and audit readiness driving high-impact results and aligning business and regulatory objectives across AbbVie’s AI landscape.
Responsibilities:
Provide advanced strategic leadership in the analysis, oversight, and execution of AI governance and controls-engineering activities, ensuring compliance with AI-specific regulatory requirements (EU AI Act, U.S. state AI law, NIST AI RMF) and corporate procedures across all AI use cases, platforms, and projects.
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing AI Controls Engineering team, including direct supervision of the Principal Quality Engineer, AI Controls Engineering role; set clear expectations, provide coaching, and support professional growth.
Lead the design and implementation of advanced AI governance control and automation solutions, applying expert solution-building skills to streamline ACTOR and OneTrust activities, reduce manual effort, and accelerate delivery of compliant AI governance reviews across the enterprise.
Architect and oversee AI governance control strategy, policy framework development, and harmonization of AI risk-management processes enterprise-wide — including platform-level versus use-case-level control placement —, ensuring alignment with business and regulatory objectives.
Drive enterprise-level audit and inspection support for AI governance, including leading audit defense, crafting responses to inspection findings, and managing the deployment and closure of CAPA solutions for AI governance findings across functional areas.
Oversee and optimize the use of vendor/platform documentation (including OneTrust), partner management, and contract oversight to ensure partner performance, quality deliverables, and compliance with SLAs.
Utilize advanced metrics, KPIs, and dashboards to monitor AI governance control effectiveness, assess AI risk exposure, and drive data-driven decisions for continuous improvement.
Proactively identify and enable opportunities for AI governance process automation and technology adoption that increase efficiency, stakeholder satisfaction, and audit-readiness — while avoiding headcount growth proportional to AI adoption.
Engage, influence, and align cross-functional partners, executive stakeholders, and AI Governance Office leadership to advance strategic technology investments and AI governance initiatives.
Foster a culture of innovation, standardize best practices and templates, promote lessons learned, and champion continuous improvement throughout the AI Governance, Operations & Monitoring (GOM) function.
Lead governance reviews for AI use cases submitted through AbbVie’s ACTOR intake, triage, and risk assessment process, applying EU AI Act and U.S. state-law risk classification and assigning proportionate controls.
Own OneTrust (or successor risk-management platform) workflow integration for AI risk assessment orchestration, control tracking, documentation, and reporting.
Identify emerging AI risks — including agentic workflows, autonomous decision-making, and new model architectures — and develop future-proof control frameworks ahead of regulatory change.
Serve as the primary technical point of contact between GOM and Privacy, Security, Quality, Risk Management, and Legal on AI control design and implementation, and support the AI Legal pillar’s Functional Embedded Partners in ensuring risk recommendations are technically implementable and monitorable.
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree with minimum of 8 years of experience; Master’s Degree with 7 years of experience; PhD plus 3 years of experience.
Respective years of demonstrated experience in SQA, CSV, investigations, and/or auditing, including at least 2 years in a formal people management and supervisory capacity leading quality professionals and managers.
Demonstrated expertise in regulatory assurance, process improvement, enterprise risk management, automation, validation strategy, and leading audit/inspection responses — applied to an AI governance context (EU AI Act, U.S. state AI law, NIST AI RMF).
Proven ability to develop and execute policy frameworks, validation strategies, and process harmonization initiatives at the enterprise level.

We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.

Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.

Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.

Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.

Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.

Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.

This lab-based role provides hands-on scientific and operational bioanalytical support for discovery and preclinical programs across a diverse and evolving portfolio.

Experience with database & system integration technologies

Splunk Certified Admin, Power User, or Architect certification
Prior experience working in an Agile team
Familiarity with cybersecurity, privacy principles, cyber threats, and vulnerabilities

Experience working with development tools and scripting languages (Python / PowerShell / Go)
Experience analyzing and pivoting on large sets of data, with the ability to identify patterns, anomalies, and outliers

title: Sr Scientist, Quantitative Bioimaging
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. We are seeking a Senior Scientist to advance quantitative bioimaging capabilities in support of immunology discovery research. In this role, you will work within a cross-functional team with access to multiple microscopy modalities, complex in vitro models, multimodal biological datasets, and advanced computational infrastructure.
You will develop and apply quantitative imaging, computer-vision, and machine-learning approaches to characterize cellular and tissue phenotypes, support the development of biological models, including co-cultures, organ-on-chip systems, organoids, and tissue explants, and generate insights that advance immunology discovery programs. This role combines hands-on delivery of robust, reproducible image-analysis workflows with the evaluation and application of advanced AI/ML approaches, including biomedical image segmentation, representation learning, foundation models, and scalable computational workflows. You will partner closely with wet-lab scientists, imaging specialists, computational scientists, and other subject-matter experts to translate biological questions into rigorous and impactful analysis strategies.
The role sits at the intersection of biology, bioengineering, microscopy, and computational science. Candidates with combined expertise in two or more of these areas are especially encouraged to apply.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, optimize, and apply imaging assays and quantitative image-analysis workflows for 2D and 3D cellular and tissue models to characterize cellular and other complex biological phenotypes.
Collaborate with wet-lab assay scientists, imaging specialists, and computational scientists from experimental and assay design through image acquisition, analysis, validation, and data delivery.
Extract biologically meaningful, multiparametric features from high-content imaging datasets and use them to characterize disease-relevant phenotypes, mechanisms, and treatment responses.
Apply statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods to identify candidate imaging biomarkers and relate imaging phenotypes to molecular, functional, and other biological readouts.
Contribute to the integration of imaging data with multimodal datasets, including molecular, single-cell, spatial, or perturbational data, where appropriate.
Establish quality-control and evaluation frameworks to assess image and assay quality, distinguish biological signal from technical artifacts, and define data-quality criteria, acceptance thresholds, and analytical limitations.
Maintain clear experimental and analytical records; analyze, visualize, and present results rigorously to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Communicate methods, assumptions, results, uncertainties, and limitations effectively to cross-functional project teams.
Stay current with advances in quantitative bioimaging, image analysis, computer vision, and AI/ML for biological imaging, and evaluate opportunities to incorporate relevant approaches into team workflows.
Basic Qualifications
BS, MS, or PhD in engineering, biophysics, computational biology, imaging science, bioinformatics, or a related discipline, with typically 10-12+ (BS), 8-10+ (MS), or 0-4+ (PhD) years experience.
Demonstrated experience developing quantitative image-analysis or computational solutions involving one or more of the following: image segmentation, feature extraction, phenotypic profiling, object classification, or analysis of high-content imaging data.
Experience with at least one relevant imaging modality or assay type, such as confocal microscopy, high-content imaging, or cell painting.
Ability to assess image quality, recognize common imaging artifacts, and interpret biologically meaningful phenotypes.
Working knowledge of machine-learning or deep-learning approaches for biological imaging, with the ability to understand model behavior, assess performance, and contribute to appropriate evaluation strategies.
Proficiency with the Python data-science ecosystem, including NumPy, pandas, Polars, scikit-learn, and/or PyTorch.
Strong biological grounding, attention to experimental rigor, and demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with wet-lab and computational colleagues.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain methods, results, assumptions, and limitations to diverse audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience working with complex in vitro models, such as organoids, organ-on-chip systems, co-cultures, tissue explants, or other advanced in vitro platforms.
Experience with classical bioimage-analysis tools such as CellProfiler, scikit-image, ImageJ/Fiji, or comparable platforms.
Exposure to deep-learning, self-supervised learning, foundation-model, embedding-based, or multimodal AI approaches for biological imaging.
Peer-reviewed publications, patents, conference presentations, or other demonstrated scientific contributions in quantitative bioimaging, computer vision, computational biology, bioengineering, or a related field.

The Global Alliance Director, AWS owns the strategic partnership between Adobe and AWS. title: System Architect, 3P Integrations, Agentic Product
description:
The Opportunity
Creative work increasingly starts inside an AI assistant, not only inside an app. Adobe is building a unified plugin and skills that brings Firefly, Photoshop, Lightroom, Premiere, Express, Acrobat and more into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and what's to come. This role owns its architecture. Want to shape how creativity sparks in every AI assistant? This is that job!
The System Architect leads technical partnerships with the companies building these assistants. The work spans protocol design, scale, and the standards (MCP, A2UI, and their successors) that will define how agents use creative tools. It suits someone who has shipped at scale, leads engineers well, and makes practical trade-offs in pursuit of what differentiates Adobe.
What you'll Do
Own the plugin architecture. Define the tools, resources, and UI contracts that expose Adobe capabilities to third-party hosts. Keep one design working across hosts with different capabilities and harnesses, while it connects seamlessly with the Adobe ecosystem.
Lead partner engineering. Run the technical relationship with partner companies and internal product teams. Shape integration contracts and pick the technical bets that differentiate Adobe.
Make it real, fast. Build compelling prototypes and demos that settle architecture debates with working code, speed up partner and leadership decisions, and get others inspired by what's possible.
Push for scale and quality. Optimize tools so models choose them correctly. Set a high bar for latency and result quality. Build evaluation suites and compatibility layers so reliability holds as hosts change. Make sure the plugin rests on a foundation that supports observability and the operational needs of a product at Adobe's scale.
Lead engineers. Set technical direction, run investigations, and help the team weigh trade-offs. Mentor engineers on MCP, agent harness, generative-UI patterns, and AI-assisted development. Work closely with the Firefly, Photoshop, Lightroom, Premiere, Express, and Acrobat teams, plus platform, security, identity, and trust and safety. Together, keep guardrails, data protection, and content credentials intact on every host.
Shape the standards and their adoption. Stay ahead of the latest models capabilities, frameworks, and agent protocols. Recommend when and how to adopt them. Represent creative and productivity use cases where those protocols are defined, with proposals and reference implementations.
What you need to succeed
Shipped user-facing products used by millions, owning technical design across several connected services.
Production work with the Model Context Protocol: tool design, servers and clients, auth flows, and versioning.
Familiarity with agent harnesses and generative UI such as A2UI, and with how large language models behave in production.
Led technical partnerships or platform integrations with other companies.
Led engineers as a technical lead or architect.
Clear writer, speaker, and presenter. Sharp in a technical review, at ease in an executive briefing or a standards group, and compelling on stage with a live demo of what the plugin can do.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience; 12+ years building software, including several years in an architect or technical lead role.
Nice to have: open standards or open-source involvement, a creative-tooling background, or work in the ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Copilot ecosystems. Have most of this but not all? Apply anyway!

The job looks much the same either way. You start with how the work really gets done, build an AI version of it, and test it until you trust the results. Then you graduate it and use what worked on the next problem. The mix of projects will keep changing as AI takes on more of the work, so we care more about how you work than about a fixed list of projects. This is a hands-on role. You design and build the workflow, prove it works with data, and ship it with engineering and product.

Drive the AI workflows and features we support from design to launch, defining the quality bar and measurement plan with engineering, product and business partners.
Prioritize projects by business impact, making trade-offs in partnership with your manager and the business and product leads you support.
Sit with the team that owns a problem, map how the work gets done today, and work out how AI can do it and where people step in for the hard cases.
Design and build AI workflows: write the prompts when needed, set up the pipeline and tooling, and monitor quality and drift once it's live.
Design the evaluation framework: build test sets, define accuracy and agreement metrics, and calibrate LLM judges against human reviewers.
Work with engineers on architecture and tooling decisions, and pressure-test estimates and scope.
Turn unclear guidelines into criteria a reviewer can apply consistently, working with product, Legal and Policy.
Work with subject matter experts to write labeling guidelines and produce human-verified labels on real data.
Run labeling at scale with vendor labeling teams, and check their work against agreement metrics and your own spot checks.
Work with product teams early to agree on what "good enough to launch" means for an AI feature, and bring the evidence and a recommendation for the go/no-go decision.
Build reusable evaluation and workflow components, document what you learn, and get other teams using them so the next team gets to production faster.
Keep our methods current as models, tools and policies change, and recommend what to retire when it stops working.
Your Expertise
8+ years in product or program management, analytics, consulting or applied AI, with a proven record of taking technical programs from idea to production and owning results such as backlog, cycle time or launch speed among others.
You're strong in SQL and in the statistics of quality: accuracy, precision and recall, sampling and reviewer agreement. You pull and analyze the data yourself instead of waiting for a report.
You’ve shipped something built on AI that other people rely on, such as a workflow, an agent or an automation, and you can show the before-and-after numbers. You can tell us where it failed and what you changed.
You're technically fluent enough to pressure-test an engineering estimate, understand how prompts, pipelines and evaluations fit together, and know when a workaround is the right call.
You're curious about how work actually gets done, including the awkward exceptions, and you've taken a messy process and made it measurable. You state the desired result first and measure success in business outcomes, not features shipped.
You have good judgment on quality. You can take messy qualitative feedback, such as reviewer comments or disagreements, and boil it down to what matters and what is worth changing.
You write clearly and can work with sales, operations, PMs and engineers in the same week, getting results through people you don't manage.
You're fine being the first person on a problem, and you try things yourself instead of waiting for someone to build them.

Hands-on Python and API experience, such as scripting data pulls, calling model APIs or building small automations.
Experience with LLM evaluation: building test sets, calibrating LLM judges or fine-tuning models.
Experience with experimentation and measurement, such as A/B tests, metric design and dashboards.

title: Deployment Program Manager, Global Logistics
description:
At Amazon, we are deploying Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking technology across our physical network in a first-of-its-kind effort — at a scale and in a way that has not been done anywhere else in the company. This initiative brings real-time, item-level visibility to inbound shipments, and getting the underlying infrastructure installed and live across many sites is the critical path to making it real.
As a Deployment Program Manager, you own the end-to-end execution of site-based infrastructure deployment — from site survey through installation, testing, and go-live — coordinating internal Amazon stakeholders (IT, Operations, Reliability & Maintenance Engineering, and Site Points of Contact) and external installation partners across multiple concurrent sites. This is a tactical, hands-on execution role focused on driving sites through the deployment pipeline. You will be based in Los Angeles and travel to sites as needed for critical milestones, safety reviews, and partner relationship-building.
Key job responsibilities
• Drive parallel pre-install workstreams — network/IT readiness, safety and compliance documentation, hardware procurement and staging, and operational readiness — to completion before installation windows are committed.
• Serve as the primary field coordination point between installation vendors, site points of contact, and internal Amazon teams during active installs.
• Provide timely, accurate site-level status input (survey, design, network readiness, installation, and go-live milestones) to the program’s reporting process.
• Escalate blockers in real time — access delays, compliance gaps, scheduling conflicts, equipment issues — to protect the program’s delivery timeline.
• Coordinate site readiness planning pre-install, including safety zones, operational vs. non-operational area access, and daily coordination plans with site operations.
• Support post-installation testing and validation coordination with technology and installation partners.
• Maintain and continuously improve deployment playbooks and pre-install checklists based on site-by-site lessons learned.
• Travel to sites as needed for critical milestones, safety reviews, and stakeholder relationship-building (frequency determined by program needs).
A day in the life
Your day balances two kinds of work. For sites approaching installation, you run proactive, scheduled readiness coordination — kickoff calls with the Site POC, site IT, and the vendor; dedicated IT follow-up on network readiness; vendor and safety/compliance prep; and a final go/no-go on the start date. For sites already in active installation, you shift to reactive, real-time troubleshooting — morning check-ins, ad hoc issue calls, same-day escalation of field blockers, and feeding site-level status into the program’s reporting. Periodic site travel and ongoing refinement of the deployment playbook round out the role.
About the team
You are part of Global Logistics which provides transportation offerings from imports and domestic shippers into the Amazon Warehouse and Distribution and Fulfillment Network. We treat our shippers as customers and obsess with giving them a loveable way to inject their inventory into our network. In this team specifically, this is a first-of-its-kind initiative bringing Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) tracking technology to Amazon’s physical network to deliver real-time, item-level visibility into inbound shipments. The deployment team is responsible for bringing this infrastructure online across sites — partnering with Operations, IT, Reliability & Maintenance Engineering, site leadership, and external installation vendors to turn the technology vision into live, working capability on the floor. It is a fast-moving, high-ownership environment where field execution directly determines how quickly the program scales.
Basic qualifications: - 2+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of maintenance planner/scheduler in industrial maintenance, manufacturing, or distribution industries experience
- 3+ years of advanced Microsoft Word and Excel experience
Preferred qualifications: - Knowledge of Lean principles and DMAIC methodology
- Experience in MS Access and SQL
- Experience in requirement gathering and ability to write clear and detailed requirement document
- Experience using Microsoft Projects software
- Experience with material handling systems (MHS) installation, operation and maintenance
- Experience working in an analytical environment with cross-functional teams

Your product managers embed directly inside enterprise customers — defining outcomes, writing specs, working hand-in-hand with engineering to ship production systems — and every engagement feeds back into AWS services and an underlying platform that makes the next one faster.
This is not a traditional AWS Product Management role. FDE product managers are field-facing: they live inside delivery, sit with customers, and turn engagement learnings into compounding platform value. You are the "CEO of the customer problem" — responsible for the *why* and *what*, while engineering owns the *how*.
Key job responsibilities
### Product Leadership
You own the customer outcomes. Your teams operate inside customer environments under real constraints and ambitious timelines — regulated data, brownfield infrastructure, multi-stakeholder governance. You lead the customer engagement strategy from the product side: define what a great pod PM does, allocate PM talent across engagements, ensure pods are solving the right problems, and hold executive customer relationships at the CIO/CTO level built on trust earned through delivered outcomes.
### Product & Platform Influence
You see what breaks  across deployments and turn that into product direction. You influence AWS service roadmap from a position of earned authority because you've lived the deployment pain firsthand, and identify when custom pod work should graduate into platform primitives or native service capabilities.
You shape the FDE engagement model: how we scope, what we deliver, what we price, what we leave behind.

You build the domain expertise that compounds. Your teams develop industry-specific accelerators, reference architectures, and blueprints that generate pipeline for the next customer in your vertical. You define the use cases that feed qualification, pricing, and pod composition. You measure what matters: asset reuse rate, time-to-value, engagement velocity
### Go-to-Market Partnership
You partner with sales, specialists, and marketing to define pricing, packaging, and positioning. You own the commercial model for FDE engagements — how we price outcomes, what the customer buys, and how we demonstrate ROI. You build pipeline through customer stories, reference architectures

95% of enterprise technology pilots deliver zero measurable P&L impact. The technology works — the gap is in the last mile: getting production systems running inside complex enterprises where legacy infrastructure, regulated data, and organizational complexity collide. AWS is making a billion-dollar investment in Forward Deployed Engineering ("FDE") to close that gap, and we're hiring product leaders who will define what we build and why.

title: Inventory Health Program Lead, Materials Allocation & Planning
description:
AWS runs the largest cloud infrastructure in the world, backed by billions of dollars in hardware inventory. We’re looking for an Inventory Health Program Lead to turn excess and obsolete (E&O) hardware into value. You’ll build secondary supply channels that don’t exist at scale today, structure commercial deals with suppliers and partners, and work with hardware engineering to qualify excess parts into current and future builds. This is a 2–3 year effort across every commodity family. The long-term goal is to change how AWS sources and commits to hardware, so E&O exposure is prevented upstream instead of cleaned up afterward.
In this role, you will:
Build a program from scratch that owns the full lifecycle of inventory health — from proactive exposure monitoring and inspection through financial alignment, cost recovery, and commercial disposition. Establish governance, standardized processes, and executive review cadences across a global network of integrator and ODM sites spanning multiple commodity families.
Drive measurable outcomes tied directly to financial planning cycles, with reduction targets tracked monthly, quarterly, and annually. Own the automation roadmap that replaces manual, fragmented workflows with scalable, system-driven execution
This isn't a role where you inherit a playbook — you're writing it. You'll work across engineering, finance, operations, and manufacturing partners to bring structure and accountability to a space with massive impact on AWS's cost structure. If you thrive on ambiguity, love building from zero, and want your work to be visible at the highest levels of the organization, this is the role.
Key job responsibilities
Design, negotiate and scale new reuse, resale and recovery channels, including secondary-market buyers, ODM/integrator buy-backs and cross-platform redeployment.
Structure strategic buy transactions with suppliers and partners on excess positions, covering returns, rebalancing and repurposing.
Work with hardware engineering to qualify excess components into current and future platforms through BOM cross-referencing and fungibility analysis, shaping platform design and sourcing decisions.
Feed recovery insights back into category strategy so future sourcing and commitment decisions reduce E&O exposure.
Own a multi-year E&O reduction strategy across all commodity families, with targets built into OP1/OP2 and tracked monthly, quarterly and annually.
Set up the governance, standard disposition processes and executive review cadences that support channel execution across global integrator and ODM sites.
Define the automation roadmap and KPIs that show leadership how much is being recovered, how fast cycles are moving and where the risk is.
A day in the life
Negotiating terms with a secondary-market buyer or an ODM on a buy-back of excess material.
Working through a BOM cross-reference with hardware engineering to qualify excess parts for a new platform build.
Modeling the recovery value of different disposition paths (redeploy, resell, return, write off) and taking a recommendation to Finance.
Partnering with commodity managers to change commit strategy based on where exposure keeps building up.
Presenting channel performance and E&O reduction progress to senior leadership
About the team
You'll join a team within AWS Infrastructure Supply Chain that ensures the right hardware is planned, allocated, and positioned across one of the largest global supply chains in the world. This role stands up a new commercial function focused on recovering value from hardware inventory. You'll have the autonomy to build new channels and the visibility to shape how AWS sources hardware. We own the end-to-end material lifecycle — from supply planning and allocation through inventory health management across a global network of manufacturing sites. We build from zero, operate at massive scale with startup energy, and sit at the center of engineering, finance, and operations. Every person has outsized impact. This role stands up a new function focused on inventory health — you'll have the autonomy to build it and the visibility to drive change.

- 5+ years of program or project management experience, or a MBA and 5+ years of working cross functionally across several teams experience
- Experience presenting to both technical and non-technical executive audiences

- Experience working with hardware engineering on component qualification, BOMs or platform design
- Financial modeling or P&L experience (recovery value, reserves, write-offs)

- Experience automating manual processes at scale

This domain is defined by scale and by ambiguity. Own the three to five year vision and strategy for payment-driven retention (Involuntary Churn), across established and emerging countries.

title: Principal Product Manager, Developer Experience and Integration Platform, Amazon Freight
description:
Every shipper and platform that connects to ASCS Shipping and Freight starts the same way: an engineer reads our documentation, requests credentials, and tries to make a first successful call or EDI transmission. When that path takes weeks instead of days, shippers delay launch and revenue waits. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to make ASCS Shipping and Freight the simplest logistics provider in the industry to integrate with, across both API and EDI.
You will own the strategy and roadmap for how developers onboard and integrate with ASCS Shipping and Freight. The role spans two integration models. 1P integrations are custom, direct integrations with large shippers, where their engineering teams connect enterprise systems to our APIs or EDI. 3P integrations are platform partnerships with ecommerce platforms, fulfillment providers, multi-carrier platforms, and TMS and WMS providers, where one integration unlocks shipping for thousands of merchants. You will define a path that serves both: repeatable and self-service for platforms, and configurable without becoming bespoke engineering for large shippers.
Your charter covers four areas. First, simplify and streamline developer onboarding, from developer registration, data-access approval, and credential management through sandbox testing, certification, and go-live. Second, own the developer documentation portal as a product, including API reference, EDI implementation guides, code samples, Postman collections, and changelogs. Third, use AI to cut time to onboard and integrate, including AI assistants that answer developer questions, generate integration code and EDI mappings, diagnose failed calls, and docs that AI coding tools can consume directly. Fourth, own the integration product strategy across API and EDI, closing capability gaps between the two channels.
You will work as a peer to the Solutions Architect (SA) team, who lead hands-on technical engagements with shippers and partners, and with Support Engineering, whose support-contact data shows where developers get stuck. SAs and Support Engineering bring direct insight into where integrations stall, and you turn those patterns into product, documentation, and tooling that remove the need for the next escalation. The goal is that SAs spend their time on the most complex, highest-value launches while standard integrations complete through self-service.
This is a deeply technical role. You will review API designs, EDI transaction mappings, and authentication models with principal engineers and Solutions Architects as a peer, and you will build working calls yourself to test the experience a developer gets. You will also influence leaders across the org whose teams build the capabilities developers integrate with.
We measure success by developer outcomes: time from registration to first successful call, time from kickoff to production go-live for 1P and 3P integrations, percentage of standard integrations completed through self-service, integration completion rate, sandbox-to-production parity, API and EDI error rates, and integration-related support contacts. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
Define the strategy for developer experience and integrations across API and EDI for ASCS Shipping and Amazon Freight, and secure alignment from engineering, Solutions Architecture, business development, partnerships, and senior leadership.
Map and instrument every step of the integration journey for 1P and 3P developers and remove the largest sources of friction first: developer registration, data-access approval, and credential lifecycle, including identity verification requests, audit pauses, and credential expiry.
Own the developer docs portal as a product with owners, standards, and metrics. Deliver accurate API reference generated from OpenAPI specifications, EDI implementation guides, quick-start guides, sample code, Postman collections, and a reliable sandbox.
Define and launch AI capabilities that cut time to integrate, such as a developer assistant trained on our docs, automated EDI mapping and validation, AI-generated sample code, failed-call diagnosis, and machine-readable docs and MCP servers for AI coding tools.
Define the EDI roadmap (for example, ANSI X12 tender, status, and invoice transactions) and close capability gaps between EDI and API across business lines.
Own the percentage of standard integrations completed through self-service. Run a shared blocker list with the Solutions Architect and Support Engineering teams, prioritize fixes, and convert custom enterprise requirements into configurable, reusable capabilities, so the next large shipper launches faster than the last.
Partner with Business Development and Solutions Architects to prioritize 3P platform integrations by shipper reach. Own the technical content of partner certification, including what gets tested, the validation tooling, and the pass criteria, in support of the certification program run by Partnerships.
Own outbound communication of built and planned enhancements to 1P shippers and 3P partners, including roadmap previews, release communications, enablement, and adoption tracking. Share field-level guidance with partners only after the owning team confirms deployment.
Partner with the product leaders who own account modeling, account lifecycle, centralized KYC, and segmentation, so developer onboarding and credential approval run on the same account and identity foundations across business lines.
Own the integration funnel metrics, run voice-of-developer programs, analyze support contacts, and use the results to set priorities.
Write PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans, coordinate developer communications and deprecations, and mentor product managers on technical product practice.

title: Principal Product Manager, Technical - Amazon Freight Support Exp, Amazon Freight
description:
When a shipper moves a truckload with Amazon Freight, they expect the load to be scheduled, tracked, and delivered without having to chase anyone. Today, too much of that experience depends on manual work. Support associates switch between many tools to find information, repetitive tasks stay manual, and some work happens outside our systems where no one can see it, measure it, or automate it. Shippers feel the result as slow answers and repeat contacts. We are hiring a Principal Product Manager - Technical to change that: to make shipper support for Amazon Freight fast, measurable, and increasingly automated.
You will own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap for the Amazon Freight shipper support experience, covering the platform, automation, and AI that associates use to resolve shipper issues. Your mandate has three parts. First, eliminate the reasons shippers contact us, by finding root causes in scheduling, tendering, tracking, disruptions, and billing and driving fixes upstream with the teams that own them. Second, make every piece of operational work visible and owned, by consolidating work done in other systems into a single operator console and ensuring every task has an owner, a queue, and a service level. Third, automate the work that does not need human judgment, using rule-based automation first and AI agents where they add value.
The heart of this role is a continuous automation flywheel. You will define the architecture for a framework that captures task-level data across operational workflows (what work is done, why, and how long it takes), then run a repeatable cycle of discover, document, model, measure, build, and automate. You will use that data and AI to find and rank automation candidates, launch rule-based automation for deterministic tasks in areas like scheduling, disruption recovery, trailer pool management, and proactive shipper communications, and route exceptions to the right operator. Every eliminated task is recorded, so the team can prove impact and reinvest the time saved.
This is a technical role. You will work with engineers on the operator platform architecture, the data model for task capture, integrations with the operational systems that work moves out of, and the design of AI agents that retrieve information, draft responses, and take actions safely. title: Senior Product Manager, Account Lifecycle, Segmentation, and KYC, ASCS Shipping and Freight
description:
Every shipper relationship with ASCS Shipping and Freight runs on its account: who the shipper is, what legal entity stands behind them, which segment they belong to, and where they are in their lifecycle. When that foundation is fragmented, shippers verify their identity more than once, sales teams merge duplicate accounts by hand, and each business line makes decisions on a different version of the truth. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to build that foundation once, for Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight.
You will own three product areas. First, centralized Know Your Customer (KYC): a single verification of a shipper's business identity and legal entity that every ASCS Shipping and Freight business line trusts and reuses, so a shipper verified once never repeats the process. Second, account lifecycle management: the states, transitions, and controls that govern an account from registration through activation, growth, dormancy, reactivation, suspension, and closure. Third, segmentation: a consistent, data-driven definition of shipper segments that sales, onboarding, pricing, support, and operations use to tailor the experience each shipper receives.
You will work closely with the Principal Product Manager who owns account modeling and sets the overall strategy for shipper account foundations. You will own the roadmap and delivery for your three areas, write the PRFAQs and PRDs, and partner with engineering, compliance, risk, sales operations, and product teams to launch them. Your work starts with the crawl phase: standing up centralized KYC and the legal-entity foundation, and cleaning existing account data so it meets the new standard.
We measure success by shipper and business outcomes: time to complete verification, share of shippers verified once and reused across business lines, duplicate account rate, accounts in a valid lifecycle state, segment coverage and accuracy, and contacts and manual work caused by account data issues. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
Deliver centralized KYC by defining requirements for a single business identity and legal-entity verification that Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight reuse. Partner with compliance, legal, and risk teams on verification standards, sanctions screening, and audit requirements, and with Amazon's identity and verification services to reuse what already exists.
Own account lifecycle management: define the account lifecycle states, the rules for moving between them, and the controls at each step. Make lifecycle status visible to sales, operations, and support so every team acts on the same account state.
Build shipper segmentation: define segments with sales, pricing, and onboarding leaders, set the data and rules behind each segment, and make segments available to downstream systems and teams through a single source.
Lead the backfill and clean-up of existing accounts, including duplicate accounts across sales and operational systems, so legacy records meet the new KYC and lifecycle standards.
Own PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans for your areas. Work with engineering on requirements, trade-offs, and phased delivery, and drive launches through to adoption.
Gather requirements from Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight, resolve conflicts between them, and drive decisions that serve shippers across both.
Instrument KYC, lifecycle, and segmentation, own the metrics, and use shipper feedback, support contacts, and operational data to set priorities.
Basic qualifications: - Bachelor's degree, or BS degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with end to end product delivery
- Experience understanding product and technical requirements and interfacing with Product/Technology teams
- Experience using data and metrics to back up assumptions, evaluate outcomes, and make data-driven decisions
- 5+ years of program management, project management or product management experience
Preferred qualifications: - MBA, or Master's degree
- 7+ years of product management experience
- Experience in logistics, or experience in e-commerce, retail or advertising
- Experience with KYC, KYB (Know Your Business), identity verification, fraud, or compliance products

title: Senior Product Manager, Shipper Communications, ASCS Shipping and Freight
description:
Shippers want to hear from us when something matters to their business: a missed pickup, a delayed load, an exception they need to act on, or a new capability that helps them ship. Today, they hear from us through many separate teams and systems. Messages overlap, arrive on channels the shipper does not watch, or arrive after the shipper has already called support to find out what happened. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to give shippers one coordinated voice from ASCS Shipping and Freight, across Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight.
You will own the product strategy and roadmap for shipper communications, covering both what reaches shippers and what reaches the internal operators and account managers who act on their behalf. Your charter has three parts. First, build the communications platform: the shared capability that every team uses to send notifications to shippers and to internal teams, with templates, routing, delivery across channels such as email, SMS, in-app, mobile push, and partner feeds. Second, source the signals: partner with operations, execution, account, billing, and marketing teams to identify the events that shippers need to know about, define a taxonomy for each event (severity, audience, channel, and how fast it must arrive), and route each signal to the right audience: the shipper, the operator who resolves the issue, the account manager who owns the relationship, or all three. Third, protect the shipper's attention: set the rules that consolidate, prioritize, and suppress messages so shippers are not overloaded with siloed communications, and deliver every message on the shipper's preferred channel.
You will be the owner of the shipper communications experience, not the author of every message. Marketing owns campaign content and brand standards, and operational teams own the quality of the signals they detect. You will own the platform, the event taxonomy, the preference and frequency rules, and the outcome metrics, and you will set the governance that every sending team follows.
We measure success by shipper outcomes: the share of shipper-impacting disruptions where we notify the shipper before they contact support, notification delivery within the target time for each severity and audience, the share of issues where the responsible operator or account manager is alerted before the shipper escalates, the share of shippers with communication preferences set, engagement and action rates, opt-out rates, communication volume per shipper, and support contacts avoided through proactive communication. You will set the baselines and targets, and report progress in weekly and monthly business reviews.
Key job responsibilities
Define the 2 to 3 year strategy and roadmap for shipper communications across Amazon Shipping and Amazon Freight, and secure alignment from operations, marketing, sales, support, and engineering leaders.
Own the requirements for a shared communications platform that every team uses to send notifications to shippers and internal teams, including templates, routing rules, multi-channel delivery, and reporting.
Partner with operations, execution, account management, billing, and marketing teams to identify the events shippers need to know about, and define a taxonomy for each event that sets severity, audience, channel, and target delivery time.
Define and deliver a shipper preference center so each shipper chooses which communications they receive, on which channel, and for which users and locations in their account.
Set frequency, consolidation, and suppression rules so related messages combine into one, lower-priority messages wait, and no shipper receives duplicate or conflicting communications from different teams.
Establish governance for every team that sends shipper communications, including template standards, an inventory of active templates, review of new communication requests, and retirement of outdated or overlapping messages.
Own the notifications that reach internal operators and account managers, so the right person is alerted when an issue needs action or a personal follow-up, and can see everything each shipper has been told.
Instrument the communications funnel from signal to delivery to action, and use the data to improve timeliness, relevance, and engagement.
Write PRFAQs, PRDs, and launch plans, and drive launches from requirements through adoption and measured impact.

These systems source data from many data sources and execute logic to determine buyability of the items in the Amazon catalog, which is consumed by hundreds of systems.
In this role, you will participate in all parts of the software development process, from collaborating with customers to understand their needs, to design, to executing that design in a scalable and extensible way. We are seeking a Sr Manufacturing Product Engineer to drive New Product Introduction (NPI) manufacturing and quality for Storage server platforms, from early design engagement through volume production. You will define manufacturing processes, test flows, and quality controls, serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM partners, and ensure products are optimized for manufacturability and launched at exceptional quality.
What You Will Do
You will own how a new Storage platform is manufactured. You will engage with hardware design early to influence testability and manufacturability, define the manufacturing test strategy and quality plan, and drive the process from prototype through Pilot and volume ramp. You will run NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments before design freeze, lead design reviews, and drive root cause corrective action on manufacturing blockers and quality escapes. When a platform ramps to volume with high first-pass yield and no quality escapes reaching the fleet, that is your impact.
Why You Will Love It
The world's most advanced frontier models train on the hardware you help build. You will see your process and test decisions scale across a large fleet of servers, and you will work at the point where design meets the factory floor. The team is deeply technical and high-trust, and you own manufacturing outcomes end to end from design engagement through volume production.
The Ideal Candidate
You think across the full manufacturing stack, from SMT assembly and test coverage to line balance, yield, and quality systems. You are as comfortable in a DFx review reading gerber files as you are on an ODM floor debugging a failing test station. You drive decisions with data, hold manufacturing partners to a high bar, and bring structured problem-solving and disciplined change management to a fast-moving NPI environment. You mentor junior engineers, contribute to hiring, and raise the manufacturing engineering bar for the team.
Key job responsibilities
Design for Manufacturability & Risk
- Perform NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments and carry-over analysis to identify and mitigate manufacturing risks before design freeze
- Participate in DFx reviews (DFM/DFA/DFT) leveraging mechanical CAD models, gerber files, and mock-up samples, driving design improvements in partnership with hardware engineering
- Lead DFMEA/PFMEA reviews and develop process flow diagrams and quality control plans
NPI Manufacturing & Test Strategy
- Own end-to-end NPI manufacturing execution for Storage server platforms across engineering phases and Pilot builds
- Define the manufacturing test strategy including test flows, coverage, duration, fixture requirements such as in circuit tests (ICT), board functional test (BFT) and system-level tests
- Own Contract Manufacturer enablement including BOM requirements, assembly workflows, testing protocols, and tooling specifications
- Research automation techniques and develop new tests and systems to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce test dwell time
Quality & Continuous Improvement
- Drive Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA) for manufacturing blockers and quality escapes
- Execute test rack inspections and quality checklists; issue quality alerts, deviations, and ship-holds as required
- Own manufacturing quality metrics and drive yield improvement, and cost optimization through process and automation engineering
Capacity & Production Ramp
- Create manufacturing capacity plans with simulations across build phases; conduct line balance and cycle time analysis to maximize throughput
- Provide on-site ODM support during critical builds and production ramp
- Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams on Storage module integration, thermal validation, and manufacturing requirements
Cross-Team Collaboration
- Serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM/CM partners
- Manage manufacturing requirements, scope, schedules, and deliverables across engineering teams, suppliers, and partners
- Perform risk assessment, mitigation, and change management throughout the program lifecycle
- Domestic and international travel (~25%) to ODM/CM and design partner sites
A day in the life
You start the day reviewing first-pass yield data from an overnight Pilot build at your ODM, isolating a test station driving a recurring failure. Mid-morning, you lead a DFx review with hardware design, pushing changes to improve testability before design freeze. In the afternoon, you drive an RCCA on a solder defect with the CM quality team and update the control plan. You end the day refining the capacity plan and line balance for the next build phase.

Located in Denver, Seattle, and Cupertino, we collaborate with global development teams and ODM/CM partners to deliver next-generation Storage server infrastructure deployed in datacenters worldwide. We move fast with small, empowered teams delivering end-to-end, from server conception through volume production and fleet-scale operations.

Together you review field data and customer feedback, looking for patterns that signal where the current architecture falls short and where the next generation needs to leap forward. You capture three hypotheses to validate with simulation runs.
The afternoon is heads-down writing time. You’re drafting a narrative that frames a customer problem — one that doesn’t have an obvious solution yet — and propose an evaluation framework for the engineering team to assess multiple architectural paths. You end the day in a cross-functional sync, aligning vehicle, software, and simulation teams on priorities for the next sprint of trade studies.

description:

Key job responsibilities
- Define and own the multi-year roadmap for technical certification programs across global AWS data center job families (DCO, DCEO, DCMAT)
- Develop and maintain a competency-based certification framework aligned to the AWS Data Center Builder Competency Framework, ensuring certifications serve as independent validators of real-world skill — not proxies for training completion
- Lead Job Task Analysis (JTA) and partner with others to translate broad competency standards into defensible, psychometrically sound certification assessments
- Partner in the design and development of certification assessments (written, practical, and performance-based) in partnership with subject matter experts, instructional designers, and third-party assessment vendors
- Ensure independence between training and certification development to maintain assessment integrity and prevent "teaching to the test"
- Establish and govern item development, review, and validation processes across global content contributors

- Stay current on industry best practices in technical credentialing, psychometrics, and workforce capability frameworks
A day in the life
Your morning kicks off with a coffee in one hand and a certification pass rate dashboard in the other — because somewhere in EMEA, a pilot just wrapped and the data is interesting. You spot an anomaly suggesting training and assessment have quietly drifted apart, fire off a note to the JTA lead, and feel that particular satisfaction of catching something before it becomes someone else's problem. Mid-morning, you're on a call with a third-party vendor, diplomatically but firmly explaining why their proposed shortcut is a no-go — assessment integrity isn't negotiable. After lunch, you're turning a gnarly dependency map into a crisp two-pager for a VP business review, making the case for more resourcing to accelerate certification coverage in APAC. We automate assessment delivery to keep the process simple, while ensuring independence and rigor through qualified assessors. Behind the scenes, we provide the tooling and data solutions that help sites plan and manage their workforce's capabilities.
Certifications are either role-based — mandatory for all Builders as part of onboarding and development — or specialty-based, tied to specific hardware or tools and managed by demand.
