title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Shipping Speed, Selection & Charges, Shipping Platform
description:
Every time someone shops on Amazon, our systems influence what they see about delivery: whether an item can ship to them, how fast it will arrive, and what shipping will cost. We own shipping speed, selection and charges for Amazon stores around the world. Our 6 Tier-1 services sit on the critical path of every product page, cart and checkout, handling millions of requests per second before checkout. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help us modernize how that works and to change how we build software along the way.
You'll lead three programs that matter to customers and to how we build:
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilities. Our ship options were first built just to describe speed. Over time each one also took on other delivery features, so a single identifier now does several jobs across many ordering, delivery and fulfillment systems. You'll drive the multi-year platform change that lets teams launch new delivery experiences, like ultra-fast quick commerce, age-verified delivery or grocery delivery, by combining reusable building blocks. Today each one needs a new ship option.
Build the customer rescue product. When an item can't be delivered to a customer, the purchase shouldn't end there. Our team is building customer rescue, the product that catches these dead ends across the shopping journey and help customers complete their order: healing carts and checkouts with substitutes and alternate offers and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery. You'll drive its delivery and adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce and other programs, partnering with the teams who own each experience.
Help lead our move to AI-driven software development. We're building toward a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in where human judgment matters. You'll own the plan to roll this out across our teams, decide how we measure success.
You'll work with principal engineers, product managers and engineering leaders across Amazon, and you'll regularly write for and present to senior leadership.
Key job responsibilities
Rebuild how Amazon models delivery capabilites
Own the roadmap to move Amazon's ordering and delivery systems off ship-option-specific logic and onto reusable capabilities and signals, so new delivery experiences launch without new ship options.
Drive adoption across shipping, checkout, fulfillment and transportation systems. Sequence integrations, align designs with principal and senior engineers, and onboard new businesses such as quick commerce, grocery and age-verified delivery.
Customer rescue product
Drive delivery of the customer rescue product from roadmap to launch: cart and checkout healing with substitutes and alternate offers, clear restriction messages, and filtering undeliverable items out of discovery.
Lead adoption across retail, grocery and quick commerce, partnering with the teams who own each shopping experience.
Coordinate A/B experiments, staged rollouts and launch readiness across marketplaces, and use the results to drive launch decisions.
Run weekly, monthly and business reviews with senior leadership, with written narratives on results, risks, recovery plans and decisions needed.
AI-driven software development
Own the plan to move our teams to a model where AI agents do much of the development work and engineers step in at key decision points. Push for full adoption over isolated pilots.
Define how adoption and impact are measured, such as coverage by service, changes shipped through agents and automated test coverage.
A day in the life
Your morning might start chairing the Ship Option Control Board, where you and principal engineers from several organizations decide whether a new delivery experience should be a reusable capability or a signal. Later you turn the latest customer rescue experiment readout into a clear recommendation for the weekly leadership review, then meet with a partner team to plan bringing the product into their shopping experience. In the afternoon you sit with a team moving its service to AI-driven development, find where the agents still get stuck, and fold those gaps into the adoption plan. You might end the day tuning an agent that drafts your program update from tracker data, so the next one takes minutes instead of hours.

title: Cellular RF Systems Architect - RF Configuration
description:
At Apple, our work is dedicated to creating products that connect and enrich people's lives. The Cellular RF Systems Engineering team sits at the very core of that mission, defining the wireless technologies that enable seamless experiences for hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
We are looking for a cellular RF engineer to translate complex 5G and 6G use cases into optimized RF configurations that bring our products to life. Configurations define how the transceiver and front-end are set up for each band, band combination, and use case, including signal routing, port mapping, gain and linearity modes and front-end control settings. If you enjoy structuring complex systems, building tools that make work scale, and connecting RF hardware and software teams, this role is for you.
In this role, you will be responsible for the optimal interaction between our RF transceivers and RF front-end modules. You will turn advanced cellular capabilities, such as carrier aggregation, MIMO, SRS antenna switching and Multi-SIM into concrete transceiver and front-end configurations. You will work closely with transmitter and receiver teams to define and refine these configurations, and partner with hardware, software and validation teams to bring them into our products. You will develop tooling and automation that keep configurations consistent across programs and contribute to the system design documentation that guides implementation.
Minimum qualifications: Minimum requirement of a bachelors degree
Solid understanding of 3GPP 5G NR and LTE physical layer and RF requirements, including band combinations, carrier aggregation, MIMO and SRS.
Working knowledge of RF front-end architectures and the system-level impact of components like PAs, LNAs, filters, and switches.
Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, or C/C++ for data analysis, system modeling, and algorithm development.
Ability to critically analyze complex trade-offs, such as routing flexibility versus insertion loss or throughput versus battery life.
Strong communication skills with a proven ability to work across diverse, cross-functional teams to solve highly complex, multi-disciplinary problems.
Preferred qualifications: MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering with a focus on advanced cellular communication topics.
5+ years of experience in RF systems engineering or 10+ years in communications circuit design.
Experience translating system requirements into hardware configurations, control settings or structured system descriptions.
Familiarity with RF configuration frameworks is a plus.
Enjoy structuring complex information with a strong focus on precision and consistency.
Experience applying AI/ML to solve system-level optimization problems.
History of successfully balancing cutting-edge hardware innovation with the practical constraints of high-volume manufacturing.

title: Custom Circuit RTL Design Engineer
description:

This requires you to work closely with the circuit design team to review design and architecture specifications and with various design teams across the SoC partitions to understand the use cases and corner conditions to develop test plans. You will also work on improving the RTL methodology as applicable to simulation and emulation scenarios.

- Work closely with custom circuit team to review schematics and understand how the RTL must model it.

Preferred qualifications: In-depth knowledge of digital design, behavioral (including emulation-friendly) and structural RTL coding especially as it pertains to SRAM and register file design
Knowledge of Verilog, System Verilog and experience with industry standard simulators and waveform debugging tools
Knowledge of regression and revision control tools, and scripting language (python / perl)
Knowledge of industry standard design and verification tools, such as ESPCV and/or LEC

title: Embedded Software Engineer - Always On Platforms, Core OS
description:
Every time your iPhone detects a car crash and calls for help, your Apple Watch notices you’ve started a workout before you tell it to, or “Hey Siri” wakes up without you touching a thing, there’s a tiny, always-on processor making it happen. At Apple, the Always-On Processor (AOP) firmware team builds the software that runs on that silicon. We write the firmware that listens to the world through accelerometers, gyroscopes, barometers, magnetometers, and more, while sipping just microwatts of power.
Our work sits underneath features people rely on every day, from emergency response and fitness tracking to camera image stabilization, spatial audio, intuitive device interactions, and all-day battery life. Because the same platform spans iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, Mac, AirPods, and Vision Pro, a line of code you write can ship in products used by hundreds of millions of people. Here, you’ll do more than join something — you’ll add something!
The Core Operating Systems (Core OS) team is responsible for the foundational software used in Apple’s most iconic and beloved products. We’re looking for a talented Embedded Software Engineer to join the Always On Platform Systems team. This team is uniquely positioned to contribute to all Apple products and has a wide range of responsibilities including: pre-silicon software development, hardware bringup, sensor driver development and integration, as well as future framework and feature development for the Always On technology area. The team also has oversight responsibilities in architecture, compute and memory resourcing, and cross-functional feature deployment.
The ideal candidate must possess a genuine passion for hardware/software integration, software quality, and the ability to collaborate and communicate effectively across teams. This is a rare opportunity to help build cutting-edge foundational technologies and have a direct impact on Apple’s widely loved products across the globe.
Minimum qualifications: Proven experience in embedded software development.
Strong proficiency in C/C++ programming.
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.

At Apple, iCloud Platform Engineering builds the server stack behind Push Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime, iCloud, iCloud Private Relay and Private Cloud Compute (PCC), the backbone of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead PCC inference routing. These systems send every inference request to the right compute across a global, multi-region fleet, while keeping latency low, availability high and PCC's privacy guarantees intact.
This is a technically grounded leadership role for someone who thrives at scale, can bring clarity to complex and fast-changing environments, and is energized by building both systems and teams. You'll guide architectural direction, scale operational practices and develop the engineers and leaders who will shape how Apple delivers cloud inference.
Routing LLM inference at Apple's scale takes systems that adapt to changing demand, available capacity and failures while keeping latency low and accelerator utilization high. As the fleet grows across regions and cells, routing must account for capacity and health across the whole fleet, not just a single site. PCC adds a basic architectural requirement: request content stays encrypted outside trusted compute nodes. You'll lead the design of routing and scheduling strategies within this privacy model. Together with inference and security teams, you'll evaluate techniques such as cache-aware request placement and prefill/decode disaggregation. Your scope includes the inference AI gateway layer, where requests are authenticated, metered, prioritized and streamed back to clients, all without exposing request content.
This work has broad reach. Every improvement to routing makes Siri AI and Apple Intelligence faster and more reliable, and makes better use of Apple's inference capacity. In your first year, you'll be expected to grow a high-performing organization, set a clear technical roadmap, and measurably improve routing latency, availability and fleet utilization.

title: ISE, Incubation - Software Development Engineer - Proactive
description:

We take big, fuzzy ideas about what might be possible and turn them into concrete concepts, prototypes and livable software! We are passionate about exploring new ideas using whatever tools help us make something tangible. Most often, we choose to modify or extend Apple’s existing software using Objective-C or Swift. But we’re open to using the best tools that help us learn: design tools, prototyping apps, ML, etc. We are looking for a creative, learning-oriented, collaborative individual to come help us explore what the future could look like.
Our team nurtures early-stage ideas into well-developed, usable experiences. For this big idea to work, is there a piece of experience that must feel great? Is there an enabling technology we need to build? Software is the tool we use most frequently to bring concepts to life on our devices. But we try to use the best tool for the job: anything that helps us see, touch, or feel an idea. We often work directly with other teams to leverage expertise from across the company, and share our work with others to find out what works and what doesn’t. Gradually, those fuzzy notions turn into tangible, brand-new ideas that can lead the future of software on our devices. The products we build are part prototype, part proof of concept and part sales pitch, so communicating clearly and being able to empathize with other people's perspectives are key skills for our team. So is the ability to give and receive feedback.

3 years experience of creative prototyping in software
Expertise in Swift or Objective-C, or equally strong experience in Python + ML stacks
Preferred qualifications: Able to deal with ambiguity, and a gut instinct for making things that will help bring clarity. We often work on projects where we need to create something to help understand the objectives & boundaries.
A learning mentality and a willingness to try things that may fail. You should be able to learn from both success and failures.

Ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical teams
Background in either machine learning or HCI
PhD in computer science or a related field

travel.

Superb written, visual, and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to foster collaboration across multidisciplinary hardware, software, and creative teams.

title: Principal Security Architect, Data Center Security
description:
The Apple Services Engineering Security team is looking for a principal-level security architect to own end-to-end trust for Apple’s next generation of data center infrastructure, the assurance that every physical and logical component, from silicon to the running workload, operates in a known, verifiable, tamper-evident state, and that this trust can be cryptographically proven to any relying party before access or data is granted. This spans hardware root of trust, DPU/IPU offload security, software and workload integrity, and the attestation protocols that tie them together into a single verifiable chain. You will partner with silicon, firmware, SOC architecture, platform, and cloud infrastructure teams to design and integrate this stack, and you’ll represent Apple in the standards bodies that define how this trust travels across the industry.
You will architect and integrate security across four layers of the data center stack:
Hardware root of trust — secure boot chains anchored in silicon (fuses, eFuse-based identity, HSMs), platform firmware integrity (UEFI/BIOS measured boot), and the physical/supply-chain controls that establish an immutable, device-unique identity at power-on.
IPU/DPU and offload security — working with platform and networking teams to ensure SmartNICs/DPUs/IPUs, as the emerging trust boundary isolating tenant workloads from infrastructure management, have their own attestable root of trust, not just line-rate crypto and policy enforcement.
Software and workload integrity — measured, signed boot through hypervisor/OS/container runtime with an unbroken chain of custody from firmware to running workload; confidential computing primitives (enclaves, TEEs, confidential VMs); drift detection against measured baselines.
Attestation and verifiable trust — the mechanism that converts the above into a dynamic, per-session trust decision: signed quotes of measured state, verification against golden measurements, key sealing/unsealing tied to attestation results, revocation of compromised measurements, and remote attestation protocols that let this trust travel to the relying party that needs it, including the agent identity layer sitting on top of this stack.
You will drive design reviews and threat models with SOC architects and platform teams, define the architecture that lets each layer attest up to the next, and ensure quality and agility through rigorous testing, participating in on-call for the systems you ship.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of security/software engineering experience, including systems-level and infrastructure security
Deep, hands-on experience with hardware root-of-trust architectures (TPM, DICE, or equivalent) and measured/attested boot chains
Proven track record designing or implementing remote attestation protocols, key sealing/provisioning tied to attestation state, and measurement revocation
Proficiency in at least one of C, C++, Go, Rust, or Python, with solid Linux systems fundamentals
Experience designing gRPC/REST backend services for identity, key management, or attestation at scale
Preferred qualifications: Direct experience with DPU/IPU/SmartNIC security architectures — tenant isolation from infrastructure management, line-rate crypto offload, and attestable DPU firmware/identity

title: Software Developement Manager, Apple Services Engineering
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center, with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements.
We're starting a new team focused on one question: how do we patch the node software across our datacenter fleet faster, and more often, with minimal impact to the workloads running on it? We're looking for a domain expert to decide the approach and then build and lead the team that delivers it.
Today, updating a node's software means choosing between speed and workload impact. This team's job is to remove that tradeoff, so we can patch the fleet faster and more often with minimal impact on users. We have not chosen an approach. Live migration, snapshot and restore, kexec-based host updates, live patching, and in-place upgrade of the runtime and VMM are all options, and a different approach may fit better than any of them. We are looking for an expert to decide and guide: which approach, or combination, gets us there, what it costs in workload impact and operational risk, and how we measure the result.
You will:
* Define the fleet patching strategy: evaluate the candidate approaches (including ones we haven't listed), choose, and make the tradeoffs explicit, grounded in a model of how each one fails.
* Set the metrics that matter, such as guest-visible downtime, total migration time, network amplification, abortability, and time to patch the fleet.
* Design and drive the first implementation, building on Cloud Hypervisor and our Linux microVM runtimes on x86 and arm64.
* Hire and grow the team. Depending on your background and interests this is a technical-lead role or a people-management role, and we will decide that together.
* Work with the SRE, Compute, and security organizations on rollout, safety, and fleet operations.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent related experience.
At least 8+ years of software design and development experience in infrastructure engineering (compute, storage and network virtualization).
Deep, demonstrated experience in one of the following, and working fluency in the other:
* Operating live migration, live patching, or kexec-style host updates across a production fleet, including the failures: non-convergence, aborts and rollback, and fleet-wide rollout safety.
* Building live migration, snapshot/restore, or device-state serialization inside a hypervisor or VMM (for example QEMU/KVM, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker, Xen, or Hyper-V).

Preferred qualifications: Experience with Linux kernel and system programming (KVM, userfaultfd, VFIO, kexec, kernel live patching).

This is an individual contributor role where you'll take ownership of significant components of a mission-critical service, working with growing independence alongside senior engineers and architects to solve increasingly complex and ambiguous problems.
Our team is building an observability platform that supports some of Apple IS&T’s most critical and high-traffic services. We are designing a platform that must remain consistent and performant even as it grows to handle petabytes of data resulting from billions of daily transactions.
As a Software Engineer, you will contribute directly to the design and implementation of core backend services. You'll work alongside senior engineers to understand system architecture, take ownership of well-scoped components, and build the skills to tackle increasingly complex problems across the stack.

12+ years of experience with OOP languages such as Java, Go, etc. with production experience building backend services or infrastructure components.
Solid experience designing and operating components of distributed systems — including replication, fault tolerance, and distributed coordination.
Hands-on experience contributing to systems that handle large-scale or petabyte-scale data workloads.

12+ years of overall experience.

title: Sr. Swift Standard Libraries Engineer
description:
Are you eager to learn, grow, and make an impact? Join the Swift Standard Libraries team and enjoy the rare opportunity to work at the intersection of:
* Computer science theory and engineering
* Programming language and library design
* Apple’s frameworks and the open-source community
* Applications, servers, scripting, AI, and more
The future is being defined right now, and the Swift Standard Libraries team is at the center of it. The work we do will shape the developer experience on Apple's platforms and beyond for decades to come.
The Swift Standard Libraries team is responsible for much of the user-facing experience of the Swift programming language via the Standard Library and Foundation, which reaches from basic types and data structures like Date and String to complex algorithms like sorting and calendrical calculation. The team also develops a growing roster of open-source Swift packages including Algorithms, Argument Parser, Async Algorithms, Atomics, Numerics, Collections, System and Subprocess. You will join a small team of thoughtful, versatile engineers in meeting the challenge of designing correct and expressive high-level APIs with carefully tuned low-level implementations. You'll work mostly in the open as an active contributor to the swift.org open-source project, collaborating with the Swift compiler team, engineers from across every part of Apple, and the Swift open-source community.
Our team strives to build a diverse, inclusive team and healthy, balanced work environment. We believe that every engineer brings unique skills and perspective. Far more than any specific experience or skill, we are looking for engineers who want to enable others to build great software, while learning and developing their skills.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience with Swift, C or Objective-C, or similar experience
Interest in programming language and library design, and engage with the open-source community
The ability to simplify complex ideas and explain them clearly
Preferred qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience.

title: Sr. Trademark Counsel
description:
Imagine what you could do here! At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming great products, services, and customer experiences very quickly! Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish.
Do you love taking on big challenges without precedent? Do you possess a deep knowledge of the legal field and a passion for innovation? As a part of our Legal group, you’ll help uphold Apple’s high ethical and corporate standards, as well as defend our intellectual property. You’ll help provide legal support for all our products and businesses across the globe. Working for a company that invents entire categories and industries means you’ll be challenged to creatively apply your deep legal expertise to rare and often unexplored aspects of the law. Together with your team, you’ll provide the critical support needed worldwide for all Apple products and businesses.
We are looking for an attorney to join Apple’s Trademark Team in the role of Senior Trademark Counsel. The position will have a strong emphasis on trademark disputes and opposition work, in the United States and internationally. The candidate must have significant experience managing complex global trademark disputes and be able to solve complex matters in creative and effective ways. This attorney will share responsibility with Apple’s other trademark attorneys and specialists for the company’s trademark practice.
Minimum qualifications: JD or equivalent and admission to at least one US state bar.
8+ years as a practicing attorney in trademark law with extensive experience managing complex trademark disputes in the US and internationally.
Significant experience with TTAB opposition matters, strong working knowledge of USPTO trademark procedures, and significant experience managing foreign counsel on international trademark disputes and oppositions.
Experience managing a heavy global dispute docket, including experience developing strategies for complex trademark disputes, leading matters from initial assessment through resolution, including initial review of watch notices, preparing demand letters, drafting briefs, collecting evidence to support matters, preparing settlement agreements, and direct engagement with opposing counsel and outside counsel.
Experience developing and executing global trademark portfolio strategies, including clearance, prosecution, enforcement, and brand protection.
Ability to provide clear, practical, strategic advice with the ability to balance legal risks with business priorities.
Preferred qualifications: Self-starter who can learn quickly and has ability to adapt to changing priorities.
Ability to work independently managing a busy working docket and collaborate with a large team.
Detail oriented and able to prioritize and handle multiple tasks.
Works well under pressure in a fast-moving environment.
Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to deliver clear and concise legal advice.
Strong business acumen with the ability to exercise sound commercial and legal judgment simultaneously.
Strong sense of ownership with a willingness to learn.
Experience in technology and consumer electronics industries a plus.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Retail & Marcom Engineering
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization.
IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.
Retail and Marcom Engineering, an IS&T team, builds and operates the systems and experiences that connect Apple's products with its customers. The team owns the technology behind both Apple's online and physical stores and drives the interactive marketing experiences and tools that keep creative operations moving. As a staff-level Software Engineer, you will architect, design, develop, test, document, improve, and maintain code mostly in Java (and other languages as needed). 8+ years proven experience developing software in a professional capacity. Longer experience strongly preferred.
4+ years proven experience with Java, including mastery in concurrency, memory management, and performance optimization techniques.
Mastery in OOP principles, data structures, algorithms, and software design patterns (e.g. GoF), with a proven focus on implementing testable, maintainable, and extensible backend code.
Mastery in Java web (e.g. ServiceTalk, Spring, Dropwizard, Quarkus, Micronaut, etc.) and unit testing frameworks (e.g. JUnit, Mockito, etc.).
Experience implementing authentication and authorization systems, including mastery in identity protocols (e.g. OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, JWT, etc.), single sign-on (SSO) architectures, role-based and attribute-based access control (RBAC/ABAC), and integration with identity providers and directory services.

Experience in API design and implementation, including mastery in RESTful API principles, gRPC, GraphQL, contract-first design (e.g. OpenAPI/Swagger, Protobuf, etc.), API versioning strategies, gateway patterns, rate limiting, and designing APIs for backward compatibility and long-term evolution.

Experience with distributed data orchestration & computing systems (e.g. Airflow, Spark, Flink, etc.), including designing and managing complex data workflows, batch and real-time stream processing pipelines, and ensuring data pipeline reliability and fault tolerance at scale.
Experience with cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, GCP, Azure, etc.), including mastery in IaC, containerization, and orchestration using industry-standard tools (e.g. Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, etc.).
Expert-level knowledge of networking concepts, protocols, and infrastructure (e.g. HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP, CDN, load balancing, edge computing, DNS, Zero Trust architecture, etc.).
Experience using relational (e.g. Oracle, Postgres, MySQL, etc.) and NoSQL (e.g. Cassandra, MongoDB, etc.) databases, including mastery in schema design, query optimization, performance tuning (e.g. execution plan analysis, indexing strategy, and query rewriting), and understanding of database transaction foundations across systems.

title: US Consumer Retail & PC Insights Lead
description:

Support automating and leverage automated intelligence platforms to translate market movements into executive category insights for Sales leadership.

- Monitor market trends and competitive dynamics across retail price bands that create new opportunities and risks for Apple's computing portfolio.
- Through a continuous improvement attitude, identify new analytical methodologies and visualization techniques to turn data into insights and action.
- Communicate effectively within the team and to other colleagues; providing consistent support to Sales leadership.
- Represent decisions and recommendations from analysis to relevant parties within the global virtual research and analytics function.

Proven knowledge of relevant market drivers across the value chain
Experience with multifaceted analytical methodologies and their application through best practices in commercial and consumer environments.
Experience in category management and decision-making process of external customers
Excellent numeracy and data management skills
Deep understanding of consumer trends and their potential impact on the business
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required
Preferred qualifications: Commercial insight experience in complex consumer electronic retailer and commercial markets, ideally with deep familiarity with the computing domain (notebooks, desktops, tablets)
Experience within the US consumer and commercial routes to market preferred
Exceptional decision-making ability to transform complex market data into actionable insights, category plans, and commercial vision
MBA preferred

Understand the customer
Deployment Partners take the deepest, most strategic accounts, leading value validation, designing the technical solution, orchestrating Forward Deployed Engineers, and driving change at the executive level.

Own the deployment plan from scoping to production, coordinating customer stakeholders across business units, IT, procurement, and compliance.

Curiosity and ownership: you keep digging past the first answer, and you follow through on every one of several complex, visible projects at once.

Cox Automotive is currently seeking an Absence Advocate to join our team.  Candidates must reside within the Eastern or Central time zones of the United States .  Atlanta, GA is the preferred location and operates under a hybrid work arrangement.  Candidates located elsewhere within the Eastern or Central time zones will be considered for remote employment.
The Role:
The Absence & Accommodations team provides compliant, consistent, and employee-centered leave, accommodation, and workers' compensation support across Cox Automotive (CAI) and its subsidiaries throughout North America.
The Absence Advocate provides day-to-day expertise in administering and coordinating absence and accommodation cases. This role partners with third-party administrators (TPAs), workers' compensation carriers, HR Business Partners, and business stakeholders to support timely, consistent, and compliant case management.  This role supports the administration of FMLA, ADA, PWFA, Workers' Compensation, DOT/FMCSA administrative leave, military leave, return-to-work activities, and related benefits transitions.
Primary Responsibilities:
Manage and support approximately 100 active leave and accommodation cases concurrently, ensuring timely and accurate case progression in accordance with established service level agreements and deadlines.
Exercise sound judgment within established guidelines to support triage, resolution, and outcome management for absence, accommodation, and workers’ compensation cases, partnering with the Absence & Accommodations Business Partners, HR Business Partners, cross-functional operations, and business stakeholders; serve as the primary employee advocate throughout the case lifecycle.
Support employee populations across the U.S. and Canada, applying jurisdictional/program requirements as applicable.
Partner with TPAs in a shared administration model in which TPAs adjudicate and approve cases.  Monitor activity, document actions, and coordinate next steps across stakeholders.
Identify and escalate complex, risk-sensitive, or employee-impacting cases to the Absence & Accommodations Business Partners while supporting a consistent “moments that matter” employee experience.
Handle escalated cases from the Employee Service Center for specific claims inquiries and activities.
Monitor the FMLA lifecycle within internal systems and serve as a liaison for employees, leaders, and site inquiries, coordinating with TPAs to resolve gaps or delays.
Manage inbound and outbound communications through phone, chat, and email in accordance with established service level expectations.
De-escalate calls and determine appropriate next steps for resolution.
Coordinate ADA accommodation cases using an interactive, well-documented approach; implement approved accommodations in partnership with HR Business Partners, business stakeholders, and cross- functional teams.
Coordinate PWFA accommodations related to pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions; ensure timely outcomes and that leave is not required when another reasonable accommodation is available.
Administer and track administrative leave statuses per Cox and CAI policy, ensuring accurate documentation, communications, and payroll alignment.
Manage DOT/FMCSA unpaid administrative leave workflows and coordinate return-to-duty readiness and documentation with the CAI DOT teams.
Coordinate concurrent leave programs (including FMLA and Workers’ Compensation), ensuring accurate tracking and acting as the point of contact for Workers’ Compensation leadership through claim handoffs and end-to-end lifecycle management.
Coordinate return-to-work (RTW) confirmations, intermittent leave tracking, and transitions to other benefit programs using clear, documented handoffs.
Data Analysis & Reporting
Compile and review claims activity data, identify trends, and provide operational insights that support continuous improvement efforts through operational insights.
Perform reporting activities related to service levels, quality assurance, escalations, and operational performance to drive continuous improvement.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of Absence & Accommodations dashboards and reporting tools supporting U.S. and Canadian populations.
Track and report TPA escalations to leadership to support vendor performance monitoring and visibility.
Support audit readiness and reporting requirements through compliance, accurate record maintenance, and documentation.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in human resources, healthcare administration, business management, or related discipline and 2 years of related experience in absence management, leave administration, or accommodations.  The right candidate could also have a different combination, such as a master’s degree and up to 2 years’ experience; or 6 years’ experience in a related field.
Strong knowledge of both self-funded and fully insured disability benefit programs, ERISA guidelines and intersections with adjacent leave and accommodations regulations.
Demonstrated working knowledge and practical application of core leave and accommodation programs, including but not limited, to: FMLA regulations and lifecycle administration; ADA accommodation fundamentals, the interactive process, and proper documentation; and PWFA accommodation support related to pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
Experience utilizing HRIS, leave management, and case management systems, such as Workday, AbsenceTracker, Service Station, UKG, Kronos, or similar platforms.
Strong working knowledge of state and federal employment laws relevant to leave/accommodations; ability to apply policies consistently and escalate when appropriate.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain complex leave, accommodation, and benefits-related processes clearly, professionally, and empathetically to employees, leaders, and stakeholders.
Ability to work independently with a sense of urgency and prioritization; strong follow-through and time management.
Capable of applying sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential medical and employee information.
Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and communicate data, including case trends, cycle times, and operational reporting.
Ability to travel up to 15% of the time, as needed, for project-based work.
If outside of Atlanta, ability to work successfully 100% remotely other than periodic required travel.
Preferred Qualifications:
PHR/SPHR or SHRM-CP/SCP certification.
Experience supporting Canada leave frameworks or other multi-jurisdiction leave programs.
Experience supporting US territorial leave and disability programs, including Puerto Rico SINOT and similar regulatory requirements.

About the Team
DashMart is a local-fulfillment center owned and operated by DoorDash, offering customers household essentials and other items to their doorsteps with speed, reliability, and quality.
About the Role
In this role, you’ll work within a 5-15k sq ft distribution center, will assist in leading the local warehouse operating team, and in some locations, includes preparing food in a light-prep kitchen, and help the Site Manager ensure we maintain high quality for our customers.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your site, helping your team to navigate new initiatives and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operate: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results in one or more specific focus areas or a specific shift for your site. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success through effective scheduling and by executing inventory management processes and deploying best practices from across the network. You’ll engage cross-functional partners as needed for support.
Strategize: Within the focus area(s) assigned by your Site Manager, you’ll analyze data and make strategic recommendations and execute actions regarding resource allocation, workflow, warehouse organization and when to engage cross-functional partners. You may also lead some process improvement projects.
Delight: We are customer-obsessed. You’ll coach and empower your team to provide a highly quality customer experience with every order. Quality metrics such as order accuracy and fulfillment speed will be key measurements of success for your team. You’ll also work cross-functionally with central teams from our inventory to training teams to ensure your team has the tools and resources they’ll need to deliver.
We’re excited about you because…
You’re a proven leader. You have managed high-performance teams of 5+ employees with successful performance and employee development outcomes.
You relish ownership. You’re excited to have ownership in a new and rapidly growing business. No problem is too big or too small for you, and you’re ready to show up however needed for your team.
You solve problems from first principles.   You’re excited to solve problems in innovative ways, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
You’re unafraid of ambiguity.   Rapid change and learning is exciting to you, and you thrive in ambiguous, startup environments.
You’re analytical . You let data win arguments. You are a data-first problem solver and you have experience using Excel or Google Sheets to analyze data, including using basic formulas and creating pivot tables.
You have 3+ years’ experience : In Operations, Warehouse Logistics, Customer Service, Retail Management, Fulfillment, or related field

title: Kitchen Manager, DashMart
description:
About the Team
We're looking for someone to help scale DoorDash's next billion dollar business, DashMart, by growing our in-house food program, DashMart Kitchens. The DashMart Kitchens team is focused on building a new type of restaurant platform within DashMart, offering a broad selection of prepared foods and well-known restaurant staples to our customers' doorsteps.
About the Role
As the Kitchen Manager for DashMart Kitchens (DMK), you’ll lead the daily operations of a DoorDash-owned kitchen located within a DashMart fulfillment center. You’ll oversee a team of operations associates and shift leads to ensure every meal is prepared safely, efficiently, and to the highest quality standards.
You’ll combine hands-on culinary leadership with operational excellence — managing staffing, scheduling, and kitchen performance while ensuring food safety, order accuracy, and team success. You’ll work closely with your Site Manager to lead multiple food concepts, improve processes, and create a great place to work. This role requires strict adherence to food safety, inventory controls, and safety protocols due to routine access to food, supplies, equipment, and operational systems.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you...
Thrive on iteration and have experience leading teams through changes
Are excited about coaching, managing, and leading teams in fast-paced environments
Enjoy building systems and processes and seeing ideas come to life
Are eager to learn how different parts of a complex operation connect
Are obsessed with preparing consistent, high-quality food for customers
Want to grow in delivery-only kitchen operations
You’ll Make an Impact By...
Leading: You’ll demonstrate compassion and commitment to inclusivity as you lead a team of hourly Kitchen Operations Associates and Shift Leads. You’ll hire, coach and develop high-performing team members, while building a safety-first culture where employees are excited to drive success, personally and for the team. Because this position supervises staff and is responsible for maintaining a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, strong adherence to professional conduct, clear communication, and employee safety standards is required. You’ll serve as a leading change agent for your DMK, helping your team to navigate new food concepts and growth projects. You’ll tackle onsite escalations, including coordination with cross-functional partners.
Operating and Building Systems: With your thumb on the pulse of all outcomes for your team, you will be directly responsible for driving results for your kitchen. To achieve your performance targets, you’ll drive success by building, implementing, and improving systems for effective scheduling, ensuring par levels are met, executing recipes accurately, and deploying best practices.Because this role oversees high-risk kitchen equipment and fast-paced food production, maintaining sound judgment and unimpaired performance is essential to ensure a safe work environment. You’ll engage cross-functional partners within DoorDash as needed for support.
Strategizing: You will analyze performance metrics, identify root causes of issues like prep gaps or order quality, and implement solutions that drive efficiency and adoption. You will refine processes, and partner with your Site Manager and cross-functional teams to execute new initiatives and continuously improve how the kitchen operates.
Delighting: You care deeply about delivering great food and a great customer experience. You will coach your team to maintain recipe accuracy, food safety, and storefront availability, knowing that consistency is key in a multi-concept kitchen. You will collaborate with central teams so your site has the tools, training, and support needed to achieve excellent quality outcomes.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 3+ years of experience in a medium/high-volume fast-casual or full-service restaurant environment.
You have 2+ years of experience leading teams, including hiring, scheduling, coaching, and performance management.
You hold (or are willing to get) a ServeSafe Manager certification and set high standards for food safety and cleanliness.
You’re a hands-on leader who motivates teams of 5+ employees to perform and grow.
You take ownership and thrive in fast-changing, startup-style environments where no task is too big or small.
You’re a creative problem solver who challenges “how it’s always been done” and finds better ways forward.
You’re analytical, data-driven, and comfortable using Excel or Google Sheets to make decisions.
As the leader of the site, you will need to ensure your team and the site is fully supported, which will include regularly scheduled late-night and weekend hours.
You’re comfortable flexing between kitchen and fulfillment operations, and you understand how culinary execution and order flow connect to overall site metrics like accuracy, quality, and efficiency.
You have (or can quickly learn) a working knowledge of inventory management systems (IMS), product flow, and fulfillment best practices within a multi-operation site.

We are leaders - Leadership is not limited to our management team. It’s something everyone at DoorDash embraces and embodies.
We are doers - We believe the only way to predict the future is to build it. Creating solutions that will lead our company and our industry is what we do -- on every project, every day.
We are learners - We’re not afraid to dig in and uncover the truth, even if it’s scary or inconvenient. Everyone here is continually learning on the job, no matter if we’ve been in a role for one year or one minute.
We are customer-obsessed - Our mission is to grow and empower local economies. We are committed to our customers, merchants, and dashers and believe in connecting people with possibility.

description:
About the Team
The Market Optimization team builds decision systems that help DoorDash invest in Dasher supply where it creates the greatest marketplace value. Market Optimizer brings together supply forecasts, causal response models, and constrained optimization to inform spending across acquisition, pay, and incentives. We work with the teams that own these levers to improve delivery speed and reliability while managing cost and supporting a healthy Dasher marketplace.
About the Role
We are looking for a hands-on technical leader to advance the causal models and production systems behind Mobilization. You will help answer where and when to offer incentives, how much to offer, and how long they should run. You will estimate the additional supply these decisions create and translate those estimates into dependable policies with Engineering, Product, Analytics, and Operations.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will
Build and calibrate response curves that estimate how incentive amount, timing, duration, and location affect incremental Dasher hours and marketplace outcomes.
Connect causal estimates and supply forecasts to constrained optimization, balancing delivery outcomes, incentive cost, and uncertainty across markets and time periods.
Design learning experiments and evaluation plans with Analytics. Account for marketplace spillovers, supply shifting between nearby areas or time periods, and interactions with other incentives.
Develop policies that direct spending toward periods when additional supply creates the most marketplace value, accounting for diminishing returns and non-linear delivery outcomes.
Own models through production deployment, calibration, monitoring, and incident diagnosis. Build diagnostics that explain policy changes and surface model or data regressions.
We are excited about you because you have
5+ years of experience developing causal inference or causal ML systems, with a record of using the results to change production decisions.
A record of leading ambiguous projects across team boundaries, making technical tradeoffs explicit, and developing other engineers.
Strong statistical judgment about randomized experiments and observational estimation, including confounding, treatment overlap, uncertainty, and the limits of causal claims.
Experience with treatment effect estimation or dose-response modeling and relevant methods such as doubly robust estimation, double machine learning, or off-policy evaluation. You choose methods based on the decision and available evidence.
Strong software and ML engineering skills. You can build reliable data and training pipelines, write maintainable production code, and diagnose failures across models and services.
Experience connecting models to constrained optimization, pricing, or resource allocation, and assessing how estimation errors affect production decisions.

The Dasher & Logistics team ensures every delivery is completed with speed, accuracy, and a positive experience for consumers, merchants, and Dashers. We own the health of DoorDash’s delivery network, including supply and demand, cost and quality, Dasher pay and incentives, Dasher acquisition and retention, assignment and batching, and real-time operations.
Within Strategy & Operations, Dasher & Logistics is made up of teams that each own part of this system, such as Network Strategy, US Markets, Regulated Markets, Canada, Supply, Pay & Efficiency, and Live Ops. About the Role
We’re hiring a Senior Manager, Strategy & Operations to own a meaningful part of the Dasher & Logistics network end-to-end. Depending on the team, that could be how we invest in Dasher supply, the health of every US market, our most complex regulated markets, or the delivery network for an entire country. title: Senior Manager, Robot Operations
description:
About the Role
As Senior Manager, Robot Operations , you will lead the day-to-day execution of Dot's autonomous delivery operations in the Phoenix area, ensuring safe, reliable, high-quality, and cost-efficient performance. You will own operational outcomes across fleet availability, productivity, service quality, and unit economics while building the processes and frontline capabilities required to scale commercial operations.
This is a hands-on leadership role at the intersection of commercial execution and robotics R&D. Beyond running daily operations, you will partner closely with Engineering and Product teams to translate field observations, operational data, and recurring robot issues into actionable feedback that improves robot performance and reliability. You will establish a culture of ownership, operational discipline, and continuous improvement—ensuring that commercial operations deliver for customers today while accelerating the development of better robots for tomorrow.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Execute Commercial Operations: Own daily operations in Phoenix, ensuring consistent execution across robot deployment, dispatch, delivery completion, fleet readiness, and field support.
Drive Operational Performance: Deliver against key metrics for safety, availability, productivity, delivery quality, reliability, customer experience, and cost per delivery.
Build Operational Discipline: Establish and continuously improve SOPs, daily operating rhythms, performance reviews, escalation mechanisms, and frontline accountability.
Optimize Fleet Performance: Monitor robot health, utilization, downtime, intervention rates, and mission success; identify bottlenecks and drive corrective actions.
Own Cost and Productivity: Optimize staffing, fleet utilization, field support, maintenance, and other operating expenses to improve unit economics without compromising safety or quality.

Improve Robot Reliability: Use operational data and frontline observations to identify recurring failures, reduce human interventions, improve mean time to recovery, and increase successful autonomous mission completion.

Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional partners and drive issues to resolution.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.

Experience launching, scaling, or optimizing commercial delivery or fleet operations.

Experience supporting R&D, field testing, product launches, and engineering validation in live operating environments.

Familiarity with SQL, BI dashboards, and data-driven operational performance management.
Experience improving unit economics through fleet utilization, labor productivity, maintenance optimization, and process standardization.

title: Senior Full Stack & Platform Engineer
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
About Compass
Compass is a new venture incubated within MISUMI Americas. We’re building it with the deep manufacturing expertise of Fictiv, MISUMI’s digital manufacturing platform.
Every physical product starts as a CAD model, and most of what it will cost is decided right there. Yet cost and manufacturability are still checked after the drawings are released, by hand and in spreadsheets, when every change is slow and expensive. The result is redesigns, missed schedules, and money left on the factory floor. Compass fixes that at the source. An engineer uploads an assembly, and Compass reads every part the way an expert manufacturing engineer would. It checks each feature against the processes that could make it, prices the part at the volume that matters, reads tolerances and GD&T straight off the drawing, and ranks exactly what to change. It does this across the entire bill of materials, reruns on every revision, and learns from every correction engineers make.
The problems underneath are genuinely hard: making sense of real-world geometry, modeling cost across machining, casting, molding, sheet metal, and additive, interpreting engineering drawings, and building AI that gets measurably better from expert feedback. The stakes are real, too. Our customers are enterprise engineering teams, including aerospace and defense programs, where the platform has to be as secure and trustworthy as it is smart. Compass is a small team that moves fast and gives engineers real ownership. You won’t inherit a finished system. You’ll help define the architecture, the security foundation, and the product that the most demanding customers in manufacturing will rely on.
About the Role
We’re looking for a cross-functional software engineer who thrives at the intersection of application development and cloud infrastructure. We’re scaling the product, fast-tracking SOC 2 Type I and Type II, and building an ITAR-ready environment for aerospace and defense customers. You’ll be one of the engineers who makes all three happen.
We don’t need a pure DevOps specialist managing servers all day. We need an engineer who treats infrastructure as code, automates our cloud environment to satisfy security audits, and writes clean application code to ship features customers use.
You’ll own our AWS infrastructure and CI/CD pipelines. In your first months, much of your time will go to building our compliance foundation. Over time, the role settles into roughly 30% platform automation and 70% full-stack feature development.
What You’ll Be Doing
Accelerate SOC 2 compliance. Work with leadership to implement, automate, and maintain the AWS security controls SOC 2 requires: encryption at rest and in transit, least-privilege IAM, logging, and vulnerability scanning.
Build our ITAR environment. Help design and run an isolated AWS GovCloud environment for customers with export-controlled data, with access restricted to US persons.
Own the platform. Manage, monitor, and scale our AWS environment using infrastructure as code (Terraform, AWS CDK, or Pulumi), with no manual configuration drift.
Build across the stack. Design, write, and deploy maintainable backend APIs and frontend features for our core product.
Automate everything. Maintain CI/CD pipelines (such as GitHub Actions) with automated testing, dependency scanning, and secure deployments built in.
Keep the architecture lean. Favor managed AWS services so the infrastructure needs minimal babysitting and you can focus on product.
Experience
A hybrid mindset. You’re a product-minded developer who moved toward DevOps because you wanted your code to ship faster, safer, and more securely.
AWS expertise. Deep hands-on experience with managed and serverless AWS services, such as Elastic Beanstalk, Lambda, RDS, SQS, Cognito, IAM, and CloudTrail.
Infrastructure as code. Proven experience managing cloud environments entirely through code (such as Terraform or AWS CDK) rather than the console.
Security and compliance experience. You’ve configured cloud environments to pass frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA. Experience with Vanta, Drata, or Secureframe is a big plus.
Full-stack proficiency. Strong production experience with Node.js and TypeScript, React, and PostgreSQL.
Startup agility. You’ve been an early engineer or on a lean team where you owned your deployments and wore multiple hats.

This multi-dimensional role carries end-to-end financial accountability, down to Contribution Profit, while leading regional capacity procurement, bespoke door-to-door solution design, and go-to-market (GTM) commercial execution.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is seeking a Cell Teardown Technician to support critical lab activities that enhance the robustness and reliability of our iron-air battery products. As part of the Core Technology Hardware Team, you will contribute to failure analysis efforts through battery cell teardowns, failure data collection, and post-teardown sample preparation and processing. This role requires hands-on work in the lab and close collaboration with a cross-functional team to ensure high-quality failure data documentation. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Perform hands-on lab work to disassemble cycled battery cells and support failure analysis using various handheld power tools.

 - Document teardown observations of electrode components and record failure modes to inform battery design and build improvements.

Curiosity and a demonstrated desire to learn and serve customers

Exceptional coach who diagnoses performance gaps and helps people improve through direct feedback and practical training.
Experience leading consultative sales of complex technical or operational solutions, navigating plant-level stakeholders, financial decision-makers, implementation considerations, and extended sales cycles.
Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including pipeline analysis, forecasting, deal economics, and Salesforce or similar CRM tools.
Hands-on, resourceful leader who can build processes, recruit talent, make difficult decisions, and close important deals.
Experience selling hardware or equipment into manufacturing operations is a plus.

description:

About the team:
Formic's Business Systems team builds and manages the software, data infrastructure, and integrations that power our operations.
Our work touches nearly every part of the company. We build internal applications that help teams manage robot deployments and field service, connect operational data across platforms, and develop AI-powered tools that make information more accessible and work more efficient. We also help shape the systems behind our sales, marketing, finance, and other business processes.
Some solutions are custom-built applications. Others involve integrating existing platforms, automating workflows, or rethinking how information moves through the business. We work directly with the people using these systems and own what we deliver, including adoption, reliability, and ongoing improvement.
We're a small team with significant autonomy, tackling technical challenges across a robotics company where the software we build has a direct impact on real-world operations.
About the role:
We're looking for a technically strong, AI-forward builder who can turn complex business problems into working software.
You'll work directly with teams across Formic to identify opportunities and build solutions, whether that's developing an internal application, connecting systems that don't communicate, automating an operational process, or applying AI to make existing tools more useful.
You'll have the autonomy to determine what to build and how to build it, along with responsibility for getting it into production and making sure it works. We want someone who moves quickly, makes sound technical decisions, and cares as much about adoption and reliability as development.
This isn't a traditional product management role or one focused exclusively on AI. It's a hands-on opportunity for someone who loves building software and wants to see the impact of their work.
We care more about what you've built than your job title or career path. You might come from software engineering, applied AI, technical product development, business systems engineering, or a startup where you've worn several hats. What matters is that you know how to turn ideas into working software and can show us what you've shipped.
In this role you will:
Build and maintain internal applications, AI-powered tools, automations, and integrations that solve problems across Formic
Work directly with employees and business leaders to understand existing processes, uncover inefficiencies, and determine what should be built
Design technical solutions, including application architecture, APIs, databases, data pipelines, and integrations with existing platforms
Experiment with LLMs, AI agents, and emerging development tools, applying them where they offer a meaningful advantage
Connect information across business systems to improve data quality, visibility, and decision-making
Take projects from initial discovery through prototyping, development, deployment, and ongoing support
Build with security, reliability, maintainability, and scalability in mind, including appropriate testing and monitoring
Gather feedback, measure adoption and results, and continuously improve the products you deliver
Collaborate with engineering and other technical teams when projects require shared infrastructure or specialized expertise
Help determine the priorities, architecture, and technical direction of our Business Systems function
What makes you a great fit:
A strong track record of personally building and shipping software, internal products, automations, or other technical solutions that people rely on
Solid software development skills, including experience working with APIs, databases, and modern application development tools
Proficiency in at least one modern programming language, such as Python or TypeScript, and experience working with APIs, databases, and SQL
Hands-on experience integrating systems and working with data across multiple platforms
Practical experience using AI in software development or building AI-powered applications, with genuine curiosity about emerging capabilities
The ability to make thoughtful technical decisions without overengineering solutions
Strong product instincts. You can understand what users need, distinguish symptoms from underlying problems, and prioritize work based on impact
Comfort working independently, navigating ambiguity, and owning projects from beginning to end
An appreciation for what happens after launch, including testing, documentation, monitoring, maintenance, and user adoption
The ability to communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical colleagues
A bias toward action, intellectual curiosity, and genuine interest in how businesses operate
Bonus points if you have:
Experience building with LLM APIs, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation, or agentic workflows
Experience building and deploying cloud-based applications
Familiarity with CRM, ERP, finance, or operational systems and the data that connects them
Experience with workflow orchestration, event-driven integrations, or data engineering
Experience building applications that handle sensitive business information
A background in robotics, manufacturing, industrial automation, logistics, or field service operations.
Experience working in a startup or small technical team where you've had substantial ownership.

Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.
We are building a company that is determined to win, and we are clear about how: strong brands, great people, and disciplined execution.
You'll join a team that puts customers first, keeps its commitments, and cuts through complexity to deliver meaningful results.
If you're looking for an opportunity to make an impact and help shape what's next for our iconic brands, we'd love to meet you. Apply now.
Explore life at Fortune Brands here .
We're looking for TWO Associate Creative Directors to join Creative X, the internal creative agency for Moen and House of Rohl at Fortune Brands Innovations, with one position dedicated to each brand. These creative leaders will help define how our brands show up in the world, bringing bold ideas, compelling storytelling, and exceptional creative execution to life. The roles blend creative leadership, conceptual thinking, brand stewardship, and hands-on creative expertise to deliver work that inspires consumers, empowers professional customers, strengthens brand equity, and drives business results across our mass-premium and luxury portfolios.
We're looking for individuals who bring strong creative vision with expertise rooted in art direction, visual storytelling, copywriting, or brand messaging. While each leader may bring different creative strengths, both will be responsible for guiding the overall creative direction across disciplines, ensuring cohesive, impactful work that reflects their brand's distinct identity and positioning.
As an Associate Creative Director, you'll partner closely with Brand, Marketing, and other cross-functional teams to translate business objectives into breakthrough creative ideas. The team operates like a startup inside a large company, so the role combines strategy with hands-on execution and you have to be a player coach. Strategy, Brand & Team
Set a bold growth strategy, plan and budget for Yale and August, with clear OKRs for revenue, share, activation and brand health, and a clear point of view on where the next wave of customers and revenue will come from.
Define a clear, differentiated brand position and set the creative standard for every campaign, launch and channel, holding internal teams and agencies to it.

Build brand partnerships and ecosystem co-marketing with smart home platforms, builders, property managers, insurers and lifestyle brands that open new customer segments and routes to market.
Identify and pilot emerging growth channels and formats (such as social commerce, short-form video, in-store experiences and AI-driven discovery) against clear hypotheses; scale what wins and stop what does not.

Partner with Product Management on the roadmap, portfolio, pricing and category view, representing customer needs, whitespace and competitive differentiation.

Drive discovery and conversion through search (SEO, AEO, GEO), ratings and reviews, enhanced content and accurate product data.

Turn Design's customer journey plans into lifecycle programs that drive measurable device activation and engagement, and turn customers into loyal advocates through onboarding, referral and loyalty programs.

Proven ownership of a marketing budget, including planning, agency buying oversight and optimization of paid media.
Strong product marketing background, with launches in both consumer and B2B or Pro channels.
Track record of building or scaling a consumer brand, growing awareness, consideration and share through creative, original and sometimes unconventional programs, not only performance media.
Experience launching creator, influencer, community or partnership programs that measurably grew a brand; experience at a consumer startup or high-growth consumer brand is a plus.
Experience turning quantitative customer, market and competitive data into positioning, portfolio and launch decisions.
Experience marketing through retail, ecomm and D2C channels, including Amazon, search, ratings and reviews, and enhanced content.
Hands-on experience using AI and agentic tools for marketing analytics, reporting, content and campaign operations, and the drive to scale them across a team.
Track record of managing agency partners to clear scopes and measurable results.
Measurement-driven, with a bias for experimentation: has built marketing KPI frameworks and scorecards, and uses attribution, testing and ROI analysis to make spend and strategy decisions, while leaving room for bold bets that data alone cannot yet justify.
Builder and growth mindset: comfortable in a startup-style team, setting strategy and doing hands-on work, with the curiosity, creativity and bias to test new ideas fast.

description:

title: Data Center Facilities Technician
description:
The Data Center team designs and operates some of the most sophisticated electrical engineering, mechanical engineering and HVAC systems in the world. Facilities Technicians at Google data centers operate, monitor and support physical facilities conditions. Some of these duties will include heating and cooling of air and water, power supply, generators, UPS systems, electrical distribution and control and monitoring systems. You regularly help inspect, maintain and repair various data center systems such as piping and non-critical electrical or mechanical system components). You provide daily assistance to senior technicians as you read blueprints/schematics, conduct tours of systems and assess their working order.
As an advocate for best practices, you develop creative approaches to reducing operational costs while improving overall data center efficiency. You ensure that environmental and safety standards are consistently met, identifying problems and making repairs quickly. In emergency situations or abnormal conditions, you manage data center performance issues and outages to minimize the recovery time from failures.
As a Facilities Technician, you will operate, monitor, and support physical facilities conditions for our data centers.

title: Assembly/Machine Operator - 3rd Shift
description:
Job Description:
Assembly/Manufacturing Operator – Entry Level
3rd Shift - 11:00pm - 7:00am
No manufacturing experience required. On-the-job training provided.
Looking to start a career in manufacturing? We are looking for dependable, safety-focused Manufacturing Operators to join our production team. In this hands-on role, you'll help package finished products, operate packaging equipment, perform quality checks, and work with your team to meet daily production goals.
What You'll Do
Operate and monitor packaging and production equipment
Load bottles, nozzles, packaging materials, and other components into equipment
Package finished products into cartons
Palletize finished products and prepare them for the next step in the process
Perform basic machine setups and operate packaging equipment
Inspect products for packaging, labeling, and other quality issues
Follow work orders and production instructions
Record production quantities, scrap, downtime, and quality information
Use manual pallet jacks and other production equipment
Keep your production line clean, safe, and organized
Follow all safety and quality procedures, including required Lockout/Tagout practices
Support other production lines and team members as needed
What We're Looking For
No previous manufacturing experience is required. We'll provide the training you need to be successful.
High school diploma or GED preferred
Willingness to learn manufacturing and packaging equipment
Basic computer skills or the ability to learn computer-based systems
Ability to perform basic math
Ability to read and follow work instructions, safety procedures, and production requirements
Strong attention to safety and quality
Dependable and comfortable working as part of a team
Physical Requirements
This is an active, hands-on manufacturing position. Employees must be able to:
Stand and walk for extended periods
Bend, stoop, reach, crouch, kneel, squat, and climb as needed
Safely work around and operate manufacturing equipment
Occasionally lift, push, pull, or move up to 65 pounds
Work Environment
You'll work indoors in a manufacturing environment around production equipment and moving machinery. The work environment may include moderate noise, vibration, temperature and humidity changes, and normal manufacturing dirt or debris.
Employees are expected to follow all safety procedures and wear required personal protective equipment.
Why Join Our Team?
This is a great opportunity for someone looking to start or grow a career in manufacturing . You don't need previous manufacturing experience. We're looking for people who are dependable, willing to learn, work safely, and take pride in being part of a team.
Ready to learn something new? Apply today.
