description:
Job Description:
Job Scope
The position is responsible for the purchasing functions of the Danville, KY facility. The buyer ensures the raw materials, outsourcing activities, and purchased material are available when needed for their respective functions. Able to proactively think and act strategically to support cost reduction and continuous improvement strategies.
Minimum Qualifications
Education
Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Purchasing, or Supply Chain or 5-10 years of experience in a purchasing role.
Experience
Minimum five (5) years of experience in purchasing or supply chain in a manufacturing environment; 10+ years of experience in purchasing or supply chain and/or Kanban systems in lieu of degree
Skills and Abilities
Thorough knowledge of supply chain theory and best practices
Understands lean techniques and principles including MRD and Kanban
Strong negotiation skills
Strong computer skills to create and maintain data (i.e. Epicor preferred)
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, with demonstrated expertise in creating and managing complex spreadsheets. Strong ability to write and troubleshoot advanced formulas, including but not limited to VLOOKUP, IF statements, and pivot tables.
Proficient in data analysis skills for creating strategies for decision-making and improving efficiency
Able to independently solve critical problems and think strategically to overcome obstacles
Technical background or experience in purchasing involving stainless steel products, preferred.
Self-directed and able to work independently
Detail oriented
Proficient in verbal and written communication in both individual and group settings
Proficient in computer programs such as Microsoft Office Suite, as well as the ability to learn and adapt to new computer systems
Preferred Qualifications
APICS Certified in Planning and Inventory Management, Certified Supply Chain Professional, Certified in Logistics, Transportation, and Distribution; SCPro Level 1, 2, 3 Certified Supply Chain Procurement Professional; Lean Six Sigma Green Belt; CPIM Certified in Production and Inventory Management; CPSM Certified Professional in Supplier Diversity)

Departmental Responsibilities
Perform complex vendor negotiations and contract set up
Purchase raw materials to ensure they are available when production is ready to produce. This includes the use of POs, monitoring inventory levels, communication with suppliers, and ensuring receipt of materials
Utilize MRD/Kanban systems in the process of planning and inventory management
Strategically reviews the purchasing history, demands, and purchasing strategy for making modifications to the ordering process affecting the inventory KPIs and desired pricing metrics
Assist and work on specialty regulatory projects and supply chain integrity programs including vendor performance ratings
Perform administrative tasks such as investigative inventory discrepancies, invoice verifications, and resolution of receipts
Product Development and Design
Work alongside engineering and quality for new product development purchasing needs
Teamwork and Collaboration
Coordinate data, tasks, and projects with the Warewash Sourcing team and Corporate Strategic Sourcing departments
Communicates and consults with engineering, quality, and operations on design changes and quality improvements
People Management
Monitor and address safety concerns and issues that arise and implement corrective actions, as well as communicate actions to cross functional teams
Supports all safety and processing procedures in collaboration with supervisors, managers, and/or engineers
Participates in and encourages continuous improvement activities and acts as a role model
Provides real-time feedback and course correction for hourly teammates, both in and outside the weld department, when needed, and communicates to the supervisor any feedback or corrections/conversations that occurred
Must be available to oversee hourly teammates when sole salaried teammates in the building
Provides corrective actions when needed and ensures proper documentation for teammate files and human resources
Continuous Improvement
Assist in PLS and 80/20 activities to minimize purchasing activity, determine better purchasing strategies, and identify potential improvements to our supply chain
Participate in workflow studies
Coordinate materials replenishment systems (kanban) and evaluate vendor quality and responsiveness
Utilize toolbox projects to investigate cost reduction strategies
Analyze improvement opportunities in the manufacturing process to determine corrective actions
Investigate advanced methodologies or technologies for continuous improvement strategies and interface with production teams to assure quality of purchased parts

Manufacturing, non-air-conditioned environment or office environment
PPE required: Steel-toe Shoes, Composite Electrical Hazard Safety Shoes, and eye protection. Based on job duties the following PPE could be required: Ear protection, gloves, sleeves, or welding equipment (i.e. face shield, apron).

title: CNC & Production Equipment Maintenance Technician
description:
Job Description:
Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a  Equipment Maintenance Technician reporting to the Production Manager position that will be based at our manufacturing location in Corona, California. Along with this location, the company has their headquarters based in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia) and has manufacturing locations in Hungary, Malaysia, and Korea. The company also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, wastewater, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
Responsible for performing highly diversified duties to troubleshoot and maintain production CNC machines and facility equipment according to safety, predictive and productive maintenance systems and processes to support the achievement of the site’s business goals and objectives.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
*Marginal position functions that are not included among the essential duties and responsibilities in this position description are also requirements of this position.
Perform highly diversified duties to maintain production CNC machines and the plant facility’s equipment.
Provide emergency/unscheduled troubleshooting of production equipment during production and performs scheduled maintenance repairs of production equipment during machine service.
Perform repair mechanic skills including, but not limited to, mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, troubleshooting and repair of production CNC machines, secondary processing equipment and ACS.
Read and interpret equipment manuals and work orders to perform required maintenance and service.
Collaborate with OEM service technicians/outside contractors and ensure safety regulations and protocols are enforced.
Perform regular preventive maintenance on machines, equipment and plant facilities, ranging from simple to complex.
Use a variety of hand and power tools, electric meters and material handling equipment in performing duties.
Detect faulty operations, defective material and report those and any unusual situations to proper supervision.
Conduct routine inspections of facilities to identify and address maintenance issues.
Create work orders on repairs and services providing legible and accurate information for work performed.
Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, including repairs and inspections.
Replaces all safety guards and/or other devices upon completion of all repairs.
Ensure compliance with OSHA safety regulations and protocols in all maintenance activities.
Participate in training sessions to stay updated on new technologies and maintenance techniques including but not limited to LOTO and Electrical Safety.
Keep work areas clean and organized to ensure a safe and efficient working environment.
Wear proper safety equipment while on plant grounds.
Performs other work-related duties as assigned.
Education and Experience
An AA degree in mechanical, electrical, or industrial maintenance a plus;
4+ years of manufacturing experience preferred; strong hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical and industrial skills
Physical Demands

ITW (Illinois Tool Works Inc.) is a Fortune 200 company and is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, automotive components, consumables, and related service business. The GTU innovates, develops, and manufactures through our Customer Back Innovation process best-in-class Power Fastening Systems for the global construction market. Our highly differentiated tools are specified to be used in a variety of applications including wood framing, wood trim, and steel to concrete installations. Tools, and related fasteners, account for a significant portion of total segment revenues
The NPD Senior Mechanical Design Engineer plays a key role in driving mechanical design execution across one or more new product development programs, with responsibility for the design and development of cordless and pneumatic power fastening tools primarily used in wood and concrete applications. This position emphasizes deep hands-on technical contribution and problem-solving skills while progressively taking ownership of project-level decision-making, design direction, and coordination across functions. The role supports the delivery of robust, high-quality, and manufacturable mechanical solutions, while developing leadership capability through increasing responsibility for project leadership and mentoring. Leads project-level mechanical design execution, leveraging strong technical judgment and project planning skills to define scope, coordinate task-level resources, and deliver committed program objectives on time and within established constraints.
Owns concept development and detailed design activities, translating customer and market inputs into viable mechanical concepts, developing and refining designs in 3D CAD, and iterating based on internal and external feedback to achieve performance, cost, and schedule goals.
Performs and drives critical design analyses such as DFMEA, Design of Experiments, Tolerance Stack-ups, and serviceability assessments to proactively identify risks and ensure alignment with product requirements and specifications.
Takes responsibility for the integrated mechanical design of electro-mechanical devices and subsystems used in power fastening systems, ensuring proper layout, interface definition, design integration, validation, and documentation.
Coordinates prototype builds and validation activities, overseeing the production of prototypes and test units and supporting transition to manufacturing while ensuring quality standards, delivery schedules, and cost targets are met.
Identifies, recommends, and implements design improvements, tracking corrective actions to resolve failures, enhance reliability, and prevent recurrence of product or system malfunctions.
Supports manufacturing process selection and supplier engagement, contributing to make/buy decisions and process definition to deliver robust, cost-effective products that meet market needs.
Executes complex assignments with increasing autonomy, demonstrating initiative, sound engineering judgment, and ownership while progressively expanding influence and leadership within the project team.
Partners closely with cross-functional teams including marketing, purchasing, manufacturing, quality, and suppliers to define project scope, assess cost targets, and ensure manufacturing feasibility throughout development.
Qualifications
BS in Mechanical / Mechatronics Engineering or related field (master’s Preferred)
8+ years of relevant product mechanical - design, including 2+ years in product development
Demonstrated experience working within structured, stage‑based product development frameworks,
Proficiency in CAD Design/Modeling Tools (preferred Pro/Engineer CREO-11)
Familiarity with PLM systems (Windchill) and version control.
Strong understanding of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) tools.
Demonstrated design capability, problem solving skills and ability to understand and trouble shoot electro-mechanical equipment.
Demonstrated experience of structured problem‑solving and continuous improvement methodologies, including A3’s Problem Solving, 8D, Fishbone (Ishikawa), cause‑and‑effect diagrams & 5 Why’s.
Experience in Leading design reviews, DFMEA, PFMEA, DVP&R, and root cause analysis sessions.
Strong understanding of modeling and simulation tools capabilities (FEA, CFD)
Advanced understanding of statistical tools such as FRD, DOE, COV, SPC, Pareto Analysis, etc.
Strong understanding of materials, manufacturing processes, and mechanical analysis including, plastic injection, stamping, aluminum, casting, machining, etc.
Experience in cross-functional collaboration to industrialize new products.
Experience with prototyping, testing, and production tooling.
Project management experience is a plus.

Standard office and lab environment.
Occasional travel to suppliers, manufacturing sites, or testing facilities.

title: Service Technician I
description:
Job Description:
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. ITW FEG has the largest service network in this industry to support our global customers, with highly specialized technicians and best-in-class supply chain procedures. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
Service/Repair Technician 1 is entry level in the service technician occupation requiring fundamental knowledge of mechanical and/or electrical aptitude with some troubleshooting experience. Responsible for providing on-site support to Hobart Service customers that includes but is not limited to: installation and/ or service of commercial food equipment. Routine work schedule including on-call, after-hours, holiday, and weekend on-site repair support.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
These are the most significant job duties performed. The size, scope and complexity of assigned duties and responsibilities are dependent on the level and experience of the incumbent. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each assigned essential duty satisfactorily. Other responsibilities or special projects not specifically listed below may also be assigned.
Installs basic mechanical commercial food equipment and assists in more advanced installs as needed.
Maintain, diagnose, and repair basic mechanical commercial food equipment for customers on contract and/or on time and material (i.e., T&M) basis.
Completes and documents preventative maintenance on basic mechanical commercial food equipment.
Implements and supports standard operating procedures outlined in Hobart Service safety manuals and programs.
Supports branch and organization financial objectives by providing a quality customer experience.
Maintains current organization, industry, and equipment knowledge.
Responsible for assigned company assets including vehicle, tools, and inventory.
Follows the company's safe driving and other applicable policies.
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Required Education and Work Experience
High school diploma or GED and,
0-2 years of electrical/mechanical experience
Desired Education/Experience
Associates Degree or Vocational Certificate is preferred.
Mechanical or electrical experience is preferred.
Experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing commercial cooking and/or refrigeration equipment is preferred.
Job Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
Mechanical Aptitude – demonstrates mechanical aptitude to operate and troubleshoot equipment. Skilled in use of various tools and equipment (e.g. basic hand tools, reading and following service manuals, gauges, meters, etc.)
Customer Service - highly professional demeanor with excellent telephone skills and etiquette. Utilizes various interpersonal styles and communication methods to positively assist and influence customers.
Problem Solving - fundamental role in finding ways to address all types of problems by having a good approach to a problem without being ineffective, favoring or causing painful consequences.
Safety at Work - learns to keep the organization safe from different risks by developing a high sense of alertness that detects danger from afar and stops it before it causes risk, danger or injury to themselves, or others.

To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies.
Technical and Analytical Skills
Ability to read and interpret standard service manuals, mechanical diagrams, sustains understanding of parts stocking and identification methods, practices, and procedures.
Understanding of basic math (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, calculations of percentages, measurement conversions)
Ensure they are following workflow processes (e.g., Inspection accuracy)
Understanding and promoting sales/lead opportunities to assist in creating customer-focused strategies for fostering business relationships (e.g., equipment leads, contract leads, water treatment order leads).
Basic knowledge of / working knowledge of Windows applications and Microsoft Office programs such as Word and Excel.
Quality
Demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness.
Looks for ways to improve and promote quality.
Applies feedback to improve performance.
Monitors own work to ensure quality.
Quantity
Meets productivity standards as set by Customer Facing Metrics (CFMs).
Completes work in timely manner.
Strives to increase productivity.

Is consistently at work and on time.
Ensures work responsibilities are covered when absent.
Arrives at meetings and appointments on time.
Dependability
Follows instructions, responds to management direction.
·       Takes responsibility for own actions.
Teamwork
Balances team and individual responsibilities.
Exhibits objectivity and openness to others' views.
Gives and welcomes feedback.
Contributes to building a positive team spirit.
Puts success of team above own interests.
Able to build morale and group commitments to goals and objectives.
Supports everyone's efforts to succeed.
Recognizes accomplishments of other team members.
Keeps commitments.
Commits to extended hours of work when necessary to reach goals.
Completes tasks on time.
Safety
Ability to read and understand safety guidelines of the business.
Ability to approach job responsibilities with an emphasis on safety, efficiency, and quality.
Performs periodic visual safety inspections of vehicle and equipment, reports vehicle and tool defects and takes them out of service until repairs are made or items replaced.
Demonstrates a comprehensive knowledge of company products and services.
Completes required safety training.
Time Management and Communication Skills
Prioritizes regular workload, special tasks and concurrent projects, allocating time and resources to ensure that work is completed accurately and efficiently within established time frame.
Demonstrated ability to communicate orally with individuals from within and outside the organization.
Demonstrates crisis/conflict resolution skills.
Ability to self-motivate and take direction from senior technicians and management.
Thrives in multi-tasking environment and can adjust priorities quickly.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT
The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this Job, the employee may:
Lift up to 75 lbs with or without assistance
Climb up to 10 ft with an A-frame ladder
Occasional roof access may be necessary through extension ladders or fixed ladders greater than 20 feet
Extensive walking 3-5 miles / day
Extensive driving 5-6 hours/day
Kneel, squat, bend, push/pull
Move in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments including tight and confined spaces
Operate motor vehicles or heavy equipment
Operate machinery and/or power tools
Working Conditions
Office facility and customer facilities (including commercial kitchens of various types of businesses)
Exposure to noise, heat, cold, slippery, wet dirty conditions may occur
Travel requirement up to 50% of time
Hours of Work
Normal business hours with occasional/frequent/extended hours as needed
Flexibility with schedule to meet critical deadlines
Extended hours may include nights and/or weekends
Normal scheduled hours cover early mornings, evenings and/or weekends

The pay rate will depend on the successful candidate’s qualifications and prior experience. The range for this position is below:
26.80 - 36.20 USD Hourly

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide
 Serve as the primary point of contact for international outbound movements from the
United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.
 Manage active Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) requests, monitor shipment
milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.
Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.
Working Conditions
Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

title: Manager System Analyst
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers (Systems Analysts) at Intuitive Surgical play a critical role in developing the safest, highest-quality robotic platforms for minimally invasive surgery through rigorous engineering analysis, innovative problem-solving, and robust technical execution.
Systems Analysts are central to the design, development, integration, and lifecycle support of next-generation products across the da Vinci Surgical System portfolio. They are responsible for developing, optimizing, and validating algorithms that govern robotic manipulator motion, force control, and system safety across surgical robots, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes.
The role requires broad systems-level expertise and close collaboration across multiple engineering disciplines, including mechanical, software, controls, user interface, electrical, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts provide early technical input into product architecture and design decisions, rapidly evaluate and validate new concepts, and proactively address complex challenges in system integration, functional safety, motion and force control, and manufacturing.
Their ownership extends throughout the product development lifecycle, from early feasibility and architecture through design verification, system integration, manufacturing readiness, and commercial release. The ultimate objective is to deliver innovative robotic technologies that meet the highest standards of safety, quality, performance, and reliability for surgeons and patients.
The Manager of a Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering (Systems Analysis) team establishes responsibilities within their team. They are responsible for defining and meeting project milestones. They advise senior management on the technical strategy for product and platform projects. They work closely with other algorithms & controls, software, hardware, manufacturing, and clinical engineering teams to enable cohesion of design inputs, design architecture, specifications, and verification. They are expected to hire, coach, and retain Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineering talent within their group
Essential Job Duties:
Manage and support a team of Robotic Algorithms & Controls Engineers towards successful accomplishment of product implementation with best-in-class solutions and architectures
Hire, retain key talent required for the team to be successful.
Provide in-depth analysis and characterization of electromechanical architectures during the entire design life cycle.
Facilitate mechanical, electrical, and software integration of new prototypes and new products including complete robotic systems, manipulators, instruments, accessories, and endoscopes
Analyze complex electro-mechanical devices for dynamic safety and clinical risk
Implement safety monitoring algorithms based on sound physics and risk analysis
Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic
Adhere to, and contribute to, design control processes, including design review presentations, design documentation, and verification & validation testing activities
Support the definition of manufacturing specifications and the ability to confirm devices meet those specifications
Document and pursue intellectual property
Communicate system architectural choices to the cross functional engineering team
Improve cross functional workflow and interaction through tool building and teaching others
Develop and own the tele-operated motion performance of robotic surgical instruments.
Ensuring motion fidelity will involve:
Working closely with the clinical development team to understand performance requirements;
Working closely with the mechanical design team to optimize the mechanism for motion fidelity;
Using analysis and experimentation to develop a deep understanding of the behavior and limitations of the instrument mechanism;
Modifying and tuning the algorithms to optimize motion fidelity and ensure consistent performance in the clinical environment.
Implement features and algorithms to support new instrument development, including collaboration with the design team to iterate through prototypes, analyze performance, and assess feasibility.
Perform risk analysis and implement safety algorithms. This includes documentation of risks, requirements, and test protocols to support requests for approval by regulatory agencies such as the FDA.
Analyze field data to continuously improve the performance and stability of the surgical instrument.
Collaborate with the manufacturing team to develop automated fixtures for calibrating, testing, and aiding assembly of the instrument. Additionally, determine manufacturing test specifications that will ensure instrument performance.
Lead by having a breadth of technical knowledge that enables a top-level view of the entire project. Using this perspective, you will act as an interface between various technical specialties.  Take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries and use your broad skillset to ensure the success of the project.
Required Skills and Experience
Exceptional embedded C/C++ programming capabilities as well as electromechanical and software integration skills.
Matlab programming capability
Familiarity with design control processes. Prior experience in product development under medical device standards (such as ISO 13485, IEC 60601, and IEC 62304), is a plus.
Demonstrate intuitive understanding of mechanical phenomena with ability to do rigorous mechanical analysis.
Knowledge of classical and modern servo control systems
Knowledge of serial-arm robot kinematics
Hardware, software, and mechanism integration skills
Intuitive understanding of mechanical phenomena with ability to do rigorous analysis.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Ability to work independently and the determination to solve challenging problems
Demonstrate ability to provide technical leadership and help define project tasks and objectives.
Required Education and Training
Minimum Masters in robotics related engineering field, with 6 years of experience in control of mechatronic systems, or Ph.D. with 3 years of experience in control of mechatronic systems.
Minimum 1-3 years of people management experience, or 3-5 years of cross-functional technical leadership in a Robotic Algorithms and Controls Engineers or equivalent role.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Prior knowledge of medical robotic and instrumentation control scheme
Knowledge of Python and basic SQL
Knowledge of statistics and probabilistic reasoning is plus
Knowledge of electrical, software, and mechanical design principles and CAD tools
Experience conducting research with human subjects
Experience launching real-world, commercially successful products

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Senior Epidemiologist, Real-World Evidence Generation will design and execute data-driven analyses
using claims databases and real-world evidence to demonstrate the clinical and economic value of
emerging robotic platforms. This role focuses on rigorous statistical analysis of U.S. commercial and
Medicare claims data, real-world outcomes research, and translating findings into evidence that supports
regulatory submissions, payer discussions, and clinical adoption. The successful candidate will combine
epidemiologic expertise with advanced statistical methods to generate peer-reviewed publications and
evidence dossiers that demonstrate procedure value and patient benefit.
Essential Job Duties
• Real-World Evidence Generation & Claims Data Analysis
• Design and execute comprehensive analyses using U.S. commercial claims databases (e.g.,
MarketScan, Optum), Medicare data, and other population-level observational datasets to
evaluate procedure outcomes, safety, and resource utilization.
• Develop and apply rigorous epidemiologic and statistical methods (descriptive, analytic, causal
inference techniques) to real-world data to characterize patient populations, identify responder
phenotypes, and quantify procedure value.
• Build and document complex research datasets by integrating multi-source claims data (medical,
pharmaceutical, facility claims) with appropriate data governance and quality assurance
protocols.
• Conduct comparative effectiveness research, cost analysis, and health outcomes assessment
using claims-based methodologies.
• Ensure compliance with data use agreements, privacy regulations, and analytical standards in all
database projects.
Statistical Analysis & Methodology
• Perform advanced statistical analyses including logistic regression, survival analysis, propensity
score matching, instrumental variable analysis, and other causal inference methods appropriate
for observational data.
Develop and document standardized analytical code libraries
(SAS, R, SQL) that enable reproducible, transparent research and
support collaboration across teams.
• Apply epidemiologic principles to address confounding, selection
bias, and other threats to validity in observational research.
• Interpret complex statistical findings and communicate results clearly to both technical and non-
technical audiences.
Health Economics Integration
• Support health economic analyses by providing clinical outcome data, cost drivers, and utilization
patterns derived from claims databases.
• Partner with HEOR colleagues to integrate real-world evidence with economic models, ensuring
clinical parameters reflect actual patient populations and healthcare system utilization.
• Quantify resource utilization, cost burden, and clinical benefits for target patient populations
using claims-based metrics.
• Contribute epidemiologic and statistical expertise to develop value propositions grounded in
evidence.
Evidence Translation, Publication Strategy & External Scientific Engagement
• Lead peer-reviewed publication development for real-world evidence studies, ensuring
methodologic rigor and clinical relevance.
• Translate research findings into clear, evidence-based value dossiers and briefing documents for
regulatory, payer, and clinical stakeholders.
• Communicate complex methodologic approaches and findings to diverse audiences through
publications, regulatory submissions, and scientific presentations.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align evidence generation with regulatory pathways
and market access objectives.
• Identify and establish relationships with key opinion leaders and clinical experts relevant to
procedural outcomes and value demonstration.
• Develop publication roadmaps in collaboration with identified KOLs to ensure real-world
evidence reaches target clinical audiences and informs procedural adoption.
• Partner with KOLs on evidence interpretation and manuscript development to strengthen
methodologic rigor, clinical relevance, and impact of findings.
• Lead strategic positioning of real-world evidence findings at key conferences, in high-impact
peer-reviewed journals, and through clinical society engagement to build procedural credibility.
• Support advisory activities and collaborative research initiatives with clinical thought leaders that
align with evidence generation priorities and external validation.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work with Clinical Affairs, Regulatory, and Market Access teams to identify key evidence gaps
and prioritize analyses that support product value demonstration.
• Partner with R&D and Product Management to inform design considerations and clinical
endpoints based on real-world data insights.
• Mentor and support junior analysts and team members in epidemiologic and statistical methods.
• Engage with external stakeholders (KOLs, clinicians, researchers) to validate findings and ensure
clinical relevance.
Required Skills and Experience
4+ years of experience in epidemiologic research, real-world
evidence generation, or outcomes research, with demonstrated
expertise in claims database analysis
• Advanced proficiency in statistical programming languages (R,
SAS, SQL) and experience building and managing large, complex datasets from multiple sources
• Direct experience accessing, analyzing, and interpreting U.S. commercial and Medicare claims
databases (e.g., MarketScan, Optum, Komodo, CMS data)
• Strong knowledge of epidemiologic study designs, causal inference methods, and statistical
approaches for observational data
• Track record of peer-reviewed publications demonstrating methodologic rigor and clinical impact
• Proven ability to work independently on complex analyses while collaborating effectively with
cross-functional teams
• Strong communication skills with ability to translate statistical findings for diverse stakeholder
groups
• Experience working in fast-paced, innovation-driven environments within medical device,
biotech, or health technology sectors
Required Education and Training
Advanced degree in Epidemiology, Public Health, Biostatistics, Statistics, or related quantitative field (PhD,
MSc strongly preferred); MD/DO with substantial epidemiologic or clinical research background may be
considered

Excellent written and communication skills

Robotics experience

title: Senior Robotics Algorithms and Controls Engineer
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The Advanced Product Development (APD) team leverages and advances the cutting-edge of technology to design and develop the surgical robotic systems of the future. Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the da Vinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.
As a Senior Systems Analyst you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This position is the software-oriented track within Systems Analysis, bridging the team’s algorithms and the software infrastructure they run on. You will own the software layer between the application and the real-time control loop, the bring-up of the embedded compute platform, the software side of the FPGA interface, and you will bring enough fluency in control algorithms to connect their signals to the right system modes and safety responses. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.
Essential Job Duties
•       Design, implement, and own the software layer between the application software and the real-time control loop.
•       Bring up the embedded compute platform and real-time execution environment for new prototype systems.
•       Own the software interface to the FPGA, including drivers and data paths between processors and FPGA logic.
•       Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems and lead embedded bring-up of new manipulators, instruments, and controller boards.
•       Implement control and safety algorithms developed with Systems Analysts as deterministic, production-quality embedded software.
•       Design and implement servo control systems with Systems Analysts, applying control theory to mechatronic and tele-robotic platforms.
•       Connect algorithm signals to the appropriate system modes and safety responses in partnership with the Systems Analysts who own the supervisory logic.
•       Root-cause problems that cross the hardware, software, and control boundary.
•       Develop test, continuous integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure for Systems Analysis software; provide tool building for other engineering issues.
•       Document software design, risks, requirements, and test protocols; document and communicate intellectual property.
•       Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.
•       Communicate system performance to the organization and support it as products evolve from design engineering to manufacturing.
•       Act as an interface between Systems Analysis and Software Engineering; take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries.
Required Skills and Experience
•       Strong embedded development skills, including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++, and experience with unit testing, continuous integration, and modern build systems.
•       Experience developing software under real-time constraints, with a solid understanding of determinism, latency, and execution-time analysis.
•       Experience with embedded architectures on multi-processor SoC/FPGA platforms, including bare-metal or RTOS development, device drivers, and inter-processor communication.
•       Hands-on experience bringing up embedded platforms and integrating prototype hardware with software.
•       Working knowledge of control systems and robotics sufficient to read, modify, and reason about control code and its timing.
•       MATLAB and Python programming capabilities for analysis, simulation, and tool building.
•       Comfort with the concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
•       Detail-oriented, with the ability to develop and drive a single solution to completion.
•       Hands-on engineering experience with a proven ability to work well in a team environment.
•       Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.
•       A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives.
Required Education and Training
•       Minimum MS degree in CS, EE, ME, or a similar field with 4–5+ years of industrial experience, or a PhD with 1–3+ years of experience, or a BS with 7+ years of relevant industrial experience.
Working Conditions
•       Position is primarily office/lab-based (Sunnyvale, CA). Requires regular access to prototype and lab environments with standard safety precautions. Up to 10% travel for clinical site visits, partner meetings, or conference participation.
Preferred Skills and Experience
•       Experience designing and implementing servo control systems, or a deeper robotics and controls background.
•       Medical device or safety-critical system product experience (FDA design controls, ISO 13485, ISO 14971).
•       Experience with surgical robotics, haptics, or tele-presence system design.
•       Familiarity with FPGA-based motor control or other embedded real-time architectures.
•       Experience developing products in a highly regulated environment, including through FDA clearance.

Serve as the primary technical interface between plant manufacturing teams and suppliers for quality issues, line disruptions, yield loss, delivery concerns, and capacity constraints.
Lead supplier issue resolution from containment through root cause investigation and corrective/preventive action implementation.
Support manufacturing operations by investigating and resolving supplier-related deviations, variances, nonconformances, and first article issues.

Support uninterrupted production by proactively managing supplier risks and escalating critical issues appropriately.

Work directly with suppliers to improve manufacturing processes, process capability, inspection methods, and process controls.
Drive sustainable corrective actions using structured problem-solving methodologies and data-driven analysis.

Supplier pFMEA
IQ/OQ/PQ and process validations
First Article Inspections and inspection reports
Gage R&R and process capability analysis (Cp/Cpk)

Assess supplier readiness and manufacturing capability to support sustaining production and NPI ramp activities.

Identify and proactively manage supplier-related risks including quality, capacity, continuity, and manufacturing constraints.
Convert recurring supplier issues into structured improvement initiatives to eliminate root causes.
Drive continuous improvement projects focused on quality, operational efficiency, manufacturing consistency, and supply continuity.
Generate and track supplier performance metrics and provide data-driven recommendations to improve supplier health and performance.
Support supplier audits, process reviews, and operational assessments as required.

Partner closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Planning, Procurement, and Engineering teams to support plant objectives.
Communicate supplier risks, issue status, recovery plans, and project updates clearly to cross-functional teams and leadership.
Support New Product Introduction (NPI) activities by evaluating supplier readiness, process capability, validation strategy, and production ramp risk.
Maintain strong supplier relationships to effectively partner between Intuitive Surgical and the supply base.
Provide technical recommendations and supplier performance updates with minimal supervision.

Experience supporting New Product Introduction (NPI) and production scaling preferred

Strong technical problem-solving and root cause investigation skills
Working knowledge of pFMEA, process validation, statistical analysis, SPC, inspection methodologies, and corrective action systems
Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Project
Experience with ERP and document management systems such as SAP and Agile preferred
Experience with Minitab or statistical analysis software preferred
CAD / 3D modeling experience is a plus

Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment
Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally and influence without direct authority

description:

We are a globally trusted producer of delicious foods for 150 years, and we provide high quality, great taste and nutrition for all eating occasions whether at home, in restaurants or on-the-go. The Kraft Heinz Company manufactures and markets food and beverage products in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, Australia and throughout Asia-Pacific. Our products include condiments and sauces, cheese and dairy, meals, meats, refreshment beverages, and other grocery products, as well as infant and nutrition products.
As one of the world’s largest food and beverage companies, we are proud to spark joy around mealtimes with a global portfolio of more than 200 brands. Our iconic brands include Kraft, Oscar Mayer, Heinz, Philadelphia, Lunchables, Velveeta, Planters, Capri Sun, Ore-Ida, Kool-Aid, Jell-O, Cracker Barrel, Classico, and McCafe, among others. No matter the brand, we are united under one vision: To Be the Best Food Company, Growing a Better World. Bringing this vision to life are our 39,000+ teammates around the world, making food people love. Together, we help provide meals to those in need through our global partnership and commitment with Rise Against Hunger. And we also stand committed to sustainability, and the health of our planet and its people. Every day, we are transforming the food industry with bold thinking and unprecedented results. If you share our passion -- and are ready to create the future, build on storied legacy, and participate as a conscientious global citizen -- there’s one thing to do: join us.   Our culture of Ownership, Meritocracy and Collaboration We’re not afraid to think differently. Embrace new ideas. Dream big. We empower our people at every level – from entry intern to senior leader -- to own their work. title: Scientist, R&D – Data Analytics & Operations​
location: Glenview R&D Center, Illinois, United States of America
description:
Job Description
Job Purpose
The R&D Scientist for Data Analytics & Operations uses R&D-owned data and technical knowledge to deliver accurate, actionable analysis that supports business decisions across business areas such as carbon accounting, nutrient profiling and compliance reporting, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). This position keeps that data accurate, consistent, traceable and accessible for use across enterprise systems and digital solutions through stewardship, governance and documentation, and helps prepare it for use in a variety of digital tools and solutions. Working with regular guidance alongside Procurement, Corporate ESG, digital and other partners, the role represents North America R&D in enterprise sustainability and compliance initiatives, serving as a trusted link between R&D subject-matter expertise and cross-functional teams. It suits data professionals with food or CPG experience as well as food or packaging scientists with strong data skills.
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Steward R&D data by investigating data-quality issues, reconciling discrepancies and keeping data accurate, consistent, and reliable across sources.
​Support data governance by applying established standards and maintaining definitions, mappings, taxonomy, metadata, validation checks and traceable documentation, flagging gaps to data owners
​Help prepare, structure and validate R&D data and content for ingestion into enterprise data platforms and downstream applications
​Query, combine and analyze R&D-owned product, ingredient, packaging and nutrition data to identify trends and deliver recurring reporting and analysis, for example carbon accounting, nutrient profiling and compliance reporting such as EPR
​Provide business requirements and validation criteria for automated, self-service and AI-enabled data solutions, and support testing for accuracy and relevance
​Use analytics to assess the impact of ingredient, packaging, specification or process changes across the portfolio by identifying affected products, technical dependencies and information gaps
​Participate in organizational sustainability and compliance initiatives, such as emissions-reduction and packaging programs, on behalf of North America R&D, contributing technical input and gathering information from R&D colleagues
​Collaborate with a wide range of cross-functional teams, support the use of relevant tools, data and guidance, and translate complex information for technical and non-technical partners ​
Manage multiple assignments across topic areas with regular guidance, moving between broad coverage and focused analysis as assignments require, prioritizing deliverables and escalating questions, risks and issues appropriately
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Food Science, Packaging, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Agricultural Science, Nutrition, Data Science or a related field, or equivalent experience
​Minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience, or one (1) year with a Master’s degree, in data analysis, stewardship or reporting in a food, consumer packaged goods (CPG) or other regulated-product setting, or in food science, R&D or technical work with hands-on data analysis (post-graduation internship and co-op experience counts ).
​Proficiency in Excel and structured data analysis; SQL strongly preferred, or equivalent experience with tools such as Python or R.
​Working familiarity with R&D product, ingredient, packaging and nutrition data, and exposure to areas such as carbon accounting, nutrient profiling or regulatory reporting, including EPR.
​Learning agility, with a track record of quickly building expertise in new technical areas.
​Strong attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy, validation and documentation.
​Effective communication, project management and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify discrepancies, interpret findings and explain data findings to non-technical partners.
​Experience with Power BI or Power Platform, or familiarity with AI tools and with information and knowledge management concepts such as data governance, data stewardship, taxonomy and metadata.
​Ability to manage competing priorities and work collaboratively, with curiosity, sound judgment and a self-starter mindset.
​Willingness to travel up to 10%, with additional travel possible depending on location and business needs.
​ ​

We believe the office is a critical driver of innovation, connection, and development, but also realize providing flexibility to our employees is critical. To create a more agile and modern workplace, this position will be able to work virtually for up to two days each week and will be expected to work in-person at the assigned work location at least three days per workweek

title: Production Leader
description:
Job Description:
Shift: Days/Afternoons Rotating Shift; this shift rotates weekly working M-F, Days hours: 7am – 3:30pm; Afternoon hours: 3pm – 11:30pm.
Site: Waco, TX
The Production Leader is a shift-based, front-line operations people leader who efficiently improves Quality, Human Safety, and Product Cost Conversion while Engaging and Developing talent. The Production Leaders are responsible for delivering operational targets and leading teams of, on average, 15 - 20 production associates.  The Production Leader drives safety, quality, continuous improvement, performance management, associate development, team engagement and operating results for their assigned area through shift-based leadership of a line or area that exists within a larger Value Stream organization. This leader will coordinate the short-term activities of the area within established guidelines and standards to produce the highest quality, lowest cost product in the safest and most efficient manner, while also partnering with the other members of the 24-hour Area Leadership Team to deliver area continuous improvement and Mars Supply Excellence (MSE) program implementation. The Production Leader is responsible for building an effective team on his/her shift and in his/her area of responsibility and for managing the training strategy for both the individual associates and the team. This Leader will implement and enforce established policy, as well as area and organizational strategies.
Key responsibilities
Conversion - Manage the efforts of operating teams of a multi- line, area or technology on one shift in the efficient conversion of materials into quality products in a safe, secure and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.
Change Agent - Implement changes in methods, equipment, systems and organization, as needed, to assure that the objectives of the line/area are met, and give input and recommendations for such changes by using a Continuous Improvement mindset
Mars Supply Excellence – Lead or participate in one or more MSE Pillars; Lead and support the implementation of Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs) in area of responsibility; Lead key connection points and own reliability data collection accuracy.
Area Ownership – Collaborate with the rest of the Area Leadership Team (Peer, Continuous Improvement Engineer, Continuous Improvement Specialist, Maintenance Coordinator) to create and execute the reliability strategy for area of responsibility
Coaching – Coach operators to build their functional and leadership capabilities and to drive accountability in safety, Quality and Food Safety, Autonomous Maintenance, and team engagement.
Line Operations - Coordinate materials, staffing and resources to support line operation and changeovers.
Standards Implementation and Adherence – Ensure standards are implemented on shift and in area of responsibility through effective communication, change management, consistent reinforcement, and through coaching, guidance, and accountability measures.
Associate Safety – Ensure safe working conditions as well as safe behaviors and mindsets through the direct implementation of Mars Safety programs and through driving a relentless focus among team of operators
Food Safety and Product Quality – Ensure the ongoing production of safe and defect free products consistent with the principles of Mars.  HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Associate Advocacy - Manage associate relations issues and guide and direct the hiring, training, retraining, development and motivation of Operations associates following self-managed, team working principles with a minimum degree of guidance from the Value Stream Manager.
Engagement - Responsible for facilitating and driving an environment of high associate engagement on the team.
Goal Setting and Measurement - With the general guidance of the Value Stream or Area Manager, and/or the support of the Continuous Improvement Engineer, establish line and individual performance standards and goals, and measure, control, take corrective action and report results as appropriate.

Technology Advancement - Advise when opportunities exist for moving the line/area forward in technological change.
Operations Strategy - Participate in the implementation of improvement strategies that will help the line/area perform more effectively in the near term.
Recruiting and Onboarding – Responsible for partnering with Talent Acquisition to recruit and select associates for operations roles, and responsible to onboard associates effectively
Associate Development – Develop associates by mentoring and supporting their development plans and helping them grow in functional capability and long-term career

Bachelor's degree or above OR
The equivalent experience, defined as greater than 4 years of experience in a technical manufacturing continuous improvement environment, along with a High School Diploma.
Experience and demonstrated capability in leading others.
Previous direct people leadership experience preferred.
Working knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices.
Ability to convey communications clearly and concisely.
Understanding of major functions within the plant and the ability to work directly with all levels and functions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Word, Excel, etc), internet software, e-mail.
Ability to succeed in an ambiguous environment.
Functional knowledge and understanding of HACCP concepts.
Experience in plant sanitation practices and procedures.
Ability to deliver critical performance feedback and hold associates accountable to business objectives.
Champion of safety with OSHA experience or certification preferred
HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.

Work with over 140,000 diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.

Job Description:
The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.  Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that TSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions, enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, TSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.
Job Specifications/Qualifications
This role is an individual contributor.
This role interfaces with customers at store level
This role has a reasonable impact on sales organizations and a reasonable impact on the company.
Education & Professional Qualification:
Bachelor’s Degree
Knowledge/Experience
Minimum Qualifications :
A bachelor’s degree, or HS Diploma and equivalent work experience
Demonstrated proficiency with intermediate technology tools, including mobile devices and basic business applications.
Strong analytical, problem solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship building capabilities.
Ability to lift and carry up to 40lbs
Able to sit, stand and/or drive for long periods of time, as well as frequently bend, kneel and stoop
Ability to walk for a minimum of 6 ½ hours per day
Demonstrate ability to work remotely
Subject to outside weather conditions and changing climates
Must live within territory boundaries
Ability to travel overnight if required
Work scheduled may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs.
Role requires daily travel to multiple customer locations and a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Preferred Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree and significant experience in field sales and territory management
2+ years with at least one year of selling experience
Proven ability to influence customers through professional selling skills and data driven insights.
Experience using technology to analyze performance, manage accounts, and support sales execution.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Power Bi.
Prior Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and/or retail sales experience
Prior selling experience in convenience, grocery or Walmart channels.

Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
Join a purpose driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.

Industry Solutions Delivery (ISD) is a global organization of more than 6,000 strategic sellers, industry experts, engineers, architects, consultants, and delivery professionals. Our team values diverse perspectives and encourages everyone to be their authentic self. Join us to help create innovations that make a global impact.
As a Client Delivery Partner (CDP) – Oil & Gas Industry , you are the executive accountable to Microsoft’s largest customers, many of them Fortune 500 and global enterprises, for the transformation programs we shape and deliver together. You build direct, trusted relationships with C-suite technology leaders, especially the CIO, CTO, and CISO, alongside business executives such as the COO. Working shoulder to shoulder with Microsoft account teams, you co-create the solutions and deals that move these customers forward, then stand behind them as the executive accountable for delivering the promised outcomes.
This is an executive-level deal-shaping and delivery leadership role. It is not a project management role. You partner with your Microsoft account team counterparts, including Account Team Unit (ATU) account executives, Specialist Team Unit (STU) solution and technical specialists, Industry Advisors, and Solution Sales Professionals (SSPs), to originate, shape, scope, and close opportunities. That work spans deal shaping, solution architecture direction, commercial structuring, estimates, statements of work (SOWs), risk and deal reviews, and executive orals.
Once an engagement is sold, your accountability is executive oversight. You lead and coach the program managers and delivery leaders who run each engagement, serve as a part-time executive sponsor and escalation point, and own the executive relationship and governance through steering committees and executive business reviews. You are accountable for outcomes, customer satisfaction, financial health, and expansion, but you are not involved in day-to-day project management, status tracking, or task-level execution. The role typically spans a portfolio of engagements simultaneously.
The job location for this role is Houston, Texas with up to 4 days in-office/with the customer onsite.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Our culture embraces a growth mindset, inspires excellence, and encourages teams and leaders to bring their best each day. Together, we create innovations that impact billions of people around the world, and you can help us deliver on that mission.

Shape and win transformational deals with the account team
Partner with ATU account executives, STU solution and technical specialists, Industry Advisors, and SSPs to originate, shape, and close large, multi-year services opportunities.
Lead deal shaping end to end: frame the customer’s business problem, set solution architecture direction, and define scope, approach, and success measures.
Own the commercial structure of each deal, including estimates, pricing approach, fixed-fee and outcome-based models, and statements of work.

Partner with Microsoft executives to align industry insight, technology strategy, and customer business outcomes.

Lead and coach the program managers and delivery leaders who own day-to-day execution, setting clear expectations for quality, outcomes, and customer experience.
Serve as part-time executive sponsor and escalation point across a portfolio of concurrent engagements, stepping in decisively when issues require attention.
Own executive governance, including steering committees and executive business reviews, keeping customer and Microsoft leadership aligned on progress, value, and risk.
Hold delivery teams accountable for outcomes, customer satisfaction, and financial health, while leaving project management and task-level execution with them.

Accelerate Microsoft Cloud consumption and adoption by ensuring solutions reach production and deliver measurable business value.
