A Microsoft Construction Quality Manager is responsible for governing the quality management system, auditing contractor quality performance, managing NCRs and quality metrics, identifying risks before they impact commissioning or operations, and ensuring data centers are delivered ready to perform—not just ready to complete.
Responsibilities
Core Responsibilities of a Microsoft Construction Quality Manager
1. Drive Construction Quality from Day One
Ensure facilities are built in accordance with design requirements, specifications, and Microsoft quality standards.
Promote a "Right First Time" culture to reduce rework, delays, and operational risks.
2. Audit Contractor Quality Programs
Verify General Contractors are executing their Quality Management System (QMS).
Conduct routine quality audits, inspections, and field observations.
Validate contractor compliance with Division 01 requirements, quality plans, inspection processes, and documentation requirements.
3. Manage NCRs and Quality Issues
Initiate and manage Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs).
Ensure corrective actions are developed, implemented, and verified.
Escalate unresolved quality issues to project leadership.
Trend recurring quality problems and drive systemic corrective actions.
4. Quality Management System Ownership
Establish and maintain project quality plans.
Review and align contractor quality plans before mobilization.
Standardize quality processes across projects and campuses.
5. Inspection & Test Planning Governance
Govern Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs).
Define hold points, quality gates, and documentation requirements.
Ensure Installer Verification Checklists (IVCs) and readiness requirements are met before commissioning milestones.
6. Digital Quality Platform Management
Administer quality tracking systems (Nexus/ACMS).
Monitor issue closure timelines and SLA performance.
Produce dashboards and quality metrics for leadership visibility.
7. Field Quality Assurance
Perform field inspections and observations.
Monitor workmanship trends and installation quality.
Verify contractors are following approved procedures and specifications.
Provide early identification of risks that could impact commissioning, IST, or turnover.
8. Readiness and Turnover Support
Support energization and commissioning readiness reviews.
Ensure documentation, inspections, punch lists, and quality issues are appropriately closed prior to turnover.
Partner with Commissioning Managers and Operations to improve startup outcomes.
9. Continuous Improvement
Analyze trends across campuses and metros.
Capture lessons learned.
Recommend process improvements that improve quality performance and reduce recurrence of defects.
10. Contractor Accountability
Hold GCs accountable for their QA/QC responsibilities.
Monitor closure performance and response times.
Reinforce that workmanship quality remains the responsibility of the contractor. Microsoft Quality provides oversight and assurance.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 5+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years related experience OR equivalent experience.
7+ years experience working on data center projects.
Proficient in data analytics, reporting, and construction management tools such as Power BI, Nexus, Bluebeam, and BIM with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Detail-oriented with strong knowledge of construction specifications, quality standards, and installation compliance requirements.
Experience with continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean, DMAIC, Six Sigma, and change management.
Experience applying structured problem-solving tools such as RCA, FMEA, 8D, and CAPA.
Knowledge of ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems, quality auditing, and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) principles.
Experience developing, implementing, and managing structured quality management systems.
Professional quality certifications preferred, including USACE CQM, OSHA 30, ASQ CQE, CQA, CMQ/OE, Six Sigma Green Belt/Black Belt, ISO 9001 Lead Auditor, or equivalent.
Experience in data center, mission-critical, industrial, semiconductor, pharmaceutical, power, or oil & gas construction environments preferred.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings.

As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.  In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.   Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties
Responsibilities
Datacenter Operations
Reviews Process Change Notifications (PCNs) and develops an understanding of the impact to work execution and awareness to changes within their area of work and/or the work of others. Asks questions when they do not have required information and may provide feedback on changes to processes to experienced technicians and/or direct-line management.
Completes assigned tickets efficiently and in alignment with relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) per task type with guidance from experienced technicians. Seeks guidance from more experienced technicians on challenging or complex tickets.
Receives guidance and supervision to develop an understanding of standard processes and procedures for preparing, installing, performing diagnostics, troubleshooting, replacing, and/or decommissioning IT datacenter technology(ies) and equipment. Develops and acquires a fundamental understanding of the functions of, and interactions between cabling infrastructure, network, server, and storage equipment.
Complies with Data Center business unit policies, procedures, and deadlines with guidance from experienced technicians and/or direct-line management. Escalates issues related to compliance or operational assurance activities to direct-line management.
Datacenter Work Environment Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Contributes to a positive and effective team environment by sharing information with other shifts or technician teams, contributing in regular team meetings, asking questions, and partnering with other shifts of technician teams to complete smooth transition and effective handover of ticketed work. Encourages providing and responding to feedback received on ways to work more effectively or enhance efficiency within their team and adopts best practices shared within-and-across shifts or technician teams.
Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies with guidance from other technicians. May escort third party vendors or IT support on-premises at data centers or network sites. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or established reporting methods.
Participates in daily safety briefings. Completes required Environmental & Health Safety (EHS) training, complies with safety procedures (e.g., equipment use, lifting, electrical hazards, ladder/rolling stair use), completes required Task Hazard Analysis (THAs), and uses appropriate equipment and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for assigned tasks. Adheres to and promotes a culture of safety, taking proactive action to alert others of safety concerns, near-misses, and/or incidents. Participates in regular cadence proactive safety observation reporting processes and systems.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Traveling up to 25% typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday, and occasionally domestically to other sites for overnight stays. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Managing Service Maintains an awareness of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) through reporting dashboards, systems, for personal monthly performance discussions as needed.
Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.
Develops an understanding of cross-functional Data Center processes to support partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
Completes required training aligned to job focus areas and workloads (i.e., Break fix, Deployment, Simple Change, Decommission, IT Critical Environment) in a timely manner per direct-line management assignment(s). Observes more experienced technicians to gain hands-on experience and relevant on-the-job training (OJT). May complete additional or supplemental training to obtain or maintain relevant industry or technical certifications.
Service Delivery Develops an understanding of effective execution order strategy(ies) for assigned tasks with assistance from experienced technicians or direct-line management. Prepares, stages, sets up, and performs basic startups and shutdowns for hardware (e.g., racks, hard drives, switches) according to specific written instructions provided via checklists, guides, standard processes, emails, guidance from other technicians, and/or direction from management. May perform tasks in tandem with other technicians to comply with procedures and safety requirements.
Follows procedures to immediately communicate, report, and escalate data center technical or safety related incidents to direct-line management. May participate in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary.
Directly performs decommissions, simple changes (e.g., memory upgrades, OS rebuilds) and refreshes of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, and server equipment, following standard procedures whilst seeking clarification and guidance from more experienced technicians as needed. Processes data-bearing devices (DBDs) for destruction or confirms any-and-all such devices (e.g. hard-drives, solid-state drives, flash cards, etc.) contained within network, storage, or server equipment has been identified for eradication or destruction with guidance.
Performs basic diagnostics and troubleshooting with guidance from experienced technicians and/or via standard procedures to identify the cause(s) of technical issues and replace faulty components in network, storage, or server equipment with zero-to-minimal customer and/or business disruption. Develops awareness of conditions, circumstances, and scenarios which may reflect significant customer or business impact within the Data Center environment.
Learns about post-execution verification of grounding, staging, labeling, and cabling to align with all safety protocols, deployment standards, and planned Network Design Templates (NDTs). Learns about errors in deployment standards or Network Design Templates (NDTs) and escalates to relevant technicians or specialists to coordinate corrections as needed.
Other Embody our culture  and  values

Required Qualifications: High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent and basic knowledge of computer hardware and components.
Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.

title: Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization
description:
Overview
About Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL)
Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL) is a newly formed organization at the core of Microsoft's Business strategy. MSL brings together the teams that decide how Microsoft prices, packages, and monetizes its commercial products, together with the licensing programs and partner agreements that carry that commercial model to market.
The organization was established as Microsoft enters its next phase of AI-driven transformation, when customer expectations and commercial models are shifting faster than ever. MSL's charter is to modernize the commercial engine beneath that shift: evolving legacy licensing constructs toward cloud- and consumption-based models, growing multi-billion-dollar revenue streams, and keeping Microsoft's programs both compliant and competitive across a complex global regulatory landscape.
Role Overview
The Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization leads the modernization of Microsoft's legacy Volume Licensing (VL) programs: the Microsoft Products & Services Agreement (MPSA), Select and Select Plus, and the Open family of programs (Open License, Open Value, and Open Value Subscription). These programs were designed for a perpetual-license, on-premises world. As customer needs shift to cloud and consumption, this role will shape how they evolve alongside Microsoft’s modern commerce motions.
This role owns the strategy to evolve these programs and guide customers and partners toward CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct, while preserving revenue, protecting customers with legitimate perpetual-licensing needs, and minimizing disruption to partners and channels. The successful candidate will operate with significant independence, lead complex cross-group work as an individual contributor, influencing without direct authority across finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field teams, and bring well-framed, data-driven options to senior leadership.
Responsibilities
Strategic Programs You Will Modernize / Key Responsibilities
This role modernizes a set of long-lived, high-revenue programs that are central to Microsoft's shift toward subscription and cloud-based commerce:
Legacy VL Program Strategy and Roadmap
Own the end-to-end strategy for MPSA, Select / Select Plus, and Open Value / Open Value Subscription. This includes building the diagnostic fact base on legacy program growth dynamics and EA-to-legacy migration patterns, evaluating future-state options and ensuring customers with specialized needs  (public sector, regulated procurement, air-gapped, and long-lifecycle scenarios).
Modern Commerce Motion Transition
Design structured migration paths that move legacy VL customers and partners to CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct while preserving customer relationships and revenue. Drive the business requirements for the modern-commerce capabilities this transition depends on, including perpetual-licensing support, indirect resell, and public sector constructs in MCA-E. Lead the opportunity to evolve transactional license sales in favor of subscription, to which MPSA, Select, and Open are major contributors.
Price Optimization and Revenue Yield
Drive pricing and program strategy across the legacy VL portfolio, using pricing, product, and partner levers together to deliver customer value and support the move to modern commerce. Bring the analytical rigor to scenario-plan and quantify the revenue, customer, and partner impact of every pricing and program action before it ships, across commercial, government, education, and non-profit segments.
Program Integrity, Compliance and Regulatory Risk
Keep legacy programs compliant while they remain in market. Partner with legal, risk, and engineering teams to strengthen program integrity while preserving legitimate customer pathways. Navigate anti-competition, transferability, and data-sovereignty considerations across geographies, applying geo-segmented treatment for international markets where appropriate.

Lead large, cross-group virtual teams without direct authority, spanning finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field organizations, through a dependency-driven, iterative strategy that keeps workstreams aligned and decisions moving.
Represent the work at leadership levels within and external to the company, bringing well-framed options and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Partner with external partners and internal product, engineering, finance, field, CELA, and partner teams to land changes with minimal market disruption.

Bachelor's Degree in Engineering/Computer Science, Economics, Business, or related field AND 6+ years product management, strategy consulting, finance, business/corporate development, or related experience OR equivalent experience.

Substantial experience (typically 5+ years) in commercial licensing, volume licensing programs, pricing, or partner-program strategy, with deep subject-matter expertise in Microsoft's volume licensing and modern commerce models (CSP, MCA-E, Web Direct).
Proven command of pricing and business-model strategy, and the analytical discipline to quantify the impact of pricing and program decisions.
Experience leading large-scale program transitions, including customer, partner, and channel change management.
Familiarity with public sector and regulated procurement requirements, and with the legal and regulatory considerations that shape licensing program changes across geographies.
Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity and influence without authority across finance, commerce, engineering, legal, partner, and sales organizations.
Direct, credible written and verbal communication and the independence to bring well-framed options to senior stakeholders at the company.

title: Principal Partner Ecosystem Strategy Lead
location: United States, Multiple Locations, Multiple Locations
description:
Overview
Microsoft Customer and Partner Solutions-Core (MCAPS) accelerates customer outcomes and business growth. By uniting product, engineering, marketing, sales, customer success, and partners around a common customer mission, we help customers realize value faster and turn innovation into measurable business impact. Through deep technical expertise and differentiated go-to-market execution, we win competitively, capture market share, and scale repeatable growth motions. We differentiate through value creation - delivering world-class, AI-powered customer experiences that accelerate adoption, strengthen loyalty, and create sustainable competitive advantage, driving growth that outpaces the market.
The Strategy & Transformation team identifies emerging opportunities and drives programmatic transformation across MCAPS Core, our customers, partners, and account teams. We design and test new programs, operating models, and customer experiences, then we scale what works to deliver AI-first transformation, customer growth, and measurable commercial impact.
The Principal Partner Ecosystem Strategy Lead is a senior strategy role responsible for identifying and advancing high-impact growth opportunities across Microsoft's partner and ISV ecosystem.
The role operates across complex organizational, commercial, technical, and go-to-market boundaries where the opportunity is often emerging, ownership is distributed, and the path forward is not yet defined.
This leader will independently interpret signals from partners, customers, field teams, business performance, and market dynamics to identify systemic barriers or untapped opportunities that could materially affect partner-led growth. They will determine which opportunities warrant investment, develop the strategic hypothesis and business case, and work across Microsoft organizations to validate the opportunity through analysis, customer and partner evidence, and focused pilots.
For opportunities that prove material, this leader will establish the strategy and intervention, mobilize the right cross-functional teams to test it, define measures of success, and ultimately transition proven motions or mechanisms to the appropriate long-term business owner.
This is not a traditional partner management or program management role. It requires strategic judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to create clarity and momentum across complex problems without relying on formal authority or established playbooks.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Identify and Prioritize Growth Opportunities
Interpret partner, customer, field, market, and business signals to identify systemic barriers and emerging opportunities for partner-led growth.
Connect signals across commercial models, incentives, customer engagement, technical investment, Marketplace, field execution, and partner strategy to identify opportunities that may not be visible within any single organization.
Distinguish between isolated operational friction and systemic constraints that materially affect growth.
Develop clear hypotheses about the business opportunity, affected behavior, potential intervention, and expected impact.
Make disciplined recommendations about which opportunities to advance, which belong with existing business owners, and which should not consume additional investment.
Validate and Incubate Strategic Opportunities
Lead discovery and validation of ambiguous, cross-organizational opportunities before significant investment is made.
Develop the evidence, business case, success measures, and decision criteria required to determine whether an opportunity should advance.
Partner with product management and other business, technical, commercial, and field teams across Microsoft to design focused pilots and experiments.
Establish clear go/no-go criteria and use evidence to refine, scale, redirect, or stop initiatives.
Maintain strategic ownership of the opportunity while drawing on functional experts and execution teams across Microsoft.
Design Scalable Growth Mechanisms
Translate validated opportunities into repeatable growth motions, operating mechanisms, commercial approaches, or changes to existing business processes.
Identify where organizational seams, incentives, ownership models, or existing mechanisms inhibit partner-led growth and determine the highest-leverage intervention.
Define how successful interventions can operate through existing Microsoft organizations rather than creating unnecessary parallel structures.
Develop clear ownership, measurement, governance, and transition models for initiatives that prove successful.
Influence and Mobilize Across Microsoft
Build coalitions across business groups, sales, engineering, commercial, finance, Marketplace, partner, and customer organizations.
Navigate situations in which multiple organizations own portions of a problem but no organization owns the end-to-end opportunity.
Influence senior stakeholders through evidence, strategic clarity, and business impact rather than positional authority.
Establish enough alignment to move from an ambiguous opportunity to a bounded test and ultimately to an organizational decision.
Scale and Transition
Define what must be true before an incubated initiative is ready to scale.
Establish measurable evidence that an intervention changes partner, customer, seller, or business outcomes.
Identify the appropriate long-term business owner and build the mechanisms required for a successful transition.
Ensure successful work becomes embedded into durable business processes rather than remaining dependent on the strategy team.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Engineering or related field AND 8+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience
Additional Preferred Qualifications:
Master's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Engineering or related field AND 12+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Engineering or related field AND 15+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement
OR equivalent experience.
Operates independently with limited direction and can turn an ambiguous signal into a structured strategic investigation.
Demonstrates judgment about what matters, what doesn't, and where to invest organizational energy.
Can move fluidly between strategy, business models, commercial considerations, customer scenarios, technology, and organizational design.
Understands partner and ISV business models and how partners create customer and platform value.
Can engage credibly with product, engineering, sales, finance, commercial, partner, and executive stakeholders.
Knows how to find the real business constraint beneath a collection of symptoms.
Can design a lightweight test or pilot rather than defaulting immediately to a large program.
Is comfortable driving work through people and organizations they do not manage.
Can challenge assumptions while building the coalition necessary to move an idea forward.
Measures success through business impact and behavior change, not activity.
Is willing to recommend not pursuing an initiative when evidence does not support further investment.
Can build something important and then deliberately hand it to someone else to run.

We are seeking Research Interns to make long-horizon Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents both  more capable  and  more secure . Agents increasingly act autonomously over long horizons and have access to tools, files, networks, and credentials. Two problems limit how far they can be trusted: they fail in ways that aggregate benchmark scores hide, and they can be manipulated by adversarial inputs. This Research Internship offers two research directions, with Research Interns focusing on one based on their expertise and interests:
Failure-driven self-improvement:  improve long-horizon agents by diagnosing failure modes in their trajectories and synthesizing targeted post-training data that closes specific capability gaps.
Agent security:  develop technologies that make existing agentic systems more secure, including sandboxing, agent permissions, and defenses against novel agent attacks.

Agent attacks and defenses.  Study prompt injection, malicious tool outputs, memory poisoning, and cross-agent attacks in controlled environments. Prototype defenses in an existing agent framework and evaluate their security effectiveness, impact on task performance, and usability.

title: Senior Security Operations Engineer
description:
Overview
Team overview
Every cloud depends on a small set of foundational services that almost everything else trusts. Together they form the cloud's Trusted Computing Base (TCB): the services where a small gap can have an outsized blast radius across the cloud and the customers who depend on it.
These are Microsoft's crown jewels, and protecting them is urgent: sophisticated attackers target exactly these kinds of services, and AI is making it faster to find and exploit weaknesses. Securing them is always top of mind for senior leadership, it comes first when we prioritize risk reduction, and the controls we prove here set the paved path for production services across the company.
The TCB Core Security Engineering team in IAM Protect, part of Microsoft's CISO organization, leads this work. We take a data-driven, attack-path view of risk, modeling the trust relationships between services to understand blast radius and focus our effort where it reduces the most risk. We are a technically deep security that operates horizontally across Microsoft. Our strategy is simple to state and hard to do: isolate these services from the rest of the cloud, minimize what has to be trusted, and defend what remains with layered controls.
Role overview
We are looking for a Senior Security Operations Engineer who pairs a deep understanding of how cloud services and platforms are actually constructed with the security instincts to see where they can be broken. You will identify new risks to our crown jewel services, model them with our attack-path and risk data, develop the policies and security controls that close them, and partner with leaders and service owners across Microsoft to drive those controls to adoption until the exposure is measurably gone. Every attack path you shut down is one no attacker can use against Microsoft's cloud or its customers.
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
Responsibilities
•    Identify and analyze risk across our most critical cloud services. Look for unintended trust and access paths into them, such as excessive privilege, credential exposure and unnecessary access between services, and turn findings into clear, prioritized risk statements.
•    Model risk with data. Work with service owners and architects to understand how their services are built, represent trust relationships accurately, and use attack-path analysis to quantify blast radius and decide which paths to remove first.
•    Develop security policies and controls that are enforceable by default rather than dependent on reviews, such as isolation boundaries, least privilege and hardening standards, each with a clear scope, safe rollout, exception handling and validation telemetry.
•    Drive risk burn-down to closure. Lead campaigns with service owners and engineering leaders across Microsoft, set targets, track progress with data, unblock teams, manage exceptions with discipline and report measurable risk reduction to senior leadership.
•    Leverage AI to automate workflows, improve efficiency, and streamline your work.
•    Govern and defend the boundary around these services. Define and run the mechanisms that keep the set of critical services small and well isolated, and partner with detection, incident response and eviction teams so we can assume breach and still contain an attacker quickly.
•    Turn incidents and red team findings into durable protection by converting the lessons into risk models, policies and controls, so the same path cannot be used twice.
•    Scale your impact with data and automation: build KQL queries, datasets, dashboards and AI-assisted tooling that make risk discovery, prioritization and campaign tracking faster.
•    Produce crisp technical artifacts, including risk write-ups, control specifications, troubleshooting guides and leadership updates that unblock execution.
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 4+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large-scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, anomaly detection, Security Operations Center (SOC) detection, threat analytics, security incident and event management (SIEM), information technology (IT), or operations incident response OR equivalent experience. Other requirements: ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements is required for this role. These include, but are not limited to, the Microsoft Cloud Background Check: this position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire or transfer and every two years thereafter.
Additional or preferred qualifications
Doctorate in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 3+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection OR Master's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 6+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field AND 8+ years experience in software development lifecycle, large scale computing, threat modeling, cyber security, or anomaly detection
OR equivalent experience.
•    6+ years of experience in cloud security engineering, security architecture, offensive security or incident response in a hyperscale or large enterprise environment.
•    Deep knowledge of how cloud services are constructed: identity and token issuance (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and service-to-service authentication), service principals and managed identities, PKI and certificate lifecycle, secret and key management, role-based access and control-plane authorization, build and release pipelines, and network segmentation.
•    Experience with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft's production environments, including Secure Future Initiative work, or equivalent experience at another cloud provider.
•    Experience modeling attack paths and blast radius with attack graphs or graph analytics (for example, BloodHound-style analysis) and using them to prioritize mitigations.
•    A proven record of designing enforceable security policies or guardrails and driving their adoption across many engineering teams to measurable risk reduction.
•    Fluency in KQL (Azure Data Explorer/Kusto) or similar query languages, plus scripting in Python or PowerShell to analyze large datasets and automate.
•    Working knowledge of attacker tradecraft (MITRE ATT&CK, privilege escalation, lateral movement and persistence) from red team, penetration testing or incident response work.
•    The ability to influence senior engineering leaders and service owners without direct authority, with clear and concise writing.
•    Industry certifications such as CISSP CISA CISM SANS OSCP Security+

We’re looking for people who bring strong B2B marketing expertise, a track record of influencing growth strategy through Data Science, and experience building and developing high-performing teams.

title: Designer, OpenAI.com
description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.
This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

We’re looking for a designer to help shape OpenAI.com. This role is responsible for designing exceptional web experiences that bring our brand, mission, and products to life for a global audience. You’ll work closely with engineering, brand design, and marketing to build and evolve OpenAI.com into a world-class destination.

 - Design pages and user flows that help people explore OpenAI’s research, understand our products, and find what they need on OpenAI.com.

 - Work from early sketches and wireframes through interactive prototypes and high-fidelity designs, refining the work as you learn what’s clear and where people get stuck.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Education team works with K-12 districts, colleges and universities to bring AI into teaching, learning, research, and campus operations. We partner with the people who know those settings best, from faculty and teaching center staff to campus IT teams. Together, we help them choose where AI can be useful, learn how to evaluate its work, and build the expertise to teach others.



About the Role

As OpenAI’s first Enablement Lead dedicated to Education, you’ll shape how we help colleges and universities build that expertise. This is a hands-on, customer-facing individual contributor role. You’ll design the learning programs, teach the first cohorts yourself, and work with campus partners to lead future cohorts independently.



ChatGPT Edu will be central to your work. You might help faculty redesign an assignment around a specific learning objective, guide student developers through an OpenAI API or Codex lab, or help a campus IT team evaluate an AI-assisted workflow. You’ll work with institutional leaders to decide what success looks like and return after the session to see what people are using, adapting, and teaching their peers.



This role blends deep technical fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live trainings, workshops, and adoption interventions for audiences ranging from students, faculty members, staff, academic leaders and other relevant constituents, helping them understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to use them effectively in real-world contexts.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence and value, increasing product adoption, helping customers progress toward production use, and turning lessons from individual engagements into resources and practices that benefit many customers.



In this role, you will:

 - Own the learning plan for an institution from onboarding through broader adoption of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Work, OpenAI APIs, Codex, Daybreak and other platform capabilities.

 - Work with Sales and Applied AI Architects to understand the institution’s goals, then identify who needs to learn what and where hands-on support will help.

 - Design and deliver high-impact training engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability training sessions, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Equip teaching centers, campus IT teams, and faculty or staff champions to teach others. Co-teach a session, give facilitators materials they can adapt, and use their experience leading the next cohort to improve the program.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions and scale them through OAI’s partner network.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years of experience owning an enterprise enablement or adoption initiative from discovery through results, aligning executive sponsors, business users, and technical teams around a measurable customer outcome.

 - Can build, test, and troubleshoot a working example using APIs or developer tools such as Codex. You can walk developers through how it works, explain how to evaluate the results, and help them adapt it to their own use case.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team is developing data center infrastructure to support increasingly demanding AI workloads. The team brings together site development, civil and structural engineering, utilities, construction, commissioning, and operations to move campuses from early evaluation through delivery.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Geotechnical Engineer to help evaluate, plan, and deliver data center campuses. You’ll translate subsurface conditions into practical recommendations for site selection, campus design, construction, and long-term reliability. The work spans early due diligence through design review and field execution, with a focus on identifying ground-related risks early and helping teams make informed decisions.

Key Responsibilities 

 - Develop, update, and maintain geotechnical and geoenvironmental scopes of work, Owner’s Project Requirements (OPRs), technical specifications, and engineering standards for site due diligence and design phases, ensuring consistency across data center and power infrastructure projects while supporting risk mitigation, cost optimization, and accelerated project deliver

 - Plan and review geotechnical investigations, including borings, in-situ testing, laboratory testing, and groundwater monitoring.

 - Evaluate subsurface conditions and develop recommendations for foundations, settlement, seismic design, earthwork, subgrades, pavements, retaining systems, slopes, and groundwater management.

 - Assess geotechnical risks during site selection and due diligence, including variable ground conditions, liquefaction, expansive or compressible soils, karst, settlement, and constructability constraints.

 - Review geotechnical reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, and consultant deliverables for technical quality and consistency with project requirements.

 - Partner with civil, structural, architectural, utilities, and construction teams to integrate geotechnical recommendations into campus plans and building designs.

 - Support permitting and agency coordination by providing clear technical documentation and responding to review comments.

 - Provide construction-phase support, including review of submittals and field conditions, evaluation of differing site conditions, and recommendations for corrective actions.

 - Help establish consistent geotechnical standards, investigation scopes, design criteria, and risk documentation across projects and sites.

 - Communicate ground-related risks, assumptions, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

 - Review construction documents for foundation systems, earthwork, and ground improvement solutions for data center buildings, equipment yards, and power generation plants to ensure compliance with owner requirements, applicable codes, and project-specific geotechnical recommendations.

Qualifications

 - A degree in civil engineering, geological engineering, geotechnical engineering, or a related discipline.

 - Professional experience in geotechnical engineering for large, complex infrastructure, industrial, mission-critical, or campus-scale projects.

 - Strong technical judgment across subsurface investigation, foundation recommendations, earthwork, settlement, groundwater, and seismic considerations.

 - Experience reviewing consultant work and translating findings into actionable design and construction recommendations.

 - Familiarity with geotechnical analysis methods and common engineering tools used for foundation, slope, settlement, and earthwork evaluation.

 - The ability to work effectively with consultants, contractors, designers, and project teams while maintaining clear ownership of technical decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain uncertainty and risk.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience supporting data centers, power generation, advanced manufacturing, or other critical infrastructure.

 - Experience with large campus developments, phased construction, and multiple building or utility packages.

 - Familiarity with local permitting, building-code, and geotechnical design requirements across different jurisdictions.

 - Professional Engineer license, or ability to obtain licensure where required.

 - Experience developing repeatable technical standards or reviewing work across a portfolio of sites.

title: HRBP, Tech
description:
ABOUT THIS TEAM

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We stay close enough to the business to understand how it works and focus our time on the decisions that benefit most from our judgment, context, and influence.

We work with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego.


ABOUT THIS ROLE

As a Senior HR Business Partner supporting Tech, you’ll partner with leaders in engineering, product, and other technical teams as they build and scale their organizations. You’ll get close enough to the work to understand what’s slowing teams down, then help leaders make decisions about structure, talent, and how teams work together as technical priorities evolve.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. You’ll advise senior leaders on complex decisions and work directly with managers to make those decisions stick.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Translate technical priorities into org and talent decisions. Help leaders decide what capabilities to build, how to structure teams, and where ownership needs to sit.

 - Diagnose what’s getting in the way of team performance. Use data and input from the people doing the work to separate structural issues from problems with roles, priorities, or how teams work together.

 - Develop technical leaders. Coach managers through performance, growth, and succession decisions, and help them set clear expectations for both people managers and individual contributors.

 - Lead change as technical priorities shift. Help leaders think through the impact of reorganizations or changes in ownership and communicate decisions clearly to the teams affected.

 - Build People practices that work for technical teams. Partner with fellow HRBPs and People specialists to adapt performance, development, and talent processes without adding unnecessary overhead.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 7–10+ years of HR experience, including at least 5 years as an HR Business Partner in a high-growth or complex environment.

 - Experience partnering with engineering, product, or other technical organizations, and curiosity about how technical teams make decisions and deliver work.

 - A track record of helping technical leaders navigate org design, workforce planning, or talent decisions as teams grow or priorities change.

 - Skill in coaching senior leaders and managers, including the ability to challenge a decision constructively and maintain trust.

 - Sound judgment under pressure and the ability to act on incomplete information while staying open to new evidence.

 - Discretion, fairness, and sound judgment when the stakes are high.

This role is based in our San Francisco or New York office and is not available remotely. We offer relocation support to new employees. Our hybrid model is three days in the office per week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI’s in-house Creative Team is looking for a Motion Design Producer to help shape and scale how our brand comes to life through motion design across every touchpoint — from identity systems and campaigns to product, web, and comms work.

You’ll partner closely with our Brand Identity & Brand Design leadership to manage intake, resourcing, timelines, and creative workflows — ensuring design projects move seamlessly from concept to delivery. You’ll serve as the operational backbone of the design practice, building clarity and momentum across a growing cross-functional team. As Motion Design is a shared function in Creative Design, you will also partner closely with other production functional ecosystems to deliver motion design support.

This is a highly collaborative role that requires both strategic oversight and hands-on execution. You’ll be a key connector across Marketing, Product, Comms, and Web — driving alignment, enabling great design, and creating the systems that keep our creative work consistent, efficient, and impactful.

 - Elevate Systems & Process: Design and implement operational frameworks that enable the design team to scale effectively — from creative reviews and feedback loops to asset tracking and tool optimization.

 - Uphold Craft & Consistency: Partner with the Brand Identity and Brand Design team to ensure design work is cohesive, high-quality, and reflective of OpenAI’s evolving visual identity.

 - Have 8+ years of experience in design production, brand operations, or creative program management within an in-house team or agency environment.

title: Product Designer, Advertiser Experiences
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Ads team is exploring how AI can create more useful connections between people and businesses while helping businesses grow.

We’re particularly interested in making sophisticated advertising capabilities accessible to small and growing businesses. Many of these businesses lack dedicated marketing teams or deep advertising expertise. We’re building AI-native tools that can help them move from an idea to effective creative and a live campaign with greater clarity, confidence, and speed.

Design plays a foundational role in defining this emerging product area. The team works across consumer experiences, advertiser tools, AI-assisted creation, and the systems needed to launch, understand, and improve campaigns.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Designer to shape the next generation of advertising experiences at OpenAI. You’ll design across the advertiser journey—from setup and activation to AI-assisted creative, campaign management, measurement, and iteration.

This is not simply a traditional ads-manager or dashboard-design role. The opportunity combines growth design, technically dense tooling, and new AI-native workflows. You’ll rethink how much expertise should be required to create effective advertising and design experiences that feel approachable to a small-business owner without limiting more sophisticated users.

Craft is central to this role. You’ll be expected to make complex tools feel clear, polished, and coherent while moving quickly, testing ideas, and learning from real-world use.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead end-to-end design for advertiser experiences, from discovery and setup through creation, launch, measurement, and iteration.

 - Establish a high bar for interaction design, visual craft, information architecture, and end-to-end product quality.

 - Design AI-assisted creative workflows that help businesses turn their goals, brand context, and existing assets into effective advertising.

 - Simplify complex campaign tools so they remain powerful for experienced advertisers and approachable to people with little advertising expertise.

 - Identify and remove friction across advertiser acquisition, onboarding, activation, engagement, and retention.

 - Partner closely with product, engineering, research, data science, go-to-market, and design to shape both strategy and execution.

 - Use prototypes, research, experimentation, and quantitative evidence to evaluate ideas and improve outcomes.

 - Define new interaction patterns for collaboration between advertisers and AI systems.

 - Contribute reusable patterns that create coherence across advertiser tooling and related business experiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a portfolio demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, visual craft, and attention to detail.

 - Have designed and shipped sophisticated SaaS, enterprise, platform, or technically dense products.

 - Can make complex tools feel intuitive and visually compelling without hiding the details users need.

 - Bring strong growth instincts and understand how design can improve acquisition, onboarding, activation, conversion, and retention.

 - Can explain the reasoning behind important craft decisions and show how iteration strengthened the final product.

 - Are highly generative, move with urgency, and can turn ambiguous opportunities into clear product direction.

 - Use AI meaningfully in your own design process to explore, prototype, communicate, or build.

 - Balance user needs, business goals, technical constraints, and measurable outcomes with strong design judgment.

About the Team

The Frontier Risks Safety team sets out safety requirements and executes planning for frontier model launches, including biological and cyber risks and government models. We work across research, engineering, and policy to assess risks, define and validate safeguards, and drive safety readiness throughout the model development and deployment process.  We also help shape frontier trusted-access programs, ensuring that access to advanced capabilities is supported by appropriate safeguards, clear requirements, and rigorous evaluation.

 

About the Role

As a Product Manager on the Frontier Risks Safety team, you will own product strategy, requirements, and delivery for initiatives that mitigate frontier AI risks and enable responsible access to advanced capabilities.  

You will partner with researchers, engineers, policy teams, and independent experts to identify the most important problems to solve, translate research and risk assessments into product requirements, and prioritize what to build.  You will guide work from discovery through deployment and iteration, making tradeoffs explicit and measuring whether the resulting safeguards and workflows address the risks they are intended to mitigate.

We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience building and shipping complex technical products, and a commitment to AI safety. You should be comfortable working through uncertainty, engaging deeply with research, and adapting direction as capabilities, evidence, and user needs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

 - Set product strategy and priorities. Develop a shared understanding of frontier risks, deployment needs, and gaps in safeguards. Own the roadmap for mitigations, prioritizing investments based on risk, evidence, technical feasibility, and the value the underlying capabilities enable for users.

 - Drive frontier trusted-access programs. Ensure defenders and scientists have access to the frontier capabilities they need to strengthen security and accelerate scientific discovery.

 - Turn safety needs into product requirements. Work with model teams, safety researchers, engineers, and policy partners to translate threat models, evaluation findings, and user needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.

 - Drive safeguards from concept to deployment. Partner with research and engineering teams to turn promising safety approaches into effective mitigations across models and products.  Resolve product and technical tradeoffs, manage dependencies, and drive delivery of improvements that close material safety gaps.

 - Own risk-area safety readiness. Own risk assessments and safeguard plans for launches in your area.  Define the requirements and evidence needed for readiness reviews with technical partners, surface unresolved risks early, and bring clear recommendations to accountable safety and deployment decision-makers.

 - Use evaluations to guide product decisions. Partner with researchers to prioritize capability evals, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including for autonomous and multi-agent systems.  Assess what the evidence establishes, where uncertainty remains, and how findings should change the roadmap.

 - Align teams and communicate decisions. Build alignment across research, engineering, product, and policy on goals, priorities, and tradeoffs.  Resolve blockers, establish clear ownership, and communicate results, limitations, and remaining risks through decision documents, launch reviews, and contributions to system cards and assessment reports.

 - Have 5+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience owning the direction and delivery of complex technical products.

 - Have defined and shipped products or systems with researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences.

 - Can turn ambiguous risks and user needs into a clear product strategy, prioritized roadmap, actionable requirements, and measurable outcomes.

title: Software Engineer, Agent Identity
description:
About the Team

The Agent Identity team builds the foundational identity infrastructure that enables AI agents to securely act on behalf of users and organizations. We develop the systems that allow agents to establish their identity, demonstrate whose authority they are operating under, and securely access resources across applications and environments.

Our team owns agent identity and delegation, authentication and authorization, credential lifecycle management, revocation, and integrations with external platforms. We also build Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling OpenAI to serve as an identity provider across a growing ecosystem of applications.

As AI agents become increasingly autonomous, our work is foundational to how users, organizations, and developers establish trust in agentic systems.

About the Role

We are looking for experienced software engineers to design and build the identity infrastructure powering the next generation of AI agents across OpenAI’s products, including ChatGPT and Codex.

You will tackle complex, largely unsolved engineering challenges at the intersection of identity, security, distributed systems, and agent infrastructure. You’ll help define how agents authenticate across environments, how users securely delegate authority to agents, and how agents interact with external applications and services.

This is an opportunity to shape foundational technical primitives at OpenAI while helping influence how the broader industry approaches identity in an increasingly agent-driven world.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build foundational agent identity primitives, including agent authentication, delegated authorization, and credential lifecycle management.

 - Develop secure mechanisms that enable agents to act on behalf of users and organizations across internal and external systems.

 - Architect authentication and authorization flows for connectors, third-party applications, and cloud-based agent execution environments.

 - Build and evolve Sign in with ChatGPT, enabling secure identity federation and interoperability across the broader application ecosystem.

 - Design highly scalable, reliable, and secure distributed systems that support credential issuance, rotation, revocation, and access enforcement.

 - Partner closely with engineering, product, security, and external platform teams to solve emerging identity challenges and help shape industry standards.

 - Drive technical direction and own complex initiatives from initial architecture through production deployment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or business-critical backend infrastructure.

 - Have deep technical experience in identity and access management, workload identity, identity providers, authentication, authorization, or credential lifecycle management.

 - Alternatively, have experience building cloud-based AI agents, agent execution environments, browser-based automation, or connector infrastructure, with firsthand exposure to identity and authentication challenges.

 - Have familiarity with identity and authorization protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, or related emerging standards.

 - Bring a security-first mindset and proactively consider trust boundaries, failure modes, and potential abuse when designing systems.

title: Software Engineer, Presence
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Presence is OpenAI’s team building AI agents that organizations can trust to handle real conversations and get things done. Our mission is to turn advances in frontier models into dependable systems that can resolve customer issues, support employees, and improve through experience in production.

Imagine calling about an unexpected charge. An agent needs to understand your situation, verify your identity, find the relevant account information, apply the right policy, and resolve the issue or bring in a person. It needs to do all of this naturally, accurately, and quickly, even when the conversation takes an unexpected turn. Presence brings together the models, execution systems, integrations, and controls that make experiences like this possible across voice, chat and email.

One of our most exciting challenges is what happens after an agent goes live. We're building a system for understanding where agents fail and making them better: investigate a production conversation, reproduce the problem in an evaluation, use Codex to develop a fix, test it against the current agent, and measure the result after deployment. Our ambition is to make more of this improvement process agentic over time, while giving people control over what changes reach users.

Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.

 


WHAT WE WORK ON

 - Realtime voice: Natural conversations with fast responses, interruptions, and reliable audio, even under heavy traffic.

 - Agent systems: Orchestration, reasoning, tool execution, integrations with company systems, and enforcing permissions and policies.

 - Agent quality: Production debugging, simulations, evaluation infrastructure, regression testing, and measuring whether changes improve real outcomes.

 - Product and developer experience: Making it easier for teams to build, test, deploy, and operate sophisticated agents using Codex and OpenAI's capabilities.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

You'll work at the intersection of frontier research, product engineering, and production systems, with a direct feedback loop from people using what you build. We collaborate closely with Research, Forward Deployed Engineers, and customers to understand where models and systems break down and turn those lessons into improvements that can benefit many deployments.

The impact is already tangible. At launch, Presence was resolving 75% of issues coming into OpenAI's English phone support without a human, and its Codex-assisted improvement process helped cut transfers to people by 15 percentage points over ten days. Introducing OpenAI Presence https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/

We're looking for people excited by ambitious engineering problems, building products people depend on, and helping define how AI agents are developed and improved in the real world.

 


YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE:

 - 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.

 - A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.

 - Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.

 - End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.

 - Strong product judgment that connects technical decisions to user needs, with the ability to balance delivery speed, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability.

Drive Cost Integrity: Lead the quarterly contract manufacturer (CM) quote review process and validate standard cost updates in the Everpure™ Platform, ensuring every component in our Bill of Materials (BOM) is accurately reflected.

Systems & Analytical Proficiency: Advanced capability in ERP systems (such as SAP or NetSuite) and data analysis tools to synthesize high volumes of supply chain data into clear financial insights.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: A proven ability to communicate complex financial concepts to non-finance partners, influencing outcomes across Operations, FP&A, and external vendors without direct authority.

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. Strong understanding of wheel and tire engineering, chassis integration, materials, manufacturing processes (including casting and forging), vehicle dynamics, and wheel/tire performance. Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.
Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.

Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.
Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.

4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.
Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.
Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.
Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.
Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.

Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.

About the role:
Samsara's Go-To-Market AI product team builds the internal products our sellers, customer success managers, and support reps use every day. As Director, AI Product Management (GTM), you will own an AI-powered GTM platform that creates a step change in impact, brings in new ways of working, centralizes data and insights, and acts as the foundational system for our GTM organization—from problem identification to development, adoption, and measurable business impact.
Functioning much like a general manager with product at the core, this broad leadership role requires you to build, coach, and grow a high-performing team of product managers while driving enablement, cross-functional alignment, and strategic execution.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.
In this role, you will:
Own the strategy, roadmap, and business outcomes for our internal AI-native GTM platform, and be accountable for whether the business adopts it.
Manage the platform as one portfolio, so every part of it shares the same data, intelligence and building blocks, and users get one consistent experience.
Build an AI-native product practice. Take the best of traditional product management, such as PRDs, prioritization, launch readiness and measurement, and reinvent it with AI so the team moves faster and builds better.
Understand internal users' problems and analyze data to identify what to build, sometimes finding the need before users can articulate it.
Write clear requirements and partner closely with engineering, which leads technical implementation, to deliver a high-quality product. Make sure you and your team test the product firsthand.
Keep pace with an engineering team that moves fast and ships at high velocity. Gather input from the field quickly, turn it into a clear direction for engineering, and use AI to shorten the loop from feedback to shipped improvement.
Define what quality means for AI products, including accuracy, trust, evaluation and human review, and hold every release to that bar.
Drive adoption by coaching sellers and partnering with Sales Enablement and Product Marketing, and measure the business impact of what you ship.
Set clear, measurable goals for adoption, productivity and business impact, instrument the product to track them, and use the results to decide what to build next.
Resolve cross-functional dependencies, such as aligning teams on shared datasets with Data Engineering or getting Product Marketing content into the AI knowledge base, and take on the analytics and operational work needed to make the product succeed.
Use AI tools in your own work to build prototypes and mini-apps that engineers can take forward into production, and apply AI to improve how Samsara's go-to-market teams work. Hands-on AI experience is a requirement for this role.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team of product managers.
Minimum requirements for the role:
10+ years of experience in product management, or in strategy and operations roles where you owned a product built with engineering.
5+ years of experience leading, developing and mentoring product managers or product-oriented teams, while staying close to execution.
Demonstrated ownership of an internal or business-facing product, including defining the problem, working with engineering to deliver it, driving adoption and showing measurable business impact.
Hands-on experience with AI, such as building or shipping AI-enabled products, using AI tools in your own work, or prototyping with them.
Strong analytical skills, with examples of using data to identify problems, shape product decisions and measure results.
Technical fluency and ability to establish credibility with engineers.
Strong problem-solving and structured thinking, with a record of driving work to completion across teams and stakeholders.
An ideal candidate also has:
Experience owning internal tools or AI products used by sales, customer success or other go-to-market teams.
Familiarity with the systems and data that run a go-to-market organization, such as CRM, forecasting and sales enablement tools.
Experience defining quality, evaluation and trust standards for AI products.
Experience coaching end users and working with enablement teams to get a new tool used.
Experience leading product teams that use AI throughout their own work, from research and requirements to prototyping and launch.
Comfort with fast-changing priorities and with the cross-functional alignment that a company at Samsara's scale requires.

title: Manufacturing Quality Inspector
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Robots only work if every part is exactly what it claims to be — and you're the one who makes sure of it. You'll be the final word on mechanical quality in our QC lab, using GD&T to catch what others miss and confirming that the parts going into our robots match the drawings they came from. Get it right, and every arm we ship starts on solid ground.


What you'll do

- Inspect mechanical parts and assemblies in the QC lab using GD&T (ASME Y14.5), catching deviations before they turn into downstream problems.

- Program and run CMMs and other advanced measurement equipment to verify parts against spec.

- Lead First Article Inspections for mechanical parts at launch and after any process change.

- Run process audits on production mechanical operations so quality holds steady as we scale.

- Mentor Receiving Inspectors on mechanical inspection techniques and GD&T fundamentals.

- Keep inspection records and traceability tight and audit-ready for all mechanical work.

- Take a seat on the Material Review Board and help resolve mechanical nonconformances.

- Review mechanical drawings for inspectability, and flag GD&T issues to NPI and Engineering before they cause rework.

- Support our 6S and FOD programs to keep the QC lab clean, organized, and safe.


What you'll bring

- 5+ years of mechanical inspection experience in a QC lab environment.

- Strong working knowledge of GD&T per ASME Y14.5.

- Hands-on skill with measurement equipment — CMM preferred, plus height gauges, optical comparators, and surface plates.

- Sharp drawing interpretation skills.

- The patience and precision to work through complex measurements without cutting corners.


Nice to have

- CMM programming experience with PC-DMIS, Calypso, or similar software.

- Experience inspecting industrial robotics or precision mechanical assemblies.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $34-40/hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

The Platform Velocity Sales team works with B2B Software Platforms to help them facilitate payments for their customers using our Stripe Connect product. If you’re motivated, smart, persistent, and a great teammate, we want to hear from you!

Contribute to the development of our platform partnership strategy by establishing repeatable processes and scalable engagement models.
