Our platform serves billions of daily requests across 100+ large language models, handling model selection, provider failover, load balancing, and cost optimization through a single unified API. Thousands of developers and enterprises depend on it to operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads.
The security surface spans API key and provider credential management across cloud boundaries, user prompt data flowing through the routing layer, a billing pipeline processing billions of daily events with financial-grade accuracy requirements, and an authentication layer federating external identity providers. You will lead and scale the security team that owns this surface — hands-on in the architecture and code, setting the technical direction, and directly elevating the security posture of the platform through your own work.
What you'll do
This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You manage a fast growing team of software and security engineers and make outsized impact through technical depth. Your focus will be cloud security infrastructure and modern AI development practices.  This is a player/coach role: you’ll establish the roadmap and grow the team while continuing to design systems, write code, evaluate tools, and work through difficult technical problems.
Own the security architecture. Threat-model the edge compute layer, provider integration surface, credential management system, billing pipeline, and analytics store. Make the architecture decisions — API key lifecycle, secrets rotation, data classification, auth enforcement — and partner with product and infra teams through implementation.
Secure the credential layer. Design and implement controls for API key issuance, rotation, revocation, and abuse detection across user-facing keys and upstream provider credentials spanning multiple secrets engines and cloud boundaries. This is the highest-risk surface on the platform and requires deep expertise in cryptographic credential management, OAuth/OIDC federation, and token-based access control.
Build detection and response. Instrument the platform for security events across edge, async processing, and database tiers. Build alerting, runbooks, and forensic tooling. Lead incident response when it matters. You own time-to-detect and time-to-contain, not just the playbook.
Integrate the platform into Stripe's security programs. Bring the platform into SecRev, vulnerability management, and incident response processes. Adapt controls designed for Stripe's primary infrastructure to fit an edge-first, multi-cloud architecture. Bridge Stripe's compliance frameworks (SOC 2, PCI DSS) with a platform that routes data across external providers.
Lead and develop the team. Manage existing team members and help rapidly scale it, in line with business and technical needs. Set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and develop people.
Who you are
You’re an engineer and a people leader who is comfortable representing the security posture to executive leadership . You enjoy building things yourself, but you also know how to create an environment where other strong engineers can do their best work. You’re resourceful, comfortable with ambiguity, and willing to start with a practical solution and improve it as you learn
Minimum requirements
Software & security engineering depth. 10+ years in software engineering with deep expertise in at least two of: API security architecture, credential and secrets management, cloud security (IAM, network segmentation, encryption), or application security for high-throughput distributed systems.
Hands-on technical leader. Strong software engineering skills and the ability to contribute directly to production code, infrastructure, and technical design. You have directly designed credential management systems, authentication architectures, or data protection controls for production systems at scale, not just reviewed others' work.
Multi-cloud and edge security. Experience securing workloads that span multiple cloud providers or edge compute platforms: secrets management across trust boundaries, data classification for data in transit, and compliance in environments where you do not control the full stack.
Team leadership. Experience managing and growing a team of engineers, setting high expectations, and developing people. You have led teams where the quality of the work depended on your technical judgment, not just your organizational skills.
Communication. You explain security risks, architecture decisions, and compliance tradeoffs clearly to engineering, product, and executive audiences.
Thrives with ambiguity. A resourceful, pragmatic approach to execution: you can prioritize under constraints, make clear build-versus-buy decisions, and deliver useful improvements without waiting for perfect information.
Preferred qualifications
The ability to secure high-throughput proxy, API gateway, or edge compute systems
Experience designing, operating, or security infrastructure on Google Cloud
Deep knowledge of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and federated identity architectures
Familiarity with LLM inference infrastructure, token-based billing, or AI/ML platform security
Experience with laptop, device and endpoint security, including device management and secure access.
Background in payments, fintech, or regulated industries (SOC 2, PCI DSS, GDPR) with strict data-handling standards
Experience integrating a newly acquired platform into an existing security organization and compliance framework

title: Lead Instrumentation and Controls Engineer
location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:
Job Family Group:
Engineering Group
Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, and inclusion are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
We are seeking an experienced instrumentation, and controls engineer to provide instrumentation, electrical, automation, and controls engineering support for the Straddle, Instrument Air and PAGL Campaigns, as well as other Facilities Engineering projects. This role will develop safe, reliable, standardized, and execution-ready designs, including complete engineering drawings and construction work packages that field teams can safely and efficiently build against. The ideal candidate will have strong technical expertise in RTUs, HMIs, PLCs, SCADA systems, and industrial electrical/instrumentation design.
We thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where energy, agility, and collaboration are key. Our team operates at a high volume and high velocity, engaging with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders daily. Success here means being proactive, adaptable, and relentlessly focused on delivering results—often under tight timelines and shifting priorities. If you’re energized by complexity, motivated by impact, and thrive in a culture that values communication and ownership, you’ll feel right at home.
Key Accountabilities
Standard Design & Technical Ownership
Manage standard automation design through engineering, procurement, construction, programming, testing, commissioning, and closeout.
Maintain standard ABB TotalFlow RTU, Red Lion HMI, and Allen-Bradley PLC programming templates and coordinate integration with CygNet SCADA.
Maintain instrumentation and controls standards, specifications, preferred equipment, typical drawings, and reusable design packages.
Evaluate alternative equipment and design approaches, including technical, operational, schedule, cost, maintainability, and standardization impacts.
Capture field learning, failures, RFIs, commissioning issues, and lessons learned to continuously improve standards and future project designs.
Existing Facility Assessment & Scope Definition
Work with the Automation team to document the instrumentation, controls, electrical, PLC/RTU, HMI, SCADA, communications, control-panel, and measurement systems installed at each facility.
Lead site walkdowns and design surveys with Automation, Operations, Facilities Engineering, Maintenance, and Construction to verify existing conditions, tie-in points, power availability, communications, equipment condition, access, and constructability.
Compare the existing facility configuration with the requirements of the Straddle Program, PAGL Campaign, Instrument Air Program, or other assigned Facilities Engineering scope.
Define the instrumentation, electrical, controls, automation, communications, metering, and programming additions, removals, relocations, and upgrades required for the project.
Document scope boundaries, existing-system assumptions, technical risks, long-lead items, outages, utility requirements, and interfaces with existing facility systems.
Engineering Drawings & Design Deliverables
Develop and review site-specific electrical, instrumentation, automation, and controls drawings that field teams can safely and efficiently build against.
Prepare and maintain P&IDs, I/O lists, instrument indexes, instrument datasheets, electrical one-lines, wiring diagrams, loop drawings, control-panel drawings, junction-box drawings, cable schedules, grounding details, installation details, and bills of material.
Develop Cause & Effect (C&E) diagrams, control narratives, alarm and shutdown requirements, permissives, interlocks, sequencing, and Allocation Flow Diagrams.
Translate P&IDs and PFDs into I/O requirements, control logic, Cause & Effect requirements, metering needs, and field installation details.
Review P&IDs, PFDs, C&E’s, equipment layouts, 3D models, vendor drawings, and equipment RFPs for separators, compressors, heaters, Instrument Air skids, metering packages, control panels, VFDs, and related facility equipment.
Ensure drawings clearly identify equipment locations, dimensions, tie-ins, cable and conduit routing, power sources, communications, installation requirements, testing requirements, demolition scope, and existing-versus-new work.
Instrumentation, Electrical & Procurement Support
Specify and support the purchase of instrumentation, metering equipment, control valves, control panels, RTUs, PLCs, HMIs, radios, VFDs, electrical equipment, and associated accessories.
Coordinate purchasing and supply-chain activities, including requisition development, technical bid evaluation, ordering, vendor data review, delivery scheduling, expediting, and cost tracking.
Coordinate with local electric utilities for new or modified electrical service, metering, load requirements, schedules, and energization.
Automation, Programming & SCADA Integration
Coordinate ABB TotalFlow PCCU configuration, Red Lion Crimson HMI development, and Allen-Bradley RSLogix 5000 / Studio 5000 PLC programming for assigned projects.
Coordinate CygNet SCADA tag creation, data mapping, alarm configuration, historian requirements, communications, radio configuration, and data verification.
Collaborate with Field Automation Technicians to configure sites, verify communications, complete point-to-point checks, and resolve field integration issues.
Apply industrial communications protocols, including Ethernet/IP, Modbus, and RS-485, and coordinate interfaces with corporate and industrial network architecture.
